jobs.title: Senior Cybersecurity and GRC Analyst
jobs.excerpt: Conjointly is an all-in-one survey research platform, with easy-to-use advanced tools, real human respondents in your target audience, and expert researchers on hand, covering everything from simple surveys to advanced conjoint, product, and pricing research, as well as conversational and video surveys.
jobs.description:
Conjointly is an all-in-one survey research platform, with easy-to-use advanced tools, real human respondents in your target audience, and expert researchers on hand, covering everything from simple surveys to advanced conjoint, product, and pricing research, as well as conversational and video surveys.

We are looking for a Senior Cybersecurity and GRC Analyst to keep Conjointly secure. You will monitor and protect our systems, find vulnerabilities, and make sure risks are closed rather than just recorded. Around 70 to 80% of the role is hands-on cybersecurity; the rest supports our governance, risk and compliance (GRC) work for SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27701.

Responsibilities:

Cybersecurity

  • Planning & Coordination: Plan and coordinate cybersecurity activities across the business, and keep security policies and procedures in line with best practice.
  • Security Monitoring: Monitor and triage security alerts across our environments, logging and monitoring tools, and endpoints, and help strengthen our monitoring, including centralised log monitoring.
  • Threat Investigation: Investigate suspicious activity such as phishing, unusual logins and malware, and track emerging threats that could affect us.
  • Vulnerability Management: Run vulnerability scans, validate and triage findings and bug bounty reports, and work with developers on fixes.
  • Access Oversight: Oversee and review user access managed by other teams, including privileged accounts and timely removal of leavers’ access.
  • Risk Assessment: Identify and assess cybersecurity risks, and follow up with owners until every issue is closed.
  • Security Controls: Recommend, tune and monitor security controls to prevent and detect breaches.
  • Incident Response: Investigate, document and coordinate the response to security incidents, and contribute to post-incident reviews.
  • Security Awareness: Run security awareness training and phishing simulations for all staff.
  • Reporting: Maintain incident logs and risk reports, and present cybersecurity updates at the annual management meeting.

Governance, risk and compliance (GRC)

  • Security Questionnaires: Complete supplier and customer security questionnaires and compliance requests.
  • Penetration Testing: Arrange penetration tests and liaise with testers.
  • Audit Support: Supply technical evidence for SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27701 audits, and help keep security documentation audit-ready.
  • Risk Management Meetings: Run the risk management meeting and keep the risk register up to date.

Requirements

  • Degree in Computer Science, IT, Cybersecurity or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • At least one cybersecurity certification is required, such as CISSP, CompTIA CySA+, GIAC (GCIH or GSEC) or a cloud security certification.
  • 5+ years of hands-on cybersecurity experience, including security operations, vulnerability management and incident response; experience in a larger or regulated organisation is preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of cloud, network, endpoint, identity and application security.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS security services, log monitoring, endpoint management and protection, and vulnerability scanning tools; SIEM and EDR experience is highly regarded.
  • Familiarity with SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27701, including audit evidence and security questionnaires.
  • Independent, cautious and thorough, with the persistence to follow up with colleagues at all levels until work is done.
  • Able to explain risk clearly to non-technical staff and present to management.

Benefits

  • Opportunity to grow into a security leadership role.
  • Engaging and dynamic team working towards a common mission.
  • Competitive salary.
  • Sponsorship of annual maintenance and membership fees for relevant cybersecurity certifications.

jobs.excerpt: Join Sapiens as our Lead Business Value Delivery Architect / Lead Solution Architect and play a pivotal role in taking client-facing insurance solutions from the sales cycle through delivery and into SaaS and AI platform migration, holding every engagement to a designed business outcome rather than an evolving list of requirements.
jobs.description:
Join Sapiens as our Lead Business Value Delivery Architect / Lead Solution Architect and play a pivotal role in taking client-facing insurance solutions from the sales cycle through delivery and into SaaS and AI platform migration, holding every engagement to a designed business outcome rather than an evolving list of requirements.

This is a role that sits between presales and delivery and stays engaged across both, spanning P&C, Life, and in future Reinsurance, with a particular focus on the non functional and operational requirements our industry consistently under-invests in. If you are deeply fluent in insurance product suites and platform roadmaps, comfortable holding both a head of claims and an engineer in the same conversation, and driven to keep clients and internal teams honest to the outcomes they signed up for - we'd love to hear from you.

What we are looking for

  • You have a track record designing or leading solution design in complex, enterprise insurance implementations, ideally spanning both presales and delivery.
  • Ability to speak credibly to both a head of claims and an engineer, across P&C, Life, and Reinsurance.
  • Strong on non functional and operational requirements: performance, scale, availability, security, integration, operability, not only functional design.
  • Demonstrated ability to hold the professional and outcome vector, keeping internal teams and clients aligned to agreed business outcomes. Given that this accountability is a core responsibility of the role, it is a required skill, not simply a welcome personality trait.
  • Experience with, or strong aptitude for, legacy to SaaS or core platform migration work.
  • Comfortable operating in a function that is still being built. Process and tooling will be defined in parallel with the first deals.
  • You ideally have hands-on experience with cloud-native platforms and a proven track record working at Born-in-the-Cloud (BIC) companies, bringing modern SaaS delivery practices to a global enterprise environment.
  • Proficient in leveraging AI-driven tools and platforms to design, optimize, and scale enterprise solution architectures.

What you will do:

You'll own the professional and content thread of the solution end to end – across four connected areas of impact:

Value Definition – Presales solution design

  • Engage during the sales cycle, from general discovery through down select, to build product and industry context on the opportunity.
  • Frame the solution around the client's business outcomes, not a requirements checklist. Map what they are trying to achieve to what the platform actually delivers.
  • Establish a business outcome baseline with the client: what they will be able to do post go live that they cannot do today, and how both sides will measure it.
  • Own the definition of done, agreed jointly with the client.
  • Explicitly cover non functional and operational requirements: performance, scale, availability, security, integration, data migration, operability, and support, rather than leaving them to surface in build.
  • Feed into the implementation plan: the right order of implementation and the known dependencies, especially those on the client.
  • Where the platform does not meet the client's expected outcomes, own the resolution with Product and R&D. Either secure a commitment to build it into the core platform, with timelines aligned accordingly, or design it into the extension layer shipped with the core. The SA owns these conversations.
  • Act as the next layer of depth behind the presales and industry expert team. Presales surfaces the opportunity, the SA architects the solution.
  • Support the bid with clearly stated assumptions. The fixed price commercial construct itself is owned by Sales and the PD.

Delivery integrity

  • Move into rapid planning immediately after signing. Harden the solution against what the platform delivers, steering toward standard configuration over bespoke build.
  • Hand over a clear, documented solution design to the delivery team at the start of build, and safeguard the integrity of that design through delivery.
  • Hold all parties, internal teams and the client, accountable to the agreed business outcomes and how they will be achieved. This is outcome and professional accountability. The PM or PD holds delivery and the client to scope, timeline, and commitments.
  • Stay engaged through quarterly business reviews to catch outcome or value drift early.
  • Apply the definition of done. The project is complete only when the client is positioned to realise the value agreed at the outset, not simply when the system goes live.

Migration

  • For assigned clients, own migration outcomes through the analyse, dispose, bridge, and migrate framework, across the existing product portfolio and beyond.
  • Define, with each client, the specific value the migration unlocks and the KPIs that will confirm it. Migration is a value conversation, not only a technical one.

Tooling, AI, and continuous improvement

  • Serve as the first internal customer for AI in delivery, and own the tools and the standard for how they are used.
  • Set which source wins when inputs conflict: signed document over email, email over deck, deck over verbal.
  • Set what a human must verify in AI drafted work, rather than approve on sight.
  • Flag what the inputs do not say: tacit process, stakeholder disagreement, edge cases, not just what the AI summarised.
  • Work as part of the SA group to improve processes, outputs, and tools for quicker, better implementations, especially the SaaS migration factory, including a feedback loop from delivery back to discovery to recalibrate where discovery got the scope wrong.

What Success Looks Like:

  • Every signed programme has a documented, client agreed business outcome baseline, a joint definition of done, and go live success criteria.
  • Non functional and operational requirements are surfaced and designed in up front, not discovered in build.
  • Platform gaps are resolved deliberately, through a core platform commitment or an extension layer build, rather than emerging during delivery.
  • Delivery builds to the handed over design with minimal rework driven by scope or requirements ambiguity.
  • The SA group's processes, tools, and outputs measurably shorten implementations over time.

jobs.description:
Find the moment. Make the first second count.

We are hiring short-form video editors for Eric Siu's AI, marketing, business, entrepreneur, podcast, and long-form content. Include “Short-form editing is cool” in the subject line. Otherwise, your application will be disqualified.

You will find strong moments in source material and turn them into polished vertical videos for Instagram Reels, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts. The work needs immediate hooks, clear pacing, kinetic captions, purposeful B-roll or graphics, clean sound, and CTAs that fit the idea.

We need editors who make strong editorial decisions without waiting for exact timestamps or frame-by-frame direction.

About Single Grain

Single Grain is a revenue marketing agency. We build pipeline-focused systems that compound, not campaigns that expire. We have helped more than 500 companies, from venture-backed startups to the Fortune 500, drive measurable growth.

Eric Siu hosts the Leveling Up podcast and co-hosts Marketing School with Neil Patel. The content reaches marketers, founders, and operators across YouTube, podcasts, email, and social platforms.

We operate as an AI-native team. Every role uses AI to improve speed, quality, judgment, and leverage. AI output still requires strong human taste and quality control.

Your mission

Edit current, platform-native short-form videos that make complex business ideas clear, hold attention, publish on schedule, and create qualified audience action.

Primary KPI: reliable weekly delivery that improves retention, completion, first-pass approval, or qualified CTA actions from the first-30-day baseline.

What you will own

  • Review podcasts, long-form videos, and original recordings to identify strong moments.

  • Build the cold open and structure the clip for immediate clarity.

  • Edit vertical videos with native pacing, accurate captions, clean audio, and purposeful visual support.

  • Adapt the edit to the idea and platform instead of applying one template to every clip.

  • Use AI for tasks such as transcript search, clip discovery, rough cuts, captions, cleanup, or quality control while keeping editorial judgment human.

  • Deliver organized files, clear versions, platform-ready exports, and fast revisions.

  • Review performance feedback and improve the next batch.

  • Flag weak source material or unclear briefs early and propose a better approach.

What success looks like

In 30 days, you understand the audience and visual language, deliver a reliable weekly batch, and meet the agreed turnaround and revision standards.

By 60 days, you find promising moments without exact timestamps and use performance feedback to improve hooks, pacing, clarity, and CTAs.

By 90 days, you own the editing workflow from source intake through organized handoff and show measurable improvement from the first-month baseline.

Evidence we need to see

  • Two recent short-form or podcast-clipping examples for B2B, AI, SaaS, business, entrepreneur, marketing, finance, or expert-led creators.

  • Your exact role in selecting the moment, shaping the hook, editing the piece, and delivering the result.

  • Current platform-native craft, not a stale reel or generic clip-farm template.

  • A concrete AI-assisted editing workflow and the QA method you use.

  • Proof that you can work with minimal handholding and meet deadlines.

  • Quantified retention, completion, CTA, lead, or business-outcome evidence attributable to your work.

This role is not

  • A role for gaming, children's media, meme-only, or broad entertainment portfolios with no strong relevant examples.

  • A role that waits for exact timestamps and complete edit instructions.

  • A template-only clipping role.

  • A role where listing AI tools substitutes for showing a real workflow.

  • A views-only role. We care whether the right audience watches and acts.

How the process works

  1. Application and portfolio review.

  2. A focused screen against the role outcomes.

  3. A paid two-clip test from one real source asset.

  4. One revision round and a short walkthrough of your decisions.

  5. References and final decision.

The paid test is timeboxed and will not be used as unpaid production work.

Work model and compensation

This is a fully remote, per-project contractor role, and we may hire more than one editor. Applicants must state their per-clip or weekly-batch rate, expected capacity, normal turnaround, revision policy, available working hours, and start date.

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Staff Software Engineer owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems. This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

What You'll Own

  • Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

  • Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

  • Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

  • Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

  • Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

  • Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

Nice to have

  • Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

  • Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

Location

This is a remote role. We hire globally and work across multiple countries and time zones.

Candidates should be comfortable working effectively in a distributed, fast-moving international team and collaborating with colleagues across different locations.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for Product Owner Technical to own product areas within BJAK's AI Investing

This role is for builders who can understand users, define product direction, work with engineering and design, launch fast and keep improving after release.

What You'll Own

  • Own product areas across insurance, payments, savings, investing, travel or other financial services.

  • Define user problems, product scope, success metrics, roadmap and launch plans.

  • Work with engineering, design, data, operations, compliance and business teams.

  • Turn complex financial products into simple, usable customer journeys.

  • Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.

  • Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.

  • Make trade-offs between speed, user experience, business impact, compliance and operational complexity.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience as Product Manager, Product Owner Technical, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.

  • Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.

  • Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.

  • Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.

  • Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.

  • High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.

  • Experience in fintech, insurance, payments, consumer apps or high-growth products is a strong advantage.

The Kind of Builder We Want

  • Starts from user problems, not feature lists.

  • Can make decisions with incomplete information.

  • Knows how to ship quickly and learn after launch.

  • Works well with engineering without hiding behind process.

  • Honest about what changed because of their work versus wider team effort.

This Role Is Not For

  • People who only write decks and do not drive execution.

  • PMs who cannot work deeply with engineering.

  • Candidates who need perfect data before making decisions.

  • People who launch features and then stop caring.

  • PMs who exaggerate business impact without understanding attribution.

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Portugal. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Portugal.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

1. Online assessment or practical task

2. Role-specific interview

3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

Projects stay organized, responsibilities are clear, and milestones are met. Risks surface early, leadership receives actionable updates, and improvements deliver results in everyday healthcare operations.

jobs.excerpt: About DarkroomFounded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.
jobs.description:
About Darkroom

Founded in 2017, we set out to redefine what a modern agency could be, by replacing the inertia of legacy advertising behemoths with a model built for speed, intelligence, and measurable impact.

At our core, Darkroom is a human services company powered by Shadow, a universal AI commerce layer that integrates executive-level strategy with proprietary agentic technology. This fusion enables our teams to deliver outsized returns by enhancing creative output, operational efficiency, and revenue generation across every stage of the customer journey.

Our track record speaks for itself: billions in attributable revenue driven across e-commerce marketplaces, media networks, DTC ecosystems, and social commerce platforms. Every engagement feeds into our proprietary data infrastructure, enabling a continuous feedback loop that accelerates growth, improves margins, and compounds results across our client portfolio.

What began as a boutique design studio has evolved into one of the fastest-growing private companies in America (Inc. 5000) and among the most effective performance media agencies of the 2020s (Varos). Our founders were recognized by Forbes 30 Under 30 for advancing the intersection of technology, marketing, and advertising, cementing Darkroom's role as a defining player in the future of media innovation.

About the Role

Our client is a fast-growing consumer AI company with a mobile app at the center of its business. They’re looking for a strategic, results-driven Head of Marketing to own user growth end to end: app installs, registrations, activation, engagement, and retention.

You’ll build and lead an integrated consumer marketing strategy spanning paid media, performance creative, organic social, website content, and lifecycle marketing. A central part of the role is serving as the primary strategic lead and point of accountability for the company’s external media, creative, and performance marketing agency of record. You’ll set objectives, guide creative and media strategy, manage investment decisions, and make sure the agency delivers measurable outcomes.

This is a role for someone who pairs strong consumer marketing and creative instincts with deep expertise in performance marketing, mobile app growth, and analytics.

What You’ll Own

  • The integrated consumer marketing strategy, aligning awareness, acquisition, activation, and retention with company growth goals

  • Performance against ambitious targets for app installs, registrations, efficient CAC, and downstream engagement and retention

  • The go-to-market calendar across product launches, feature releases, seasonal campaigns, and growth initiatives

  • The agency of record relationship: translating business goals into clear briefs, priorities, creative requirements, and KPIs, and holding the agency accountable to results

  • Paid acquisition strategy across Meta, Google, Apple Ads, TikTok, YouTube, and emerging platforms, including budget allocation, channel diversification, audience strategy, and testing priorities

  • Performance creative strategy that continuously tests messaging, value propositions, use cases, audiences, and formats

  • Weekly performance reviews, strategic planning sessions, and periodic business reviews with the agency

  • Organic social strategy and brand voice across TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, X, and LinkedIn, making advanced AI feel accessible and relevant to everyday consumers

  • Creator, influencer, community, and partnership programs that drive authentic product advocacy

  • Lifecycle marketing from onboarding through activation, engagement, retention, and win-back, across email, push, and in-app messaging

  • Behavioral segmentation and activation milestones, in partnership with Product, tied to stronger retention

  • Website and app store content strategy, landing pages, and conversion optimization (visitor-to-registration, web-to-app)

  • Organic discoverability across SEO, ASO, and GEO, including AI-powered search and answer experiences

  • Brand positioning and messaging that translate complex AI capabilities into clear, emotionally resonant, accurately substantiated benefits

  • Integrated launches aligning creative, paid, organic, web, and lifecycle

  • The measurement framework connecting spend to installs, registrations, activation, retention, and LTV, including attribution, incrementality testing, and executive reporting

  • Marketing budgets, vendors, tooling, workflows, and a prioritized roadmap, plus recommendations on future team structure and hiring

Must Have

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in consumer, growth, or digital marketing, with significant ownership of strategy and business results

  • Experience leading marketing for a consumer mobile app, subscription product, or high-growth consumer tech business

  • A proven track record driving measurable growth in app installs, registrations, acquisition, and activation

  • Deep knowledge of performance marketing across paid social, search, video, and mobile app advertising

  • Significant experience directing external media, creative, or performance agencies, with direct ownership of budget, strategy, and results

  • Strong creative judgment and the ability to give actionable creative direction that connects storytelling to performance

  • Hands-on experience with lifecycle and retention marketing (onboarding, CRM, segmentation, re-engagement)

  • Experience owning website content, landing pages, SEO, and CRO

  • Strong analytical fluency across attribution, funnel performance, cohort retention, and marketing ROI

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication, with the ability to turn complex products into compelling consumer narratives

Nice to Have

  • Experience marketing AI, productivity, or other emerging consumer tech products

  • Hands-on experience with incrementality testing or MMM

  • Familiarity with mobile measurement and lifecycle tools (e.g., AppsFlyer, Adjust, Braze, Iterable)

  • Experience with ASO and optimizing for AI-driven search (GEO)

  • A background building organic social or creator programs centered on short-form video

Culture Fit

  • You own the number, even when execution sits with a partner

  • You’re comfortable moving between big-picture strategy and hands-on execution in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment

  • You hold a high creative bar and back decisions with data

  • You build strong working relationships across Product, Engineering, Data, Creative, and leadership

  • You default to experimentation and learn quickly from results

Not the bar: if your experience is mainly in B2B or ecommerce without mobile app growth, or you’ve managed agencies only from a distance without owning budget and outcomes yourself, this likely isn’t the right fit.

What It's Like to Work at Darkroom

Darkroom is not a typical agency. We are looking for A players who want to build something great. We move fast, think deeply, and expect every team member to bring insight and rigor to everything they touch. We hold a high bar for performance, creativity, and ownership, but we also support each other relentlessly. No egos, no red tape. Just world-class talent building something remarkable.

We believe in autonomy with accountability, truth over comfort, and outcomes over optics.

  • Unlimited PTO + US holidays: Rebooting is part of the work. Take the time you need to stay sharp.

  • Embedded with the client: This role is based in the San José Area and works from the client's office four to five days a week, as part of a 150-person independent agency.

  • Health & Wellness: Company-sponsored medical, dental, and vision coverage.

  • Finances, growth, and retirement: Darkroom offers a robust 401(k) program with company match and profit-sharing opportunities to help you save and grow as the company grows.

  • Parental Leave: Flexible parental leave to support new parents during this important transition.

  • Growth: Our interdisciplinary model gives every Darkroomer exposure far beyond their core role. Grow your skills, expand your influence, and stay at the forefront of the industry.

Equal Opportunity Statement

Darkroom is an equal opportunity workplace. We are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.

jobs.description:
Overview

Reporting to the Senior Director, Corporate FP&A & Enterprise Functions, the Senior Financial Analyst will own the company’s consolidated financial model and financial metrics framework. This role combines revenue and functional plans from Finance Business Partner (FBP) teams into a unified outlook for revenue, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, and other key results; validates cross-functional assumptions and dependencies; and turns consolidated results into actionable company-wide insights. The analyst will partner closely with FP&A teams supporting Sales and Marketing/GTM, Product and Professional Services, R&D and Engineering, and Enterprise Functions, while serving as the Finance Business Partner for designated G&A functions.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Own and continuously improve the consolidated financial model, integrating validated assumptions and outputs for revenue, gross margin, labor, operating expenses, EBITDA, and other material measures across forecasts, budgets, and long-range plans.
  • Partner with FBP teams to understand and consolidate forecasts and models for revenue, Professional Services, CVO, Product, R&D, G&A, labor, and other operations.
  • Maintain clear links and reconciliations among functional models, the consolidated P&L, actual results, and executive reporting, and partner with Accounting to resolve material variances.
  • Review functional plans for consistency and identify dependencies, gaps, duplicate or conflicting assumptions, risks, opportunities, and potential management actions.
  • Develop company-wide scenarios and sensitivity analyses that show how changes in functional drivers affect consolidated P&L results and inform recommendations.
  • Own the company-wide financial metrics framework, including standard definitions, calculation methods, governance, documentation, and reporting consistency, in partnership with functional metric owners.
  • Support monthly and executive reporting with consolidated analysis, KPI reporting, validated model outputs, company-wide scenarios, and key risks and opportunities.
  • Analyze company-wide variances and work with FBPs to connect functional drivers to consolidated financial impacts.
  • Serve as Finance Business Partner for designated G&A functions, supporting budgets, forecasts, monthly budget-to-actual analysis, headcount and purchase requests, business cases, ad hoc decisions, and recommendations to functional leaders.
  • Partner with systems teams and external consultants to document and implement approved consolidation logic, model integrations, and metric calculations in the planning environment.
  • Maintain model documentation, assumption tracking, data-validation controls, and governance standards, while identifying opportunities to automate recurring consolidations, reconciliations, scenario analyses, and KPI reporting.
  • Clearly present financial findings, scenarios, implications, and recommendations to FP&A leaders and other stakeholders.
  • Support Corporate FP&A’s ownership of executive deliverables and the consolidated financial narrative by providing validated results, metrics, scenarios, and analysis.
  • Complete other duties and projects as assigned.

Skills Required

  • Strong financial modeling, analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to combine multiple functional models into a consolidated company view.
  • Strong knowledge of income-statement relationships, forecasting, budgeting, long-range planning, variance analysis, and scenario modeling.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and business-partnering skills, with the ability to explain model results to technical and nontechnical audiences and collaborate across FP&A, Accounting, and business leadership.
  • Advanced Excel proficiency and experience with financial planning platforms; familiarity with data-querying, analytics, and visualization tools is preferred.
  • Strong organizational and documentation skills, including model governance, assumption tracking, metric definitions, and process documentation.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and recurring deliverables in a fast-paced environment, with strong attention to detail and awareness of broader business and financial implications.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Analytics, or a related discipline.
  • At least five years of relevant experience in FP&A, corporate finance, financial modeling, or a comparable analytical role.
  • Proven experience building or maintaining consolidated P&L forecasts and financial models.
  • Experience consolidating inputs across multiple functions, business units, or operating models.
  • Experience supporting annual budgets, rolling forecasts, long-range plans, and scenario planning.
  • Experience defining, calculating, or governing company-wide financial and operating metrics.
  • Experience providing FP&A support to business functions or G&A leaders.
  • Experience in SaaS or another subscription-based business is preferred.
  • Experience in a private equity-backed organization is preferred.
  • Familiarity with planning systems such as Adaptive and BI tools such as Power BI is preferred.
  • Experience working with ERP, CRM, business intelligence, or other financial data sources is preferred.

Position Overview

The Principal HL7 Integration Engineer oversees all technical aspects of Synapse product HL7 integration, from install, configure and validation phases through product go-live, for all Synapse MI products. The Principal HL7 Integration Engineer must have expert level knowledge in all areas of medical informatics, IT infrastructure design and deployment, medical imaging industry in general and clinical environment workflow.

In addition to technical expertise, HCUS relies on The Principal HL7 Integration Engineer to deliver industry leading customer satisfaction, requiring excellent communication and verbal skills within project teams and externally with customers.

The person must be adept to working in highly dynamic multi-vendor environment and stay up to date on healthcare and general IT trends, best practices, regulations, and a wide range of hardware and software products.

This position requires interaction with sales, technical support, field service, the end user, outside vendors and all other service and administrative groups within Fujifilm involved in the order through remittance process. Must develop relationships and communication channels to ensure status feedback and cooperation with shareholders. Responsible in maintaining existing written documentation, periodic review, and publish.

Company Overview

At FUJIFILM Healthcare Americas Corporation, we’re on a mission to innovate for a healthier world, and we need passionate, driven people like you to help us get there. Our cutting-edge healthcare solutions span diagnostic imaging, enterprise imaging, endoscopic and surgical imaging, as well as in-vitro diagnostics.

But we don’t stop at healthcare; our Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) team harnesses advanced radiography solutions to keep transportation infrastructure, aerospace, and oil and gas assets safe and running smoothly.

Ready to innovate, collaborate, and make a difference? Join us and bring your big ideas to life while working in a dynamic, flexible environment that fuels your creativity and drive.

Our headquarters is in Lexington, Massachusetts, an inspiring healthcare research hub in a historic town.

Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit:

Job Description

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Work closely with MI Project Management (PM) team to deliver high quality Synapse product solutions.
  • Act as primary technical resource for MI HL7 Implementation projects across Synapse product lines in designing end to end HL7 integration architectures (inbound / outbound/ bidirectional).
  • Perform enterprise level custom projects:
    • Data migrations
    • Interface integration and data conversion
    • Integrate at least one or more Synapse MI products with all third-party healthcare information systems e.g. dictation, EMR, PACS, CVIS, RIS, HIS, VNA, Synchronicity, EMR, LIS (Laboratory Information Systems) and Anatomic Pathology, etc.
  • Design reusable integration patterns and templates. Develop secure end to end communication (TLS, VPN, Certificates and encryption).
    • Adhere to rigorous internal project communication guidelines using tools provided.
    • Extensive documentation development:
    • Customer specific solution design documentation.
    • Best practice documentation.
    • Specification revisions
    • Validation and testing procedures (Test plan)
  • Learn new Synapse and third-party products as they are released.
  • Participate in Subject Matter Expert (SME) program.
  • Participate in non-project related activities, such as presenting material at team meetings or working with cross-functional teams on internal projects.
  • Mentor, train, and actively participate in knowledge transfer to peers.
  • Must be able to work independently as the lead project technical resource.
  • Deliver consistently high level of customer satisfaction.
  • Possess consistently high level of customer satisfaction.
  • Ability to lead HL7 projects with minimal supervision.
  • Strong decision making and problem-solving skills.
  • Mentoring and couching mindset.
  • Adheres to the Company's quality and regulatory compliance requirements, without exception, and ensures that all job duties inherent in the position description are performed in accordance with established policies and procedures.
  • Comply with all applicable U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) medical device regulatory requirements, applicable ISO 13485 standard requirements and all other applicable laws, regulations, and standards.

Qualifications

Principal HL7 Integration Engineer must be professional experienced in designing, implementing, validating, documenting, and executing complex technical projects. A person in this position is expected to possess an expert understanding of Information Technologies and their utilization in a clinical environment. Emphasis is on the areas of radiology, cardiology, RIS, Synchronicity, Anatomic Pathology, LIS (laboratory Information System) and VNA services. Areas of expertise include but are not limited to internal and third-party product testing and validation, systems functionality and availability, business continuity and disaster recovery (DR), business and academic needs, work and data flows, integration. A well-developed analytical, leadership, project management, decision making, and oral and written communication skills, with the ability to quickly learn new technologies are required.

  • BS, BE or equivalent degree in computer related field. AA with significant experience working in a related industry.
  • Experienced in use and applicability of HL-7 and DICOM standards.
  • Experienced in working with relational databases (Oracle and SQL Server)
  • Minimum of 6-8 years’ experience in HL7 integration in a hospital related environment.

  • Familiarity with EMR systems such as Epic, Cerner, Athena, Trubridge (CPSi), Meditech, Affinity, etc.

  • Hands-on experience with interface engines (e.g., Iguana, Rhapsody, Mirth Connect, Cloverleaf, CorePoint, Ensemble, etc.)

  • Demonstrated problem solving skills and project management skills
  • Assertive team player with demonstrated initiative.
  • Ability to work independently and meet deadlines.
  • Able to demonstrate excellent organizational and time management skills.
  • Must be very organized and multi-tasking.
  • Must be able to interact with various teams in a matrix environment.
  • Experience in general computer network technology and high-performance computing systems and familiarity with:
    • MS Windows Client Operating System
    • MS Windows Server Operating Systems
    • MS Clustering
    • MS Message Queuing
    • MS Internet Information Server
    • Basic TCP/IP Networking Skills
    • Proficient with MS products, VMWare, and Remote Access, etc.
  • Experience in healthcare related field or hospital environment required.
  • Knowledge of Radiology, Dictation, Cardiology and Electronic Medical Records systems workflow.
  • Demonstrated ability to transfer knowledge to peers and other associates.
  • Supervises the work of others as requested.
  • Demonstrates exceptional project leadership, time management, negotiation, communication, and prioritization skills.

The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

As Principal Machine Learning Engineer, you own the execution layer of our intelligence, turning research and model capabilities into reliable, scalable production systems.

You will work across the model lifecycle: data, training, evaluation, inference, and deployment. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who wants to operate at the intersection of research, systems, and product.

  • Own the end-to-end ML systems powering our company, from data and training to evaluation, inference, and deployment.

  • Build and evolve training and fine-tuning pipelines for large models.

  • Design evaluation systems that measure capability, robustness, safety, and real-world product performance.

  • Build data pipelines and systems for high-quality real-world and synthetic training data.

  • Establish reliable production infrastructure for deploying, monitoring, and continuously improving models.

  • Partner closely with research and application engineering to turn model capabilities into product improvements.

  • Make pragmatic technical trade-offs and rapidly iterate based on real-world performance.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience building and shipping ML systems used in production, not just research prototypes.

  • Strong understanding of modern large-model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and inference.

  • Strong software engineering and systems fundamentals.

  • Experience operating ML workloads at meaningful scale, particularly GPU-based systems.

  • Strong technical judgment and the ability to navigate ambiguous problems independently.

  • A bias toward experimentation, measurement, and shipping.

  • High standards for correctness, reliability, and production quality.

Outcomes

  • Research and models reliably translate into production-ready solutions with clear performance and quality targets.

  • ML pipelines, training loops, and inference systems are stable, efficient, and maintainable.

Tech Stack

  • Draft, edit, and finalize design plans and details using appropriate and efficient methods and adhering to Geosyntec drafting standards.
  • Understand and visualize overall civil/geotechnical engineering concepts, such as grading / site layouts, and translating abstract concepts to design drawings.
  • Analyze sketches, notes and other input material to determine best approach to complete a drawing set.
  • Manage the production of drawing sets / design data from creation, markup and modification based on overall design.
  • Assign work to, mentor, train, and supervise CAD technicians in the preparation of design drawings and details and reviewing completed work products to ensure quality.

(required)

Proficiency includes a strong understanding of Civil 3D annotation styles and annotation tools, object and label styles, solid understanding of key objects such as surfaces, alignments, profiles, profile views, pipe networks, feature Lines, grading groups, assemblies, and corridors, surface analyses and volume calculations. (required)

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, MNO Data
jobs.excerpt: About GiveDirectlyWhat if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?
locationRestrictions: Congo, The Democratic Republic of the
jobs.description:
About GiveDirectly

What if the most effective way to fight poverty was also the simplest: give people money and trust them to decide what they need?

Since 2011, GiveDirectly has proven that idea at scale. We’ve delivered more than $1B in cash directly to 2+ million people living in poverty and crisis across 15 countries, and rigorous research shows the results: healthier kids, stronger businesses, sturdier homes, and more resilient families and local economies. Cash is now widely recognized as one of the most scalable, cost-effective, and dignified forms of aid.

Our ambition goes beyond our own programs. We want cash to become the benchmark for aid, much as the index fund became the benchmark for investing, so that every aid dollar is held to one question: is this doing more good than giving the money directly to people living in poverty?

We’re growing fast, and this is a rare and important moment to join.

We expect to hit $1B in revenue in 2026 with significant growth forecast for 2027. At the same time we are building a new technology stack and operating model designed for a roughly 10x change in scale, and we are actively pursuing partnerships with major funders to move even more money in bigger ways, to people who need it. We are known for our extensive integration of technology into field processes; our quantitative approach to performance measurement; and our commitment to rigorous, independent, experimental evaluation of our impact, with multiple Randomized Control Trials completed and others in progress.

How we work

Our team spans 20+ countries and 69 languages. Our culture is candid, analytical, and non-hierarchical. We expect high ownership and give people real responsibility early. Our values are central to how we hire, work, and grow, and they are deliberately opinionated:

  1. Recipients first. Recipients’ preferences come before those of donors or ourselves.
  2. Team next. We optimize for organizational success, not individual success.
  3. Be proactively candid. We say what we believe and share information openly.
  4. Create positive energy. We aim to be a source of energy for colleagues, not a drain.
  5. Think rigorously; act quickly. We reason from first principles, then act rather than debate.
  6. Know yourself and grow. We own our imperfections and seek feedback to grow.
  7. Accept reality. Propose solutions. We focus on what can change and bring solutions, not just problems.
  8. Be productively ambitious. We take risks for step-change impact, not incremental progress.

If they describe how you like to work and they energize you, this could be a great fit.

Want to learn more? Read and listen:

We are one of Time100’s Most Influential Companies of 2026, and our work has been covered by The Economist, NPR, TED, and The Washington Post. We're now preparing to deliver billions of dollars a year to people in extreme poverty, if funding allows. Read our CEO's essay on what that will take.

About this role

GiveDirectly gives cash directly to people living in poverty and in emergencies. Both depend on the same question: did this person live in this place, at this time? We ask it when we target the poorest households, and when a disaster displaces a community overnight. Location records held by Mobile Network Operators (MNO) can help us estimate an answer to this question at scale. We work with MNOs so they can infer, from their own records, whether a subscriber was resident in a target area over a defined period. Robust residence location inference from MNO data requires in-depth analytical work, and the methods we design have to run on an operator's systems - most often implemented by their engineers - under strict data protection and confidentiality rules.

We are hiring a Senior Data Scientist to progress our work on location inference from MNO data, and to make it repeatable. Your job is to improve and extend our library of method templates, adapt them to each new operator and setting, and design new elements when an intervention requires it. You'll assess what can be inferred from a given operator's data, specify the analysis clearly enough for their data engineers to implement, then test it with them remotely or on site. You'll support introductory meetings with MNOs, describing methodologies at a high level, and inform the work of data privacy and cybersecurity teams to ensure only necessary data are shared securely. You'll also help colleagues across GiveDirectly understand the strengths and limitations of this data source, so we design programs around questions it can best answer.

This work is live in several countries, and we're expanding it across the countries where we have offices and to low- and middle-income countries anywhere in the world when a crisis hits.

Reports to: Senior Product Manager - MNO data

Level: Senior Manager

Location: At this stage of GiveDirectly’s growth and scale, we’re prioritizing hiring in the countries below, where we can employ you through a GD entity or an established employer of record: Cameroon, Canada, Colombia, DRC, Germany, Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Netherlands, Nigeria, Poland, Portugal, Rwanda, South Africa, Spain, Turkey, Uganda, United Kingdom, and United States. This list reflects where our employment infrastructure is established today, and may evolve as we grow. If you’re based elsewhere and not open to relocation, we may not be able to consider your application for this role right now, but we’d encourage you to check back. Please note that we are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment Visas in the U.S. or U.K. at this time.

Travel Requirement: Substantial international travel, roughly 25 to 50% of your time depending on emergencies, sometimes at short notice - for workshops with operators to support programs and emergency responses.

What you’ll do:

  • Improve and extend our library of analytical method templates for establishing where people live from MNO data, and depending on circumstances, for detecting displacement or estimating poverty. Design novel methods when an intervention requires it.
  • Support colleagues in technical conversations with operators, bringing clarity on the data we need and why, and steering discussions toward technical designs that make the analysis workable.
  • Assess the information that can be inferred from each operator's data given data types and sparsity, and for each geography and targeted area. Support intervention design to account for data quality.
  • Write tests and method specifications for MNO data engineers to implement: steps, parameters, pseudocode, validation criteria.
  • Guide operator engineering teams through implementation, in writing and in person. Adapt methods to accommodate large data volume and computational constraints, balancing accuracy and operational needs.
  • Run in-country workshops with operators to support the set-up of new analyses and - where feasible - tune parameters based on statistical tests and distributions.
  • Feed every new analytical and implementation element back into standard templates, so the next country or intervention starts from a better position than the last.
  • Design for privacy from the start, so that as little data as possible has to be shared: aggregation, minimization, and where useful, privacy-enhancing technologies such as private set intersection or homomorphic encryption.
  • Protect the confidentiality of what operators share with us and improve internal data security processes and tools as we grow.
  • Build internal training material so that our technical and non-technical teams understand the strengths and limits of this data, and design interventions accordingly.

What you’ll bring:

  • Exceptional alignment with GiveDirectly Values and active demonstration of our core competencies: emotional intelligence, problem solving, project management, follow-through, and fostering inclusivity. We welcome and strongly encourage applications from candidates who have personal or professional experience in the low-income and/or historically marginalized communities that we serve.
  • Strong mathematical modeling, machine learning and statistics. You choose methods for the question rather than for their sophistication, and you value being able to explain a result over squeezing out the last point of performance.
  • Deep comfort with spatio-temporal data: temporal filtering, GIS, probability distributions, combinatorial reasoning, and working with sparse, irregular observations. Direct experience with Call Detail Records (CDRs) or latching data is a strong plus. Comparable experience with mobility, transport, sensor or remote-sensing data counts.
  • The ability to reason without ground truth. Much of this work has no validated answer to check against, and you're comfortable setting parameters by reading the shape of the data and defending that choice.
  • Pragmatism about the trade-off between accuracy and implementability. You've deliberately simplified a method to fit an operational constraint, and you can say what it cost you.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills. You can explain a method and its limitations to an operator's engineers, to their data protection officer, to their leadership and to colleagues with or without technical background. You write well and are comfortable presenting to these multiple audiences. You build trust with counterparts you don’t manage, and they want to work with you again.
  • Experience writing technical specifications that other teams implemented, clear enough that people you don't manage could follow them correctly.
  • Able to read and review SQL and Python written by others, and to find the logical error in someone else's query. Writing production-quality code yourself is welcome but not required. Enough understanding of large data volumes and databases to judge when analytical simplification is required.
  • Commitment to privacy by design as a foundational value and starting point rather than a compliance step: designing analyses so that less personal data has to be shared. Familiarity with privacy-enhancing technologies for shared computation (private set intersection, secure multi-party computation, homomorphic encryption) is a strong plus.
  • Commitment to confidentiality. You've handled a partner's commercially sensitive data and can describe the habits you built around it, not just the clause you signed.
  • Experience designing training material that changed how non-specialist colleagues used a data source.
  • Comfort in fast-moving contexts where the brief may often shift, and where your technical expertise and understanding may not be shared by other stakeholders.
  • Additional desirable experience may include: poverty modeling; familiarity with survey data and survey instruments; experience inside a mobile network operator or working closely with one; open-source contributions in the mobility estimation space.
  • Comfortable with travel to fragile and post-disaster contexts.
  • Language Requirement: English.
  • Language Preferences: French, Portuguese, Swahili or Spanish.

Compensation

We also have a no negotiation policy to ensure we are paying staff equitably across roles. Read more about our compensation philosophy here.

This role is fully remote, so if you are not based in the US, UK or Kenya, we will share an estimated salary benchmark for the country you are based in during the hiring process.

Working at GiveDirectly

All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to the person’s race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Flagging for US applicants: We invite you to "Know Your Rights" as an applicant.

Commitment to Safeguarding

As a global organization working with communities to eliminate extreme poverty, GiveDirectly takes the safeguarding of its recipients, staff, and partners seriously. To that end, GiveDirectly is a member of the Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, and will systematically check with previous employers about any abuse or misconduct related matters involving potential new hires. We may also employ other robust pre-hire screens, including in-depth reference checks, criminal background checks, and sanctions screens.

These efforts help us continue to build and maintain trust with the communities we work with, and prevent abuse to our recipients and staff.

**GD is committed to observing all local, national and international laws that protect people and basic human rights of all. GD is committed to a policy of “zero tolerance when it comes to preventing, reporting, or responding to any form of abuse or exploitation.” and expects anyone who works for GD to uphold the protection and safeguarding of our recipients as a priority.**

jobs.description:
School of Medicine Established in 1930, Duke University School of Medicine is the youngest of the nation's top medical schools. Be You

Occupational Summary

This position has the option to be 100% remote. Candidates must reside in one of the approved states for remote work, which can be viewed here:

This position will be located within the School of Medicine Shared Research Administration Resource Group and will play an active role in working with specifically identified departments to manage their portfolio of grants and contracts.

Pre-award activities include assisting departmental faculty/PI in the development, preparation, and submission of grant and contract proposals. Ensure all applications and contracts meet agency and university guidelines and published time tables and deadlines. Ensure proposals are entered and routed in a timely manner for further review. Post-award activities include detailed reconciliation of assigned project budgets, preparing complex budget reports, preparing adjustments and corrections in assigned project budgets for further review and approval in order to meet project goals and federal requirements.

This position is responsible for managing and overseeing an assigned portfolio of complex grants and contracts using knowledge of grant and contract management rules and regulations, technical expertise, and analytical skills.

Be Bold

Required Qualifications at this Level

Education/Training:

Work requires communications, analytical and organizational skills generally acquired through completion of a bachelor's degree program. Research or grants education and/or certification is preferred.

Successful completion of Financial Services Introduction to R3, Introduction to Duke GL, Introduction to Accounting, Sponsored Research Reporting, Research Administration at Duke (online), Basic Compliance (online), Duke Human Research Training (online), Budget Development and Negotiation Training, and Industry Funded Clinical Research—Process for Contracts within first six months of hire is required.

Successful completion of the Research Administration Academy (RAA) is expected. Employees hired into this classification without RAA training will work closely with their manager to schedule and complete the training within 12 months of start date. The expectation is that the staff member will maintain the requirements for their level. Failing to meet these requirements will be addressed through the performance review process.

Upon successful completion of expected training, the employee must maintain certification(s) by completing continuing education requirements.

Experience:

No experience required for candidates who possess a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a field of study directly related to the specific position.

Skills:

- Ability to analyze data and formulate conclusions.

- Ability to learn changing technologies related to grants and contracts management.

- Proficient use of computers; requires solid working knowledge of MS Office Suite (Word, Access, Excel, Power Point).

- Ability to communicate both verbally and in writing with all levels of the organization.

- Ability to manage and prioritize multiple projects/tasks simultaneously.

- Ability to create verbal and written reports.

- Knowledge of federal rules and regulations relating to research grant and/or contract activity

- Knowledge of Duke University policies and procedures relating to grant and contracts activity

- Knowledge of Duke University processes, systems and offices related to and/or involved in grant and contract submission and management.

- Understand and be able to apply federal and university rules to management of effort allocation for individuals compensated whole or in part from federal awards.

- Understand and be able to apply costing rules and regulations to federally funded projects.

- Experience with/Ability to perform required functions in SPS, R3, grants.duke and SES relating to assigned duties.

- Understand financial processes and controls including the reconciliation process

Tier Structure

Associate: Proficient as a grants and contracts administrator.

Advanced: Experienced, highly capable, and requires minimal oversight of work. Experience - 3 years of relevant experience (2 years for internal employees who have received 2 Exceeds Expectations on performance reviews). Training - RAA required in addition to 2 electives to prepare for AGM is required. AGM must be completed within 12 months.

Senior: Subject matter expert. May be responsible for mentoring and developing others. Experience - 6 years of relevant experience (5 years for internal employees who have received 4 Exceeds Expectations on performance reviews. CRA certification can also reduce the years of experience requirement to 5 years). Training - RAA and AGM required. Expected to attend all the appropriate internal updates.

Lead: Advanced tier competencies as well as responsibilities for mentoring and developing staff. Oversees work of others. May or may not carry same responsibilities as a full supervisor. Experience - 3 years of relevant experience (2 years for internal employees who have received 2 Exceeds Expectations on performance reviews). Training - RAA and AGM required. Expected to attend all the appropriate internal updates.

Choose Duke

Work Performed

Pre-award Job Responsibilities (30%)

  • Develop budgets and budget justification which include proofing the budget for inconsistencies and ensuring accuracy.
  • Prepare and submit grants and contracts through pre-award process utilizing both Sponsor and Duke regulations. Follow through to submission to Sponsor.
  • Advise the faculty/PI on administrative requirements in preparing proposal submissions.
  • Assist faculty/PI and study team with development of internal cost assessment and subsequent budget development and negotiation with sponsor including the use of the Clinical Research Management System, if applicable.
  • Prepare, coordinate and review proposal elements such as biosketches, justifications and facilities & resources for consistency, accuracy, and completeness.
  • Monitor compliance with agency and University regulations regarding submission; verify all financial information, including the application of the appropriate overhead rate for the project.
  • Review sponsored projects through Sponsored Projects System to Office of Research Administration to ensure compliance with University procedures and institutional signatures.
  • Participate, as necessary, in study initiation meetings to help facilitate internal cost assessment development and budget negotiations.

Post-award Job Responsibilities (50%)

  • Manage assigned projects and financial project portfolios.
  • Ensure understanding of the current fiscal performance of studies and identify areas of concern that need resolution. Advise faculty/PI on budget adjustments and revisions necessary to meet the sponsor requirements.
  • Monitor proposal status and advise faculty/PI on requirements and deadlines associated with research protection protocols
  • Manage budget, reporting and compliance timelines through the lifecycle of the grant or contract; communicate new WBSEs to appropriate department personnel.
  • Establish sub-recipient financial and reporting requirements; coordinate issuance of sub-agreements with ORA.
  • Reconcile monthly budget reports and inform faculty/PI and/or supervisor of corrections/adjustments that have been made.
  • Identify and submit the cost transfers resulting from budget reconciliation.
  • As requirements change, prepare and submit requests for re- budgeting/modifying the funded project. Reconcile and close all sub-recipient cost objects and obtain all sponsor-required reports.
  • Monitor compliance with agency and University regulations regarding reporting.
  • Maintain financial records per the institutional documents retention guidelines.
  • Monitor and determine appropriate charging of patient care expenses to the study cost object(s).
  • Manage overdrafts in line with unit procedures and institution guidelines.
  • Ensure proper recording of revenue associated with all projects; applying revenue management standards.
  • Close all funded projects consistent with university processes and timelines.

Administrative Job Responsibilities (20%)

  • Develop project management plan for review by the faculty/PI or senior level grants administrator.
  • May make cost-sharing adjustments to reflect appropriate labor distribution or related cost-sharing obligations.
  • Ensure process (SOP) is in place within the unit for proper handling and tracking of Sponsor payments into the project cost object. This process must be handled in accordance with the institution’s current policy.
  • Interpret departmental policies and procedures, making decisions on specific operating problems and issuing instructions on behalf of unit.
  • Apply federal and university rules to appropriately manage effort for individuals compensated, in whole or in part, from sponsored awards
  • Submit reports to the Grants and Contracts Manager/Divisional Administrator/Business Manager when requested

We’re looking for a hands-on Senior IoT Solutions Engineer to join Engineering Services, the team that takes on the technical problems that fall outside what our product and Support handle today. You’ll look at a PLC, a sensor, or a 20-year-old CNC and work out how to get its data into Factbird. Sales and Support turn to you when the answer is “it depends,” and you turn that into a clear yes, no, or “here’s how.” Then you write it down so the next person doesn’t need to ask.

About the role

Engineering Services solves the hardest technical problems, documents them, and shares the knowledge, so Factbird gets smarter and the same problem doesn’t come back. You’ll answer feasibility questions before deals close, design and build custom solutions, and fix the cross-domain problems no other team can place.

The team mission we are on: Engineering Services is a small team of experts finding solutions to a wide variety of challenges. In pre-sales we are supporting our AE's and Solution Consultants with feasibility testing the most complex customer setups or requirements. Often directly with the customers and their technical teams. In post-sales we collaborate with Cloud, FW and HW teams, and build and support a range of custom solutions. Our core mission is to increase documentation, standardization and empowering our colleagues in both pre- and post-sales roles to server the customers in the most technical cases.

What You'll Do

  • Answer feasibility questions from Sales: can we connect this machine, PLC, or sensor, and how
  • Design and build custom solutions: logic boxes, signal converters, IO-Link modules, EDGE flows, and Factbird® powered by OMRON NX1 programs that fill gaps the cloud platform can’t handle yet.
  • Design the integration: map the customer’s OT/IT environment and plan the data sources, tag structures, transformations, and security.
  • Root cause troubleshooting in live production. Smaller share of time, highest stakes
  • Document everything you build and fix: Solution Records, runbooks, and wiring guides for customers and internal teams, clear enough that someone else can pick it up. Version and back up every configuration.
  • Bench-test hardware before it ships, test the full data flow end to end (including failure recovery and restarts), and hand hardware to Logistics with a clear packing list.
  • Integrate customer systems through Kepware, Ignition, OPC UA, MQTT, EtherNet/IP, Modbus, and Node-RED.
  • Share what you know: help Support, Solution Consultants, and Hardware handle more on their own.
  • Streamline as you go: spot repeat work and clunky processes, and fix them or flag them. Build templates and scripts that make the next delivery faster.
  • Turn repeat workarounds into product input with a business case, so the workaround can disappear.
  • Join customer and prospect calls as the technical voice alongside Solution Consultants and Account Managers.

About you

You’re an experienced industrial automation engineer, as happy with a screwdriver as with a terminal. You know how factories work, and you’re comfortable saying “not directly, but here’s the route.”
You document like the next person depends on it, because they do. You can’t leave a clunky process alone: you always have an eye on how to make things simpler and more repeatable.
You’re flexible and self-directed: you take a high level of accountability and ownership. You can prioritize and deliver without daily supervision, and you troubleshoot systematically when things get ambiguous. The work changes week to week, and the team’s shape will keep evolving as Factbird grows. You’re happy to do what’s needed today while helping move things in a more scalable direction.

You love being the expert, but you equally love teaching others and making the teams around you smarter. And most of all, you care about making the answer simple for whoever asked.

Requirements:
  • A bachelor's degree in automation, electrical engineering, mechatronics, or similar, or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • At least 5 years in industrial automation or controls engineering, including hands-on work on the shop floor (7+ years preferred).
  • Hands-on PLC experience with at least one major vendor, e.g. Siemens, Omron, or Rockwell/Allen-Bradley.
  • Solid understanding of industrial protocols, e.g. OPC UA, Modbus, EtherNet/IP, MQTT.
  • Working knowledge of sensors and signals, like digital, analog (4–20 mA, 0–10 V), IO-Link, PNP/NPN, and energy metering.
  • Root cause analysis across hardware, networks, and software in live production environments.
  • Field experience commissioning or troubleshooting equipment in live plants.
  • Comfortable troubleshooting site networks, e.g. IP setup, routers, SIMs, and firewalls.
  • A clear communicator in English who can explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers.
  • A strong documentation habit: when you build it, you write it down.

Why Factbird?

The Sr. Director of Security Operations is responsible for overseeing a worldwide security operations team that protects the critical data center infrastructure for a complex, multi-hundred-million-dollar client account. This senior leadership position also leads operational control of the Physical Security Operations Center (PSOC), integrating strategic threat response with operational security oversight. The role provides executive-level direction, aligns Securitas and client objectives, and drives program performance, service delivery, and global consistency across all regions. This role requires a forward-thinking professional with a strong command of security operations, a passion for operational excellence, and the ability to lead and inspire high-performing teams in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.

What you’ll do

In this role, you will lead regional directors and manage the full spectrum of global physical security operations, ensuring audit compliance, operational standardization, and quality control. You will also lead global threat and incident response initiatives, develop preventative security strategies, and ensure effective PSOC operations. Your responsibilities include delivering executive-level briefings, nurturing key client relationships, collaborating across functions and time zones, and driving continuous improvement in security operations. Additionally, you’ll coordinate closely with our Program Management Office (PMO), lead cross-functional teams, and provide strategic insights to internal and client leadership.

What you need to apply

We are looking for a seasoned professional that has a bachelor’s degree in business, security, or a related field, along with 10–15 years of progressive leadership experience in physical security or account management, including 3–5 years at the senior director level. Global operational experience is required and a background in data centers, threat response, or PSOC leadership are strongly preferred. The role demands excellent communication skills across all organizational levels, strong leadership and crisis management capabilities, and a process-driven mindset.

This position involves travel (approximately 30% of the time), so a passion for travel (and a valid passport) is essential. This role may also have to work nights and weekends to support high priority events and off-hours incidents.

The role involves regular use of a computer and keyboard, frequent lifting or moving of items up to 10 pounds, and occasional lifting of up to 25 pounds.
