This leader will run intake, scheduling, matching, care coordination, and the day-to-day operations of Community Health Workers, with accountability for both the family experience and the operating performance behind it.

This is a hands-on builder role. You will make New Mexico work better now and build the model FronteraCare will use as we enter new states. We need someone who has already led operations across multiple markets, knows what should be standardized, and can recognize where local payer, regulatory, or workforce realities require a different approach.

Because Frontera builds its own technology, this role will also be a senior thought partner to Product and Engineering. You will help define what we build, pressure-test solutions against real workflows, and ensure our tools make access teams faster and more effective. Success means families reach care sooner, capacity is used well, leaders can see constraints early, and every new market begins with a stronger operating system than the one before it.

What You Will Do

Lead the Referral to Care Journey

  • Own the day-to-day performance of intake, scheduling, matching, care coordination, and CHW operations supporting ABA and diagnostic services.

  • Set priorities and operating expectations for responsiveness, throughput, accuracy, service quality, documentation, and escalations.

  • Create clear ownership and dependable handoffs across the referral-to-care journey, including handoffs with Payer Operations, so families do not get lost between teams or workflows.

  • Identify bottlenecks and failure points, then implement practical improvements that increase speed, reliability, and continuity of care.

Build the Access Operations Model for New Markets

  • Turn New Mexico's access operations into the foundation for future markets, with clear workflows, service expectations, systems, and playbooks.

  • Use direct multi-state operating experience to launch new markets quickly without rebuilding the function each time.

  • Define which elements should remain consistent across markets and where payer, regulatory, or local operating requirements call for flexibility.

  • Build the access readiness plan for each new state, including team capacity, systems setup, payer-operation dependencies, and ramp milestones.

  • Measure new-market performance against a common standard and adapt the model based on operating results.

Build and Lead the Team

  • Lead, coach, and develop team members and front-line leaders across access operations.

  • Set clear expectations for quality, responsiveness, productivity, accuracy, judgment, and ownership.

  • Create the management rhythm the team needs to perform consistently, including clear roles, training, coaching, quality review, and performance management.

  • Evolve the organization as the company grows, including adding specialized functional leadership when scale requires it.

  • Own onboarding, performance, development, and retention for the access organization after team members are hired.

Partner with Payer Operations

  • Build clear handoffs between access workflows and Payer Operations so authorization requirements do not create preventable delays in activation or continuity of care.

  • Maintain shared visibility into authorization and reauthorization status, aging, and escalation needs while Payer Operations retains direct ownership of execution.

  • Partner with Payer Operations, Clinical leadership, and Quality and Performance Systems to resolve cross-functional issues and improve the end-to-end family experience.

Lead Community Health Worker Operations

  • Own the daily workflows and process accountability for Community Health Workers embedded in intake and related care coordination work.

  • Set operational expectations for prioritization, productivity, process adherence, documentation, and training.

  • Maintain clear decision rights with the designated clinical leader, who provides clinical oversight through a dotted-line partnership.

Use Data to See Around Corners

  • Own the systems, workflow infrastructure, and reporting that support intake, scheduling, matching, and care coordination, including the interfaces with payer workflows.

  • Give leaders a reliable view of referral pipeline health, activation, scheduling performance, matching constraints, authorization turnaround, and capacity by market.

  • Own monthly forecasts for client demand and provider capacity across geography, schedules, matching needs, and coverage constraints.

  • Spot risks early, including seasonality, cancellations, provider attrition, payer delays, and local capacity constraints, and turn them into clear operating and hiring decisions.

Shape the Technology Behind Access

  • Act as a senior operating advisor and thought partner to Product and Engineering on the access roadmap, bringing a clear point of view on the problems worth solving.

  • Separate process, policy, training, and product problems so the team builds technology where it can create real leverage.

  • Translate complex front-line workflows into clear product requirements and decision criteria without oversimplifying the realities of care delivery.

  • Partner from discovery through rollout by testing solutions with users, driving adoption, and measuring whether the product improved speed, quality, or capacity.

  • Help design systems that can support multiple states while preserving the flexibility required by local markets and payer workflows.

Partner Across FronteraCare

  • Serve as the primary access operations partner to Clinical Directors and other clinical leaders on market execution.

  • Give the centralized People and Talent team the demand forecasts, role requirements, and interview partnership needed to recruit against operating needs. The People team retains ownership of recruiting.

  • Work closely with Payer Operations, Credentialing and Enrollment, and Quality and Performance Systems. Those teams retain functional ownership of payer operations, credentialing, provider enrollment, compliance readiness, and enterprise quality systems.

  • Partner with Finance on revenue-cycle handoffs and with Clinical leadership on diagnostics, ABA delivery, and clinical decisions, while those teams retain operating ownership of their functions.

Scope of the Role

This role directly owns the following functions and outcomes

  • Intake, scheduling, and matching

  • Care coordination workflows and CHW operational accountability

  • SOPs, training, quality review, escalations, and performance management within access operations

  • Access systems, workflow infrastructure, and operational reporting

  • Client demand and provider capacity forecasting tied to matching and hiring needs

  • The multi-state access operations playbook and common performance standards

What We Are Looking For

  • 10 or more years of progressive experience in access operations, intake, scheduling, care coordination, or adjacent healthcare services operations within ABA, behavioral health, or another complex healthcare services environment.

  • Direct responsibility for operations across multiple states, including experience opening, integrating, or scaling new markets.

  • A track record of building a repeatable operating model while adapting appropriately to differences in payer environments, regulation, labor markets, and local demand.

  • Working knowledge of authorization and reauthorization dependencies and the ability to build strong operating partnerships with payer operations teams.

  • Experience serving as a senior operating partner to Product and Engineering teams, with the ability to shape a roadmap, translate messy workflows into clear requirements, and drive adoption after launch.

  • Strong people leadership across front-line teams and managers, with the ability to create clarity, accountability, and consistent execution.

  • Experience building SOPs, quality controls, operating cadences, reporting, and scalable workflow discipline.

  • Strong judgment across capacity planning, matching, activation, schedule utilization, and care-delivery constraints.

  • Strong command of operating data and the judgment to look past the dashboard, find the underlying problem, and act.

  • A hands-on leadership style and the ability to move easily between strategy, team leadership, and the details of how the work gets done.

What Success Looks Like

  • New Mexico's access operations are predictable and responsive, with clear ownership at every handoff.

  • Families move from referral to active care faster and experience fewer avoidable delays.

  • Leaders have trusted visibility into the referral pipeline, authorization turnaround, scheduling performance, matching constraints, and market capacity.

  • Forecasts give the People team and market leaders enough lead time to respond to demand, seasonality, cancellations, attrition, and payer disruption.

  • A repeatable access playbook is ready for new states, including team design, systems, workflows, quality standards, payer requirements, and ramp milestones.

  • New markets reach access and scheduling standards faster because they begin with a proven operating model.

jobs.excerpt: About KestraKestra is the universal orchestration platform: open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.
jobs.description:
About Kestra

Kestra is the universal orchestration platform: open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide, including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole, Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars, hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.

About the role

Kestra Cloud is our fully managed SaaS edition of Kestra. Each customer gets a dedicated Kestra instance on dedicated infrastructure, so the platform is a fleet of isolated stacks rather than one shared cluster. It is in Beta today, running production workloads for early customers, with General Availability planned for 2027. Each instance runs arbitrary user code (scripts, containers, queries against their own systems) through hundreds of plugins, and the fleet grows with every new customer. Provisioning, upgrading, and observing dozens to hundreds of identical stacks without drift is the core problem.

We're looking for a Lead Tech SRE to own Kestra Cloud end to end: the architecture and specs, the delivery, the monitoring, and the continuous improvement of the platform. You decide how the platform should evolve, write it down, split it into work, and ship it with your team.

You would lead a team of three, yourself included. That means you stay hands-on (a large share of your week is Terraform, Kubernetes manifests, and incident work) while setting the technical direction, reviewing designs, and dispatching work to two SREs.

You work closely with the CTO, the platform engineering teams building the Kestra core, and our security engineer. This is an engineering leadership role, not a people-management-only one.

What you would do

Architecture & specs

  • Own the target architecture of Kestra Cloud on GCP: the per-customer dedicated stack (cluster, network, databases, queues), how it is templated and versioned, regions, and the path from Beta to GA.

  • Write the specs (design docs, RFCs, ADRs) that turn product needs into infrastructure work, and defend the trade-offs: cost per customer vs isolation level, GCP project vs cluster vs node pool per customer, managed service vs self-run.

  • Define SLOs and error budgets per service and per tier, and make them the basis for prioritization.

Delivery

  • Break specs into work and dispatch it across the team, then review and unblock. You set the bar for Terraform modules, Helm charts, and GitOps conventions.

  • Automate the customer instance lifecycle: provisioning, upgrades, scaling, backups, migration, and decommissioning, with no manual steps.

  • Own the release path of Kestra Cloud with ArgoCD and GitHub Actions: progressive rollouts, rollback, and upgrade safety across the whole fleet of customer instances.

Monitoring & operations

  • Build the observability stack (metrics, logs, traces, alerting) so that issues are caught before customers report them.

  • Run on-call and incident response for the team: rotation, runbooks, blameless postmortems, and follow-ups that actually ship.

  • Plan capacity for a workload that is bursty by nature, and keep autoscaling honest.

Continuous improvement

  • Drive cost efficiency (FinOps) on GCP: per-customer cost visibility, right-sizing, committed use, and spot where it fits.

  • Harden the platform with our security engineer: network policies, workload identity, secrets, and audit trails toward SOC 2 expectations.

  • Feed back into the product: when Kestra itself makes the cloud hard to run, you write the issue, propose the fix, and work with core engineering to land it.

Our Tech Stack

  • Cloud: GCP (GKE, Cloud SQL, GCS, Cloud Load Balancing, IAM / Workload Identity)

  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, Helm

  • Orchestration: Kubernetes, Docker

  • Deployment & Repository: GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

  • Monitoring & Logs: OpenTelemetry, Elastic, Prometheus, Grafana

  • Datastore: PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

  • Queuing: Redis, Kafka, AMQP

  • Programming language: Java, TypeScript (you read it; you don't need to write it daily)

What we are looking for

  • 8+ years in SRE, platform, or infrastructure engineering, including at least 2 years leading the technical direction of a team or a platform.

  • Deep, production-grade Kubernetes expertise: you have operated fleets of clusters at scale and know where they break (upgrades, configuration drift, networking, resource sizing).

  • Strong Google Cloud experience: GKE, IAM, networking (VPC, private clusters, load balancing), and managed data services. Equivalent depth on AWS or Azure is not a substitute here.

  • Expert Terraform: you have designed module structures and state layouts that scale to many identical customer environments, not just written resources.

  • Proven ability to architect, spec, and dispatch: you can show design docs you wrote, explain the trade-offs you made, and describe how you split the work and delivered it.

  • Real on-call and incident experience, including running postmortems and turning them into durable fixes.

  • SaaS operations background: you have run a product for paying customers, with SLOs that mattered.

  • Fluent in English and comfortable working autonomously in a fully remote environment.

  • Pragmatism: you pick the boring solution when it works and can explain why.

Nice to have

  • Experience running workloads that execute untrusted or user-defined code (sandboxing, gVisor, node pool isolation).

  • Built or operated a fleet control plane for per-customer environments (Kubernetes operators, Crossplane, GKE Fleet / Config Sync, or custom provisioning services).

  • FinOps practice on GCP: per-customer cost attribution, committed use discounts, spot node pools.

  • Exposure to SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audits from the infrastructure side.

  • Familiarity with workflow orchestration (Kestra, Airflow, Temporal, or similar) or the JVM in production.

Your first six months

  1. Month 1: take over the current architecture, audit the current Kestra Cloud architecture, and map the gaps between Beta and GA.

  2. Months 2 to 3: publish the GA architecture spec and the SLOs, agree on them with the CTO, and turn them into a roadmap the team can execute.

  3. Months 4 to 6: deliver the first GA milestones (one-click provisioning of a customer instance, observability coverage, safe upgrade path) with your two SREs.

  4. After month 6: drive continuous improvement of the platform, including a re-architecture of the first version of Kestra Cloud based on what Beta and the first GA customers taught us.

Perks & Benefits

  • Work from anywhere: We're a remote-first company, so you can work from wherever feels like home. Plus, you'll have access to coworking spaces worldwide if you ever need a change of scenery.

  • Health coverage: From medical support, dental, and vision, we've got you covered.

  • Home office setup on us: We'll provide all the equipment you need to work comfortably.

Our Hiring Process

jobs.excerpt: OverviewDecisionPoint seeks a Performance & Resilience Test Engineer to evaluate the scalability, stability, responsiveness, failover behavior, and recovery capabilities of mission-critical software supporting the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.
jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Performance & Resilience Test Engineer to evaluate the scalability, stability, responsiveness, failover behavior, and recovery capabilities of mission-critical software supporting the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This role develops regression, API, integration, load, stress, endurance, and resilience tests; creates realistic workload models; and produces reproducible evidence of system behavior under normal, peak, degraded, and recovery conditions.

The Performance & Resilience Test Engineer works with architects, software developers, API and integration engineers, infrastructure and cloud teams, database specialists, cybersecurity personnel, CI/CD engineers, operations teams, and Government stakeholders. The position identifies performance bottlenecks, validates failover and recovery procedures, and provides evidence-based recommendations supporting release readiness, capacity planning, and operational resilience.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Performance & Resilience Test Engineer will:

  • Develop and maintain performance, load, stress, spike, endurance, volume, scalability, failover, and recovery tests.
  • Build automated regression, API, and integration tests supporting repeatable performance and resilience validation.
  • Analyze mission workflows, usage patterns, transaction volumes, concurrency, data characteristics, interfaces, and operational objectives.
  • Develop workload models that represent normal operations, peak demand, surge conditions, degraded environments, and recovery scenarios.
  • Define test objectives, performance baselines, service thresholds, acceptance criteria, and measurable expected results.
  • Develop test plans, scenarios, scripts, data, configurations, and execution schedules.
  • Prepare representative test data for functional, high-volume, boundary, exception, failover, and recovery scenarios.
  • Maintain repeatable processes for test-data creation, setup, refresh, reset, reconciliation, and cleanup.
  • Execute tests in development, integration, test, staging, performance, or other Government-approved environments.
  • Automate test execution through approved CI/CD pipelines where appropriate.
  • Produce reproducible test results, logs, reports, metrics, graphs, and objective evidence.
  • Measure and analyze response time, throughput, latency, concurrency, error rates, resource utilization, saturation, queue depth, and transaction completion.
  • Establish performance baselines and compare results across builds, releases, configurations, environments, and infrastructure changes.
  • Identify application, database, interface, network, cloud, infrastructure, configuration, or external-service bottlenecks.
  • Correlate test results with application logs, infrastructure metrics, traces, events, and monitoring data.
  • Work with technical teams to isolate root causes and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
  • Validate failover behavior for applications, services, interfaces, databases, infrastructure components, and dependent capabilities.
  • Test approved recovery procedures and confirm that services return to an acceptable operational state.
  • Validate recovery sequencing, data consistency, transaction handling, dependency restoration, and post-recovery functionality.
  • Evaluate behavior during component failures, network interruptions, service degradation, capacity constraints, and dependency outages.
  • Verify that systems fail safely and provide appropriate errors, alerts, retries, timeouts, and recovery behavior.
  • Support disaster-recovery, continuity, restoration, and operational-readiness exercises where applicable.
  • Document performance defects, resilience gaps, capacity risks, recovery failures, and release impacts.
  • Support defect triage, root-cause analysis, correction verification, and targeted regression testing.
  • Coordinate with architects and engineering teams to evaluate scalability, capacity, extensibility, and recovery approaches.
  • Coordinate with CI/CD engineers to integrate repeatable performance checks, thresholds, reports, and quality gates.
  • Coordinate with operations teams to incorporate production observations and operational feedback into future testing.
  • Support Government demonstrations, user acceptance testing, release testing, and operational validation.
  • Provide performance and resilience results, residual risks, and release-readiness recommendations to technical and program stakeholders.
  • Maintain test source code, scripts, configurations, data, and documentation in approved version-control repositories.
  • Participate in sprint planning, backlog refinement, reviews, demonstrations, retrospectives, and release-readiness activities.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of performance engineering, workload modeling, observability, failover testing, and recovery validation.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Candidates must possess all the following:

  • An active Secret clearance or higher.
  • A bachelor’s degree in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent permitted by the applicable labor category.
  • At least six years of relevant professional experience.
  • Experience designing and executing load and performance tests.
  • Experience developing realistic workload models based on user behavior, transaction volumes, concurrency, or operational demand.
  • Experience analyzing performance results and identifying application, integration, database, infrastructure, or network bottlenecks.
  • Experience planning or executing failover tests.
  • Experience validating system, application, service, or data recovery.
  • Ability to build or maintain regression, API, integration, and automated test coverage.
  • Ability to prepare and maintain representative test data.
  • Ability to produce repeatable automated execution and reproducible test results.
  • Ability to define measurable performance baselines, thresholds, acceptance criteria, and expected results.
  • Ability to correlate test results with logs, metrics, traces, events, or other observability data.
  • Ability to document performance defects, resilience gaps, capacity risks, recovery failures, and release impacts.

jobs.title: Senior Biostatistician
jobs.excerpt: Senior Biostatistician All U. S.  Locations (remote); candidates must reside in the United States Position Scope: The Senior Biostatistician is PaceMate's first biostatistician.
jobs.description:
Senior Biostatistician
All U.S. Locations (remote); candidates must reside in the United States

Position Scope:
The Senior Biostatistician is PaceMate's first biostatistician. The role independently leads the statistical design, analysis, and reporting of PaceMate's clinical research, including internal quality and research studies and externally published work.
The role owns each study from analysis plan through peer-reviewed publication and response to reviewers, working directly with the Chief Medical Officer and PaceMate's clinical team. About a quarter to a third of the role applies the same methods to operational and business questions. Routine operational reporting and dashboards sit outside this role. AI-assisted tools are part of how this role works every day, and the role is accountable for validating every result they help produce. The position has latitude to shape its own workflow and a potential path to expanded oversight of research-related functions.

Essential Functions and Job Responsibilities:
  • Write and execute statistical analysis plans for retrospective and real-world evidence studies, including target trial emulation. Define estimands (ICH E9(R1)), cohorts, exposure windows, and outcomes with the Chief Medical Officer and clinical investigators.
  • Link and validate multi-table device data. Confirm denominators, person-time, and follow-up, and address left truncation and immortal time bias around device implant and remote monitoring enrollment.
  • Analyze count and rate outcomes (Poisson and negative binomial regression with person-time offsets), recurrent events (Andersen-Gill, PWP, and frailty models; mean cumulative function), time-to-event outcomes with competing risks (cause-specific hazards, Fine-Gray, Aalen-Johansen), and clustered data (mixed-effects models, GEE).
  • Control confounding with propensity score methods (IPTW, overlap weights, matching). Handle informative censoring with IPCW and missing data with multiple imputation. Test robustness with E-values, negative control outcomes, and tipping-point analyses.
  • Write and review methods and results sections for abstracts and peer-reviewed manuscripts to STROBE and RECORD standards. Respond to co-author and external advisor critique.
  • Respond to peer review: re-analyses, statistical sections of response letters, and defensible positions under methodological critique.
  • Evaluate operational and business changes using interrupted time series, segmented regression, difference-in-differences, and statistical process control. Present effect estimates with confidence intervals to leadership in plain language.
  • Use AI coding assistants (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT) daily to write, review, debug, and document R and SQL code and analysis reports. Validate all generated code and results before use, and use only PaceMate-approved tools with protected health information.
  • Provide statistical input and limited analyses to support quality improvement, patient safety monitoring, and clinical operations when needed. This is not a primary QA role.
  • Build reusable research infrastructure with the data science team: standardized cohort definitions, reusable R code, and templated outputs.
  • Maintain the analytic queue and the documentation that lets any published result be reproduced by script from the raw data extract.
  • Maintain high level understanding of PaceMate products and services.
  • Maintain appropriate levels of current knowledge and the ability to interpret, comprehend, and apply policies. Assist in ensuring consistency in practices and PaceMate Mission, Vision, and Customer Service standards are met. Adhere to the Code of Conduct and all Company Policies and Procedures.

Non-Essential Functions:
  • Infrequently, prepare IRB documentation, including determination requests and reliance materials.
  • When requested, evaluate predictive models for discrimination, calibration, and clinical usefulness (decision curve analysis), including temporal and external validation (TRIPOD+AI).

Qualifications: An individual must be able to perform each Essential Function of the job satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to enable individuals with disabilities, who are otherwise qualified, to perform the essential functions. Nothing within this job description restricts management’s right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

Education and Experience:
  • PhD in biostatistics, statistics, or epidemiology; or a Master's in one of these fields with at least 8 years applying statistics to health data with clear independent ownership of analyses.
  • Lead or methods statistician on peer-reviewed cardiovascular clinical research (electrophysiology, heart failure, cardiac devices, or closely related). General healthcare analytics experience alone is not sufficient.
  • Peer-reviewed publication track record as a contributing statistician, including successful responses to reviewer critique.
  • Command of the methods this data demands: linking many related tables; count and rate outcomes with exposure offsets; recurrent-event and time-to-event methods including competing risks; clustered and repeated-measures data; confounding control in observational data; non-random missingness and informative censoring.
  • High proficiency in R across the full pipeline, including R Markdown or Quarto.
  • SQL sufficient to query and join relational clinical tables.
  • Reproducible practice by default: Git, dependency management (e.g., renv), scripted pipelines, and literate reporting.
  • Ability to explain methods and limitations to physicians and to a manager who is not a statistician, and willingness to state clearly when the data cannot support a conclusion.
  • Current, regular use of AI coding assistants in analytical work, with a consistent method for checking their output and protecting patient data.
  • Interest in applying statistical methods to operational and business questions.

Preferred:
  • Research using CIED, electrophysiology, or remote monitoring data, especially transmission-level data.
  • Published work using target trial emulation.
  • Working knowledge of Python.

Preferred or Required Certifications
PStat or GStat a plus

Physical Requirements:
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee will be consistently required to remain in a stationary position working at a computer, constantly operate a computer and other office equipment, and frequently communicate with customers and employees via voice and video.•
  • Must be able to exchange accurate information, with the ability to effectively utilize voice over internet protocol; and repetitive motions using fingers and forearms in data entry.
Other Requirements:
  • Home office setup: Maintain a dedicated, separate office or room at home to ensure privacy and professional working conditions.
  • Connectivity: Maintain a reliable, high-speed internet connection at your residence.
  • Geographic restriction: Must reside and work exclusively within the contiguous United States.
  • Must legally be eligible to work in the United States.
  • Notification protocol: You must inform and receive approval from the IT department before working from any location other than the legal address PaceMate has on file. To update your address or request approval for a temporary work location, contact PaceMate IT or your HR representative. Additional information is available in the PaceMate official handbook.
  • Foreign transport of sensitive information: When confidential information is carried into a foreign country, it must be stored in an inaccessible form (e.g., encrypted external storage) or remain in the worker’s possession at all times. PaceMate workers may not take secret PaceMate information into another country without permission from Physical Security management.
  • May require limited travel based on the needs of the business.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement: We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and value diversity at our company. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

jobs.excerpt: Senior Backend Engineer - Credit Card PaymentsHybrid in London, United KingdomWe're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join the Payments Infrastructure team.
jobs.description:
Senior Backend Engineer - Credit Card Payments

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom

We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join the Payments Infrastructure team.

You’ll design and build the payments platform behind iwoca’s business credit card – the services that approve each payment, monitor transactions for fraud, and pay out cashback.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

iwoca launched its business credit card in 2026. It gives small businesses a fast, flexible way to pay for what they need and control their cash flow, alongside iwoca’s loans. The card is a core part of iwoca’s long-term growth.

The Payments infrastructure team builds iwoca’s card payments platform. Its job is to approve each payment in moments when a customer uses their card. The team also builds the platforms that pay out rewards as customers spend and monitor every transaction.

The team is small – a principal engineer, a product manager with a background in payments, and you. It works closely with iwoca’s ledger, fraud and customer product teams.

The role

As a senior backend engineer, you’ll own services and projects end to end, and shape the platform’s architecture with the principal engineer, from service boundaries to how authorisation, rewards, and transaction monitoring fit together. You’ll work closely with product to decide what the team builds and how. There’s still plenty to build, and you’ll take new services into production.

You’ll build on your payments expertise alongside the principal engineer, with scope to grow as the platform matures. Most of the challenge is technical: scaling payments within card scheme rules and the regulation iwoca has to meet. Your code will run every time a small business uses its iwoca card.

Live project examples:

  • Payment authorisation. Extending the service built to approve or decline each card payment in real time, using data held in other services. It places a hold on available credit in the ledger and applies iwoca's own checks, such as account status, merchant category code restrictions, and spend limits.

  • Transaction monitoring. Building the service that will screen card transactions for fraud and financial-crime risk as customers spend, so iwoca will rely less on third parties.

  • Rewards. Extending the service that pays out cashback, as the team adds to what the card offers.

  • Testing for failure. Designing sandbox tests that cover edge cases and failures across the card transaction lifecycle.

  • Ledger cutover and go-live. Moving the card platform onto iwoca's own ledger and infrastructure with as little downtime as possible, then fixing the issues that only show up in production.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Payment systems. You've designed and run highly available, low-latency payment systems in production, ideally on the issuing side.

  • Card payment flows. You've worked on card authorisation and clearing, and traced transactions from the terminal, through the acquirer and card scheme, to the issuer. You've used response codes to diagnose declined transactions.

  • Backend engineering. You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You've written and run backend services in it.

  • Distributed systems. You've built microservices, REST APIs, and asynchronous messaging with queues or topics, and designed the database schemas behind them, ideally in PostgreSQL.

  • AI leverage. You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone, at work or in your own projects. You judge when to use it and when not to, and you check its output before it reaches production.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

  • Ledgers and clearing. You've worked on a ledger, reconciliation, or clearing system – for cards, loyalty points, bank transfers, or money remittance.

  • Testing. You've written automated tests for payment systems, ideally test-first.

  • Python. You've used Python in production. It's the language the team works in.

The salary

We expect to pay from £100,000 to £120,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Useful links:

  • iwoca benefits & policies

  • Interview welcome pack

Compensation Range: £100K - £120K

The Role
Menlo builds open source and production AI systems, from the brain, to developer facing tools to the runtime infrastructure and humanoid platform underneath. This fellowship is deliberately open ended: tell us your strengths and we'll match you to high impact work across software engineering, systems, applied AI, or research. You'll be hands on from day one, with a Menlo engineer or researcher directly responsible for your mentorship and your results. You own deliverables at the same level as the team you join. We expect you to contribute, not observe.

This is a paid internship program that runs year round. Candidates go through a rigorous interview process and get matched with a senior researcher or engineer working on real world problems.

What You'll Do

  • Own a real project end to end, from problem definition through implementation, testing, and documentation.

  • Ship production grade work in one or more areas: product engineering, systems, infrastructure, applied AI, or research.

  • Work on core Menlo projects, including developer tooling, model runtime and performance, automation, and reliability improvements.

  • Debug real issues across codebases and environments, and propose fixes that improve correctness, performance, and maintainability.

  • Write clear docs, runbooks, or internal notes that make your work easy for the team to adopt.

  • Collaborate closely with engineers and researchers through code reviews and technical discussions.

What We Look For

  • University, high school or mid-career individuals looking for a crash course in physical AI and robotics

  • The ability to read unfamiliar codebases and make safe, well scoped changes.

  • Practical debugging skills: you can isolate problems and validate fixes.

  • A grasp of software or hardware engineering basics: testing, version control, and review.

  • A high ownership mindset and the ability to work independently with fast feedback loops.

  • Above all, we hire for slope: how fast you grow matters more than where you start.

Logistics

  • 3 months minimum, based in one of our offices: San Francisco, Ho Chi Minh City, or Singapore

  • Paid role.

  • Open to pre university and university students.

  • You'll need existing work authorization for your office location, as we don't provide visa sponsorship for this role.

Why Join Menlo
You'll do real work that ships, not busywork on the bench. Genuine ownership, direct mentorship from the people building Asimov, and a chance to prove yourself on hard problems alongside some of the most curious and driven people you'll meet. If you want your work to matter beyond a paper or a demo, this is the place.

A Note on AI

You don't need deep AI expertise for every role, but we do expect everyone at Menlo to be intellectually curious, drawn to tinkering and discovery, and excited to use AI as a real collaborator in their work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement. When that's the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don't treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on.

Equal Opportunity and Accommodations

jobs.title: Senior Security Engineer - Data Security (DLP & Information Protection)
jobs.excerpt: Role type & Location• Full time Remote (Work from home) based either Dublin or UK only • Occasional Travel to Dublin office if Ireland based (Glasnevin) or UK (Oxford) if UK based Visa• We regret we cannot offer Irish or UK visa sponsorship for this role About this RoleYou will be the engineer who protects sensitive data at Deciphex We work in clinical and research digital pathology, so the data includes patient health information, personal data and confidential business and customer data.
jobs.description:
Role type & Location

  • Full time Remote (Work from home) based either Dublin or UK only
  • Occasional Travel to Dublin office if Ireland based (Glasnevin) or UK (Oxford) if UK based

Visa

  • We regret we cannot offer Irish or UK visa sponsorship for this role

About this Role

You will be the engineer who protects sensitive data at Deciphex

We work in clinical and research digital pathology, so the data includes patient health information, personal data and confidential business and customer data.

You will report to the Principal Engineer - Cybersecurity & DevOps and join a lean, hands-on team where each engineer owns a defined area, with no large support structure.

In your first 12 months, three priorities come first:

  1. Data loss prevention and information protection on Google Workspace and Microsoft 365: classification, labelling and sharing controls, so sensitive data is shared only as intended.
  2. Least-privilege access to sensitive data: regular access reviews, and controlled, logged sharing with external providers and customers.
  3. Security review of the tools, integrations and data flows that touch sensitive data, including flows to on-premises laboratory systems, integrations and workflows, and the data side of our AWS-hosted products.

Our technology environment:

  • We are a Google Workspace company that also uses Microsoft services, and our products run on AWS.
  • You will work with the native data-protection and audit features of each platform: Google Workspace DLP, labels and context-aware access, Microsoft Purview and SharePoint, and AWS storage, encryption and logging services, alongside the security hubs of each platform.
  • We also use dedicated enterprise tools for endpoint protection and email security, and Vanta for compliance automation.

About our DTO Team

  • Our Digital Trust & Transformation Office (DTO) brings together the teams that keep Deciphex trustworthy and moving forward: information security, cybersecurity, application security, DevOps, IT, data protection and privacy, AI and AI governance, and operational resilience.
  • We work to one aim: our customers, clinicians and patients can trust our systems and the data in them, and our engineers can ship safely and quickly.

What You Will help us with

  • This is a hands-on engineering role in our Digital Trust & Transformation Office (DTO).
  • The Information Security team and Data Protection Officer own governance, risk and compliance, and rely on YOU as the data security specialist.
  • The Cybersecurity Engineer owns identity, endpoints and general security operations, and YOU work together on data incidents.

More specifically;

  • You will build and run the technical controls that keep it confidential wherever it lives: Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, our AWS-hosted products, other cloud and SaaS tools, or on-premises.
  • Design, deploy and tune data loss prevention and information-protection controls. Set retention, versioning and recovery settings so critical data survives ransomware and accidental deletion.
  • Enforce least privilege, run access reviews, fix oversharing, and control and log what leaves the company.
  • Keep sensitive data located through discovery and flow mapping. Set encryption and key-management requirements for cloud data stores and verify them. The DevOps team runs the keys and infrastructure encryption.
  • Carry out the technical security review of new tools, integrations and AI services before they touch sensitive data. The Information Security team, Data Protection Officer and AI governance decide on risk and approval.
  • Support the application security team on app data security, and collaborate with the product and data teams to lead good practice such as access models and logging. Those teams own product controls and anonymisation.
  • Monitor data access and movement in audit logs and security hubs
  • Lead the technical side of data incidents: scope, contain, preserve evidence and brief the Information Security team and DPO.
  • Support data subject and customer data requests. General security operations stay with the Cybersecurity Engineer.
  • Support the Information Security team with the technical side of ISO 27001, NHS DSPT, GDPR and customer assurance, providing data security expertise and automated evidence. They run the frameworks and audits.
  • Automate administration, investigation and reporting with Python, APIs and generative AI tooling.

What This Is Not

  • Not a paperwork or policy-only role. The controls must exist and be evidenced.
  • Not the application security lead. You support the application security team on app data security.
  • Not a general security-operations, identity-platform, endpoint or vulnerability-management role. Those sit with the Cybersecurity Engineer. Your incident work is about data.
  • Not a privacy-engineering or anonymisation role. Those sit with the data and product teams.
  • Not a legal or compliance role. The Information Security team and Data Protection Officer own governance.

Experience You Bring

  • 5/6+ years of hands-on security engineering, including ownership of security controls in production.
  • Hands-on DLP or information-protection experience in Google Workspace: sharing and external-access controls, labels and rules, and context-aware access.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 data security: Purview, SharePoint sharing and permissions, and how Entra ID access applies to data.
  • Strong access-control fundamentals across SaaS and cloud (Google Workspace, Entra ID, AWS), including how data is stored and encrypted.
  • Python scripting and API automation, and practical experience using generative AI tooling to work faster and more reliably.
  • Able to investigate data access and movement using audit logs, a SIEM, a security hub or native platform tools.
  • Able to work with product, engineering, research, clinical, privacy and information-security colleagues, and explain both the risk and the practical control.
  • Experience with health or other regulated data helps. We will teach you our regulatory and clinical context, so you need to arrive knowing how to protect data with working controls.

What Success Looks Like

  • We know where our sensitive data is, who can reach it and how it moves.
  • Sensitive data is shared only as intended, access is reviewed regularly, and external sharing is controlled and logged.
  • New tools and integrations are security-reviewed before they touch sensitive data, without slowing delivery.
  • Data incidents are scoped quickly and accurately, and audit evidence is automated and current.

What are the benefits of working with Deciphex?

  • 💰 Salary with performance-based annual increases to recognise your contribution.
  • 🩺 Healthcare benefits to support your wellbeing.
  • 🌴 Annual leave plus additional Christmas leave to rest and recharge.
  • 🔬 Meaningful work that helps improve patient outcomes.
  • 🚀 A growing company where you can make your mark.
  • 💡 Varied, challenging projects to keep you learning.
  • 📈 Regular feedback and career opportunities to help you progress.
  • 🤝 A supportive, multicultural team to share ideas and learn from.

About Deciphex

Through the work that we do, the team at Deciphex helps pharma to accelerate the process of essential drug development and helps cancer patients get a timely and accurate diagnosis.

Founded in Dublin (Ireland) in 2017, Deciphex has scaled rapidly to a team of over 230 people and counting who are providing software solutions to address the pathology gap in research pathology and clinical areas. We have offices in Dublin, Exeter, Oxford, Chicago and Toronto, and are expanding our team throughout the world.

We are software developers, clinical specialists, artificial intelligence engineers, operations professionals and so much more, all working as one team to support our customers and patients.

Read more about Deciphex here and more about our team on our Careers Page here.

Deciphex is an equal opportunities employer and we are committed to the principle of equality. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to age, race, religious beliefs, political views, gender identity, affectional or sexual orientation, national origin, family or marital status (including pregnancy), disability, membership of the travelling community or any other classification protected by applicable law.

jobs.description:
Looking for an opportunity to make an impact?

Leidos is a Fortune 500® company with nearly $18B in sales and 50,000 employees that brings over 70 years of experience in support of both investor-owned and municipal utility growth goals. Leidos Energy helps utilities address complex challenges through comprehensive, performance-based solutions delivered across the full project lifecycle. Our capabilities include engineering, planning, project management, construction management, and commissioning services for electric power substations, transmission and distribution systems, protection and controls design, and electrification programs. Utilities nationwide rely on Leidos for trusted power industry expertise, demonstrated by our work with more than 75 investor-owned utilities and over 100 municipal and cooperative utilities, as well as a growing portfolio of private developer clients.

Your greatest work is ahead!

Leidos Energy is seeking a Power Consultant Senior Project Manager - Transaction Services to play an important part in transactions, giving you an opportunity to contribute to the transformation of the energy industry. Older, inefficient power generation and transmission systems are being upgraded and replaced with modern, environmentally friendly alternatives. You will be an integral part of an exceptional team of power industry experts, providing consulting services and work products that our clients view as critical inputs to their business decisions. We evaluate a wide variety of technologies, from wind turbines and solar panels to battery storage systems, fuel cells, and advanced fuel conversion technologies.

We provide expertise, guidance, and consultation to our clients, and our work is centered on supporting financial transactions - the development, financing, acquisition and sale of generation (and non-generation) hard assets. We identify technical and commercial risks and help our clients to find and/or evaluate solutions to their challenges. Because we are exposed to numerous unique projects over short periods of time, we (i) are diversified in technologies and commercial approaches to project execution; (ii) contribute to and learn how problems are solved by industry leaders and how those solutions drive financial viability; and (iii) benefit from this knowledge as a team and as individuals, resulting in a professional experience that evolves, is dynamic, and is well-rounded.

Location: Fully remote will be considered based on candidate experience and qualifications. Candidates within commuting distance of Denver, CO, or Framingham, MA is a plus.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Collaborate regularly with project developers, utilities, equipment manufacturers, engineering firms, investors, bankers, and legal and financial advisors.
  • Determine, monitor, and review all project economics including costs, operational budgets, staffing requirements, sub-contractors, resources, and risk.
  • Plan, schedule, monitor, and report on activities related to the project.
  • Lead the project teams based on client requirements and objectives.
  • Facilitate status review meetings among project team members and clients.
  • Work with senior management on project proposals, bids, contracts, estimates, and schedules.
  • Manage project requirements, scope, and change issues.

jobs.title: Growth Strategist
jobs.excerpt: GROWTH STRATEGISTAt Fresh Prints, we work with thousands of customers, but not every customer should have the same experience with us.
jobs.description:
GROWTH STRATEGIST

At Fresh Prints, we work with thousands of customers, but not every customer should have the same experience with us.

Some might be ordering for the first time. Others have been buying from us for years. Some need an occasional reminder or a well-timed offer, while others represent significant opportunities that deserve a much more personalized approach.

Today, we reach these customers through emails, SMS, automated journeys, promotional campaigns, gifting programs, and direct outreach. We've built much of the infrastructure to make these things possible, but there's a much bigger opportunity ahead of us: bringing all of these touchpoints together into a thoughtful, cohesive strategy for how we grow our customer relationships.

That's what we're hiring a Growth Strategist to do.

Your job is to understand our customers, figure out what they need at different stages of their relationship with Fresh Prints, and build experiences that make them want to engage, purchase, return, and grow with us.

For some customers, that might mean a great email at exactly the right moment. For others, it might mean an entirely different experience, with personalized outreach, exclusive offers, samples, or programs designed around their long-term potential.

We don't want someone who thinks about growth as a collection of campaigns or channels. We want someone who can see the bigger picture, identify where the opportunities are, and turn those opportunities into programs that drive meaningful business results.

This isn't a role where you inherit a finished playbook. You'll have the freedom, and responsibility, to question how we do things today, build better systems, and shape what customer growth looks like at Fresh Prints.

This role is about:

  • Understanding our customers deeply: Who they are, what they care about, why they buy, what brings them back, and what makes them disengage.
  • Designing the right experience for different customers: Knowing when automation and great content are enough, and when a relationship deserves a more personalized, high-touch approach.
  • Finding opportunities to grow customer value: Identifying where we're losing customers, leaving revenue on the table, or missing opportunities to build stronger relationships.
  • Being a great marketer: Understanding what makes someone open an email, click a link, respond to an offer, or take the next step, and being able to create that experience yourself.
  • Turning ideas into execution: Building programs, writing compelling content, coordinating teams, testing approaches, and taking ownership of the results.
  • Building systems that scale: Using data, technology, AI, and automation to create experiences that become smarter and more effective over time.

What You'll Own

Understanding Customers & Finding Growth Opportunities

  • Develop a deep understanding of Fresh Prints' customers, their buying behavior, motivations, needs, and decision-making journeys.
  • Use customer insights, data, and commercial judgment to identify the biggest opportunities to improve engagement, conversion, repeat purchases, retention, and customer value.
  • Build meaningful customer segments based on behavior, lifecycle stage, value, and growth potential, rather than treating everyone on our list the same way.
  • Identify where different customers need different experiences, and determine where we should invest more time, effort, and resources.
  • Continuously question our existing approach and develop new ideas that could materially change how customers engage and grow with Fresh Prints.

Building Experiences That Drive Growth

  • Own how Fresh Prints engages with customers throughout their relationship with us, from their first interaction to becoming loyal, repeat customers.
  • Develop thoughtful customer journeys that bring together content, communication, offers, personalization, and outreach to move customers toward the next meaningful action.
  • Own the strategy, messaging, and execution of customer communications across email, SMS, automated journeys, and promotional programs.
  • Build experiences around key customer moments, including onboarding, first purchases, post-purchase engagement, repeat purchases, reactivation, and win-back.
  • Develop more personalized approaches for our highest-value customers, including targeted campaigns, gifting, exclusive programs, and coordinated outreach with account-facing teams.
  • Create compelling content that customers actually want to engage with, from subject lines and SMS messages to promotional concepts and personalized pitches.
  • Work closely with Brand and Creative to make sure everything we put in front of customers feels relevant, engaging, and distinctly Fresh Prints.

Turning Strategy Into Results

  • Take ideas from insight to execution. You'll be expected to develop the strategy, build the plan, and make sure it actually happens.
  • Own performance across the experiences and programs you build, using engagement, conversion, retention, repeat purchase behavior, revenue, and customer value to measure success.
  • Develop a disciplined approach to experimentation, constantly testing messaging, offers, timing, audience selection, and customer experiences.
  • Look beyond surface-level metrics to understand what's actually driving performance and what needs to change.
  • Use our marketing technology, customer data, automation platforms, and AI tools to build and improve programs efficiently.
  • Maintain strong execution standards across customer communications, including segmentation accuracy, deliverability, list health, testing, and quality control.
  • Build processes, playbooks, and systems that allow successful programs to scale without requiring constant manual intervention.

Making Growth a Company-Wide Effort

  • Work closely with Sales, Marketing, Creative, Data, Tech, and Operations to turn customer insights and growth opportunities into coordinated action.
  • Influence how different teams engage with customers when changes are needed to improve retention, expansion, or the overall customer experience.
  • Bring a clear point of view on where we should focus, what we should test, and what we should stop doing.
  • Make the business case for new initiatives, align stakeholders, and drive execution even when the people involved don't report to you.
  • Help build a more connected approach to customer growth, where every interaction contributes to a stronger long-term relationship.

Who You Are

  • You're a marketer first. You understand people, what motivates them, and how to turn that understanding into messaging and experiences that drive action. You can write a great subject line as comfortably as you can design a customer growth strategy.
  • You think in customer journeys, not marketing channels. You don't see email, SMS, or account-based programs as separate worlds. You see different ways to engage different customers based on what they need and what they're worth to the business.
  • You're commercially minded. You understand that engagement is a means to an end. You're constantly thinking about how your work influences purchases, retention, revenue, and long-term customer value.
  • You're both strategic and hands-on. You enjoy figuring out the big picture, but you're equally comfortable rolling up your sleeves to write the copy, build a journey, launch a test, or troubleshoot a problem.
  • You're curious about customers. You don't assume you know what people want. You ask questions, study behavior, challenge assumptions, and use what you learn to build better experiences.
  • You think in systems. Rather than solving the same problem every month with another campaign, you look for ways to build something that will keep working and improving.
  • You have strong ownership. You don't need someone else to constantly set priorities or check the quality of your work. You hold yourself accountable for both the thinking and the execution.
  • You're comfortable with ambiguity. You don't need a detailed playbook to get started. You can take an unclear opportunity, develop a strong point of view, and create a path forward.
  • You know how to bring people along. You can challenge ideas, communicate clearly, and work across teams to get things done without relying on formal authority.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in growth marketing, lifecycle marketing, CRM, retention, customer growth, or a related role.
  • Demonstrated experience owning marketing initiatives end-to-end, from identifying opportunities and developing strategy to execution and performance analysis.
  • Strong marketing instincts and writing ability, with experience creating messaging, campaigns, or customer experiences that drive measurable action.
  • Experience working with customer segmentation, behavioral data, and lifecycle journeys.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort using data to understand customer behavior, evaluate performance, and make decisions.
  • Experience improving conversion, customer engagement, repeat purchases, retention, or revenue through marketing initiatives.
  • Ability to work cross-functionally and independently drive projects from concept to completion.
  • Experience with SMS, account-based marketing, loyalty programs, or high-value customer engagement is a plus.
  • Experience in B2C, DTC, e-commerce, or businesses with repeat-purchase behavior is strongly preferred.

Above all, we're looking for someone who combines great marketing instincts with strong strategic thinking and the ability to execute. Someone who can look at how we engage with customers today, see what we could be doing better, and take ownership of making it happen.

Details and other benefits

  • Work From Home / Remote
  • Competitive annual salary
  • Learning opportunities
  • Working in a great culture
  • At Fresh Prints, we deeply value the long-term contributions of our team. To recognize and celebrate that commitment, we offer a 2-month paid Sabbatical to eligible employees

Fresh Prints is an equal employment opportunity employer and promotes diversity, actively encouraging people of all backgrounds, ages, LGBTQ+, and those with disabilities to apply.

You own the go-to-market strategy — defining who to target, with what message, through what channels — and you lead that thinking in close partnership with product, engineering, sales, support, and marketing teams.   • Lead go-to-market strategy, defining target audiences, the messages that resonate with each, and how we reach them — building programs that find customers and help them find us
  • Partner with Product Owners to shape go-to-market plans for new products and releases, ensuring market and buyer perspectives are embedded in how we develop, launch, and evolve the portfolio

About You

  • Ability to develop strategic relationships and sell the vision; ability to influence at multiple levels of an organization

  • Intellectual curiosity and the ability to deliver business insight
  • Ideally, a strong public speaker, comfortable in front of large, senior groups, and a solid writer
  • Demonstrated ability to build strong cross-functional relationships and lead effectively in a fluid, customer-oriented environment; able to manage competing priorities and drive to results across diverse teams and stakeholders
  • Comfortable leveraging AI tools to accelerate research, content development, and analysis — using technology to work smarter and deliver higher-quality output faster

Celebrating Difference

At Imagine Communications, we don’t just accept difference — we celebrate it, we support it, and we thrive on it for the benefit of our customers, our employees, our products, and our communities. We are committed to providing an environment of mutual respect. Imagine Communications is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer.

jobs.description:
JOB ROLE: Business Development Manager – New Client Acquisition

LOCATION: Remote

HOURS: Monday - Friday 8am-5pm (UK hours)

SALARY: 20,000 ZAR per month + Bonus based on performance

About the role

Optimal delivers property maintenance and refurbishment services. We’re looking for a proactive, commercially driven salesperson whose sole focus is winning new business clients.

Your job is to identify suitable businesses, reach decision-makers, understand their property requirements and demonstrate why Optimal is the right partner for them. You’ll build your own pipeline, generate qualified opportunities and turn prospects into clients with the potential for regular, repeat work.

You’ll own the sales process from first contact through to securing the client and supporting their first confirmed opportunity. You’ll then provide a clear handover to our Client Project Management team, who will take responsibility for ongoing account management and delivery.

We’re building our own system with AI and automations to reduce administration and improve productivity. We want someone who already uses tools such as ChatGPT and is constantly looking for ways to research better, improve outreach and win more business.

Key responsibilities

Find and engage new prospects

  • Identify businesses with ongoing property maintenance and refurbishment requirements.
  • Build targeted prospect lists, focusing on organisations where Optimal can win profitable, repeat work.
  • Identify decision-makers and understand how they appoint and assess maintenance contractors.
  • Generate opportunities through outbound calls, email, LinkedIn, referrals and networking.
  • Take ownership of your prospecting activity and consistently create new sales conversations.

Turn conversations into opportunities

  • Understand each prospect’s property portfolio, service requirements and frustrations with existing arrangements.
  • Ask effective questions to establish business potential, decision-making authority, buying process and timing.
  • Explain clearly how Optimal can meet their needs and address their concerns.
  • Secure meetings, introductions, quote opportunities and access to relevant supplier onboarding processes.
  • Maintain consistent follow-up and move prospects towards a clear next step.

Win new business clients

  • Own the new business sales process from initial approach through to agreement and activation.
  • Work with the quoting and operational teams to develop credible proposals and competitive offers.
  • Present proposals confidently, handle objections and negotiate within agreed commercial guidelines.
  • Secure the first confirmed work and establish a clear opportunity for an ongoing relationship.
  • Focus on clients whose needs fit Optimal’s capabilities and offer sustainable commercial value.
  • Make accurate commitments on pricing, service and delivery, with internal agreement where needed.

Deliver a clear client handover

  • Coordinate a smooth introduction to the Client Project Management team once the client is won.
  • Record the client’s requirements, key contacts, agreed terms, commitments and immediate opportunities.
  • Ensure the client understands who will manage their work and how to request services.
  • Support the initial transition so the relationship starts well, then return your focus to winning the next client.

Manage your pipeline and performance

  • Keep prospect records, sales stages, next actions and expected outcomes accurate in our system.
  • Maintain a healthy pipeline and provide realistic forecasts.
  • Track which sectors, messages and outreach methods produce the strongest results.
  • Participate in daily stand-ups and regular sales reviews.
  • Take responsibility for meeting agreed activity, conversion and new business targets.

Use AI to sell more effectively

  • Use ChatGPT and other approved AI tools to support prospect research, meeting preparation, outreach drafting and follow-up.
  • Personalise communications and check facts before contacting prospects.
  • Use our developing system and automations to improve consistency and reduce repetitive administration.
  • Keep learning about new AI capabilities and share practical ideas that improve sales performance.
  • Handle prospect and company information responsibly.

What success looks like

Your primary measure of success is new business clients won and the profitable work they generate.

We’ll also measure:

  • Qualified new business opportunities created.
  • Meetings held with relevant decision-makers.
  • Conversion from prospect to first confirmed job.
  • New client revenue and gross profit against agreed targets.
  • Sales cycle length and pipeline quality.
  • The accuracy and completeness of client handovers.
  • Activity targets support these outcomes. We want someone who turns outreach into commercial results.

Requirements

  • A proven track record in outbound B2B sales and winning new business clients.
  • Evidence that you can generate your own pipeline and close opportunities.
  • Confidence making cold calls, reaching decision-makers and asking for business.
  • Strong questioning, listening, presentation and negotiation skills.
  • Persistence and discipline with follow-up, combined with sound judgement about where to focus your time.
  • Commercial awareness and an understanding of the difference between winning revenue and winning profitable business.
  • Experience in property maintenance, refurbishment, facilities management, construction or a related service sector.
  • Enough trade knowledge to hold credible conversations, recognise opportunities and involve technical colleagues when needed.
  • Hands-on experience using ChatGPT or similar AI tools to improve productivity.
  • A commitment to continually developing your sales skills, trade knowledge and use of AI.
  • Confidence using CRM systems, Microsoft Office and digital prospecting tools.
  • Strong written and spoken communication and the ability to work independently against clear targets.
  • Experience selling to property managers, managing agents, landlords, facilities teams or businesses with multiple sites is an advantage.

Additional requirement for remote working, you must have:

  • Your own well-specified computer: A reliable, modern computer capable of running multiple business applications, AI tools and video calls smoothly.
  • Two screens: A dual-screen setup for efficient prospecting, research and client communication.
  • A good-quality camera: A clear, professional webcam for client and team meetings.
  • A good-quality headset: Headphones with a clear microphone suitable for frequent sales calls.
  • Fast, reliable internet: A stable connection that supports uninterrupted calls and cloud-based systems.
  • A suitable home office: A dedicated, quiet and professional workspace where you can make sales calls without interruptions.
  • Availability aligned with UK operations: The ability to work agreed hours that suit UK prospects and colleagues.
  • You must be comfortable maintaining a consistent outbound sales routine, staying accessible and taking ownership of your results.

Benefits

  • A role with a clear focus on winning new business.
  • Support from quoting and delivery colleagues to help turn opportunities into successful client relationships.
  • The opportunity to contribute to a business developing its own system with AI and automations.
  • A collaborative, commercially focused environment where your results are visible.
  • Opportunities to develop as the business grows.
