jobs.title: Global Value and Access Senior Manager - Rare Disease
jobs.excerpt: Career CategoryValue and AccessJob DescriptionJoin Amgen’s Mission of Serving PatientsAt Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are.
jobs.description:
Career Category

Value and Access

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.


Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.


Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


Global Value and Access Senior Manager - Rare Disease


What you will do

The Sr. Manager will support an innovative treatment approved for three distinct rare-disease indications and which is entering a period of global growth. Reimbursement expansion across more than 27 markets through 2026–2027, often across multiple indications at the same time, creates a dynamic and unprecedented launch environment requiring high-quality access materials and close partnership with local teams.


The treatment franchise has a large sales ambition and a growing pipeline of more than six potential indication expansions across different disease areas, and additional proof-of-concept opportunities. This scale offers the chance to contribute to a high-visibility brand undergoing international expansion and to build experience across a broad range of Patient Impact Expansions (PIEs). Each disease under investigation represents an opportunity to serve patients living with a severe, rare condition.


Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role, you will be part of the Global Integrated Access Strategy organization, reporting to the Access Strategy Lead (ASL) for the innovative treatment within the Rare Disease therapeutic area. You will support access strategy and launch execution across the innovative treatment’s approved indications and evolving pipeline.


  • As Senior Manager, you will become the subject matter expert for a selection of indications in launch phase and potential indication expansion opportunities. You will lead indication-specific Value, Access and Pricing assessments and serve as the Global Access strategy point of contact within indication-specific global cross-functional working groups.
  • For your assigned indications, you will assess payer needs, competitor pricing, and evolving policies across the US and priority ELMAC markets. You will translate their implications into clear, actionable recommendations for the innovative treatment’s Value & Access strategy.
  • You will partner with global colleagues in Marketing, Health Economics, Medical, Clinical Development, Regulatory, Operational Pricing, Forecasting and Advocacy, as well as country and regional access teams. Your contribution will help shape evidence needs and country access plans and will inform the clinical development plan, early Target Product Profile, launch strategy and forecasts. You will also contribute to key global materials, including the Global Brand Plan and forecasting guidance.
  • You will lead payer research execution in partnership with Global Insights teams and manage external vendor work as needed, ensuring that research questions, methods and deliverables generate clear insights for access and pricing decisions. You will create high-quality Global Value & Access materials, such as early value stories and objection handlers.
  • As a key member of the Global Access Team, you will regularly present your work, help organize team meetings, and support Access Best Practice Sharing sessions and other calls with local access teams.
  • This role is ideal for someone who takes ownership, thrives on overcoming challenges, and is eager to grow in a high-visibility global position. You will collaborate closely with the ASL while independently leading assigned workstreams from strategy through execution, with meaningful exposure to senior stakeholders and markets.

What We Expect of You

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The collaborative, curious and self-directed professional we seek has these qualifications.


Basic Qualifications:

Doctorate degree and 2 years of payer, market access and/or analytics experience

OR

Master’s degree and 6 years of of payer, market access and/or analytics experience

OR

Bachelor’s degree and 8 years of of payer, market access and/or analytics experience

OR

Associate’s degree and 10 years of of payer, market access and/or analytics experience

OR

High school diploma / GED and 12 years of payer, market access and/or analytics experience

In addition to meeting at least one of the above requirements, you must have a minimum of 2 years experience directly managing people and/or leadership experience leading teams, projects, programs, or directing the allocation or resources. Your managerial experience may run concurrently with the required technical experience referenced above


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Direct market access, health economics or pricing experience, with a strong understanding of the US and global payer environment.
  • Experience developing value, access and pricing assessments and materials for specialty or rare-disease medicines for top markets
  • Ability to assess payer needs, market dynamics, and competitors and translate into clear insights and recommendations
  • Ability to interpret clinical and health economic evidence, identify evidence gaps, and shape value propositions and payer research
  • Experience working in cross-functional teams and partnering effectively with Medical, Health Economics, Marketing, Regulatory, and country access teams
  • Experience conducting payer research and managing external vendors
  • Strong communication, collaboration and relationship-building skills
  • A proactive and curious mindset, with the ability to work autonomously, prioritize effectively, navigate ambiguity and deliver high-quality results

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

  • A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts
  • A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan
  • Stock-based long-term incentives
  • Award-winning time-off plans
  • Flexible work models where possible. Refer to the Work Location Type in the job posting to see if this applies.

Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team.

careers.amgen.com

In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.


Application deadline

Amgen does not have an application deadline for this position; we will continue accepting applications until we receive a sufficient number or select a candidate for the position.

Sponsorship

Sponsorship for this role is not guaranteed.

As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease.

jobs.description:
About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, assessible and safe.

We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it's the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit builds technology products used by millions of users across Southeast Asia. As our products and systems scale, we need technical leaders who can solve difficult engineering problems and raise the engineering bar around them.

The Principal Software Engineer owns technical direction and execution for major products and systems. This is a hands-on role - you will design systems, write code, and drive critical engineering work from idea to production.

What You'll Own

  • Owning technical design and execution for major products, systems and engineering initiatives.

  • Designing scalable, reliable systems across backend, frontend, APIs, databases and infrastructure.

  • Building alongside the team through coding, prototyping, code reviews, debugging and production problem-solving.

  • Driving architecture decisions and trade-offs across speed, scalability, reliability, cost and maintainability.

  • Turning ambiguous product problems into clear technical solutions and execution plans.

  • Raising engineering quality through stronger system design, testing, security, observability and development practices.

  • Leading technically critical initiatives and mentoring engineers across teams.

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems.

  • Deep expertise in backend, frontend, distributed systems, APIs, databases or cloud infrastructure.

  • Strong system design and architecture skills for complex or high-scale systems.

  • Strong coding ability and willingness to remain hands-on.

  • Track record of technically leading major engineering projects from design through production.

  • Ability to make sound technical trade-offs, influence engineers and solve complex production problems.

Nice to have

  • Experience scaling engineering teams, systems or development practices through significant growth.

  • Experience operating across multiple products, markets or countries.

Location

This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our local office at least 3 days per week, with the remaining days offering flexibility to work remotely.

Candidates should be based in, or able to work from, the location where the role is advertised.

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

Interview Process

Our process is designed to move fast:

  1. Online assessment or practical task

  2. Technical interview

  3. CEO / final round

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

  • 4+ years of experience in a Systems role.

Qualifications We Prefer:

  • Industry Experience of Software Lifecycle Development (Design, Requirements, Integration, Test)

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Pricing
jobs.excerpt: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe.
jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

You will join a collaborative team of data scientists, analysts, engineers, product managers and designers who build innovative products for Airbnb guests and hosts. Your core team will consist of data scientists within the Guest & Host Data Science organization, who develop models, measurement frameworks, foundational data products, and intelligence to improve and shape Airbnb marketplace and product.

The Difference You Will Make:

Under this general application, you will be considered for applications over several tracks.

  • Pricing Data Science - Responsible for developing a pricing guidance system for hosts, as well as methods (experimental and observational) to measure the impact of pricing feature launches.
  • Guest and Host Product Data Science - Responsible for building optimized products, tools, and programs that empower our hosts to thrive on our platform and our guests to easily discover and book stays that match their needs.
  • Marketplace Data Science - Responsible for building data products, inference frameworks, and intelligence to enable the growth of our marketplace.

As a data scientist on the team, you will directly impact the Airbnb user community and marketplace with the data products and insights you deliver. Your work may range from building models to understand the impact of supply and demand on marketplace outcomes, to applying causal inference methods to measure the impact of a new pricing guidance tool, to generating destination recommendations based on our understanding of guest travel preferences.

A Typical Day:

  • Building strong relationships with cross-functional partners across Product, Design, Engineering, and Analytics to drive collaboration and innovation.
  • Contribute directly to the development and launch of data-driven products and models, leveraging AI tools to enhance efficiency and impact.
  • Writing software in Python, SQL, or R to model, simulate, and measure the impact of new features, applying advanced causal inference techniques where necessary.
  • Analyzing structured or unstructured data to uncover meaningful insights and craft actionable proposals that help shape strategy.
  • Communicating learnings to leaders and stakeholders in a clear, compelling manner that drives informed data-driven decision making.

Your Expertise:

  • 5+ years of experience with BS/masters degree, 2+ years of experience with PhD.
  • Experience with experimentation, causal observational analysis, and machine learning techniques.
  • Experience partnering with product, engineering, and design to enable data-driven model or product development.
  • Ability to prototype, build, and scale derived data assets.
  • Strong coding skills in SQL and either Python or R.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills - an ability to communicate complex technical concepts to a non-technical audience.
  • Work authorization (if applicable)
  • Travel requirements (if applicable)

Your Location:

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. While the position is Remote Eligible, you must live in a state where Airbnb, Inc. has a registered entity. Click here for the up-to-date list of excluded states. This list is continuously evolving, so please check back with us if the state you live in is on the exclusion list. If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from.

Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging:

Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: . Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process.

We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

Equal Employment Opportunity:

Airbnb values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Airbnb are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, gender, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic.

How We'll Take Care of You:

Our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay is dependent upon many factors, such as: training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs and market demands. The base pay range is subject to change and may be modified in the future. This role may also be eligible for bonus, equity, benefits, and Employee Travel Credits.

Pay Range
$179,000—$210,000 USD

Reasonable Accommodations: We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process for applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.

A Note on Recruiting Scams: Scammers sometimes pose as Airbnb recruiters to get money or personal information from candidates. A few things that will always be true for Airbnb’s hiring process: our open roles are posted on Airbnb’s Career’s Page at careers.airbnb.com, and our recruiters correspond only from @ or @ email addresses. Our recruiters will never ask for your Social Security number, bank account details, passport, or payment app information while you are interviewing. We’ll also never ask you to pay a fee, send money, deposit or cash a check, or purchase work-related equipment (such as a company laptop) during the interview process. We encourage candidates to remain vigilant of these recruiting scams and not share sensitive information if you do not believe an individual is actually affiliated with Airbnb.

Fender Musical Instruments Corporation is a world famous brand with offices across the globe. Within Fender Musical Instruments Corporation’s ("FMIC") Americas Sales team, we work directly with our dealer network to build strong business relationships and deliver a best-in-class experience throughout the dealer lifecycle.

An American icon, Fender was born in Southern California and has built a worldwide influence extending beyond the studio and the stage. A Fender is more than an instrument, it’s a cultural symbol that resonates globally.

We are searching for a Business Development Manager based remotely within an assigned territory. This territory-aligned commercial leadership role owns sales strategy, budget, and performance across the full FMIC brand portfolio: Fender, Squier, Jackson, Charvel, EVH, Gretsch, and Bigsby. You will partner with aligned Dealer Experience Representatives to build trusted dealer relationships while retaining ultimate accountability for territory results. This role reports to the Manager, Regional Sales.

The ideal candidate will be located in either the Atlanta, GA or northern FL area.

Essential Functions:

  • Own and achieve monthly, quarterly, and annual sales targets and budget for the assigned territory across the full FMIC brand portfolio.
  • Develop and execute territory strategy and account plans that grow revenue, expand distribution, and strengthen FMIC’s position.
  • Manage the dealer order book for core products and new product introductions, balancing assortment, sell-in, and sell-through.
  • Make data-driven sales decisions, forecast demand, and manage dealer inventory and credit health in partnership with Finance and Credit.
  • Build and grow long-term dealer relationships as the strategic commercial contact, through regular in-person visits and phone, video, and electronic communication.
  • Partner with aligned Dealer Experience Representatives, providing direction and account context and acting on the insights, opportunities, and risks they surface.
  • Drive dealer marketing and program adoption, and support in-store events, demos, clinics, trade shows, and regional events.
  • Collaborate with Sales Operations, Finance, Credit, Supply Chain, Product, and Marketing to deliver seamless order processing, fulfillment, and dealer program execution.
  • Maintain accurate, timely CRM records of accounts, plans, pipeline, and opportunities.
  • Attend required sales meetings, territory reviews, product training, conferences, and industry events, continuously building product and brand expertise.
  • Additional duties as assigned

Qualifications:

  • 3–5 years of sales and territory management experience with a record of achieving sales targets; music industry or musical-instrument experience is a strong asset.
  • Excellent sales, prospecting, and negotiation skills.
  • Knowledge of finance, inventory management, credit, and forecasting, with strong analytical skills to make data-based recommendations.

jobs.description:
D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) is a leader in the development and delivery of quantum computing systems, software, and services. It is the world’s first commercial supplier of quantum computers, and the first and only to offer dual-platform quantum computing products and services, spanning both annealing and gate-model quantum computing technologies. D-Wave’s mission is to help customers realize the value of quantum today through enterprise-grade systems available on-premises and via its Leap™ quantum cloud service, which offers 99.9% availability and uptime. More than 100 organizations across commercial, government, and research sectors trust D-Wave to address complex computational challenges using quantum computing. Learn more about realizing the value of quantum computing today and how D-Wave is shaping the quantum-driven industrial and societal advancements of tomorrow: .

About the role

D-Wave is seeking a Senior FPGA Engineer to join our Quantum Systems and Technologies team. In this role, you will design and implement the signal processing and real-time control systems that connect our quantum computing hardware with the software that operates it.

We are looking for an innovative problem solver who is eager to take on challenging FPGA problems, take initiative, and contribute as a productive member of a small, collaborative team. You will have the opportunity to help shape our quantum processor control systems, contributing to highly visible, impactful projects that advance the future of quantum computing.

What you'll do

  • Design, implement, and verify SystemVerilog modules for low-latency, high-bandwidth signal processing chains that support quantum processor control
  • Develop FPGA-based real-time control and signal processing systems on AMD Xilinx Ultrascale+ platforms
  • Contribute to architecture discussions and decisions, collaborating upstream with quantum compiler engineers and downstream with RF hardware designers
  • Develop embedded software and Linux device drivers, including work with the Xilinx Pynq framework, to interface FPGA hardware with control software
  • Write clean, well-documented code, and participate in code reviews to ensure code quality and maintainability
  • Manage a complex toolchain and test/verification environment
  • Troubleshoot and debug issues, identify bottlenecks, and develop unit tests to ensure system reliability
  • Collaborate with software engineers, scientists, and hardware engineers to design and implement working solutions

About You

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field; Master's degree preferred
  • 5+ years of FPGA development experience with Verilog/SystemVerilog for synthesis and simulation
  • Experience with Python, with a focus on performance in embedded systems
  • Experience with Embedded C programming, with a focus on performant code
  • Experience with AMD Xilinx SoC platforms (e.g., Ultrascale+) and mixed-signal processing
  • Experience with system-level design, the Xilinx Pynq framework, and Pynq device driver development
  • Strong Linux skills, including system programming, device driver development, bash scripting, and configuration management
  • Competence with Git for version control, build tools, and CI/CD pipelines
  • Strong problem-solving skills, exceptional attention to detail, and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative, fast-paced team environment
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with a desire to learn from experienced engineers and contribute to a multi-disciplinary team

A D-Waver's DNA

  • We look at the future and say “why not”; we see possibilities where others see problems or routines. We show the way ahead and are committed to achieving ambitious goals.
  • We practice straight talk and listen generously to each other with empathy. We value different opinions and points of views. We ensure that we connect outside as well as inside to learn from others and inspire each other.
  • We hold ourselves accountable for delivering results. We make decisions & take responsibility so that we can act & support each other.
  • As leaders we motivate & engage our teams to undertake beyond what they originally thought possible, by developing our teams & creating the conditions for people to grow and empower themselves through enabling & coaching.

Our Compensation Philosophy is Simple but Powerful:

We believe providing D-Wavers with company ownership, competitive pay, and a range of meaningful benefits is the start of creating a culture where people want to give the best they’ve got — not because they’re simply making money, but because they’ve fallen in love with our vision, mission, values, and team.

During the interview process, your Recruiter will review our total rewards (base, equity, bonus, perks, benefit, culture) offerings. The final offer is determined by your proficiencies within this level.

Inclusion:

We celebrate diverse perspectives to drive innovation in our pursuit. Our employees range from distinguished domain experts with decades of experience in their respective fields, to bright and motivated graduates eager to make their mark. Our diverse and innovative team will make you feel appreciated, supported and empower your career growth at D-Wave.

Senior Data Engineer, Customer Data

AI & Data Workflows |Remote | Full-Time | EMEA

Who We Are: Front Office Transformation Experts

Bluprintx (BPX) is a global, AI-powered consultancy built to design and deliver the intelligent front office for CMO and CRO executives. We are private equity-backed and scaling fast, with 300 active customers across 10 countries and more than 1,750 implementations. We connect people, technology, and AI to turn fragmentation into performance, partnering with global leaders to modernize how marketing, CRM, content, AI & Data connect. At BPX, we hire operators and specialists who thrive at the intersection of commercial strategy and technical execution.

What We Do: Cutting Complexity Across the Front Office

We help the world's most ambitious companies, including Uber Eats, BNY, and Xerox, untangle the operational complexity that slows enterprise growth. As a Gold Adobe Solution Partner and Salesforce Summit Partner, we deliver strategy and implementation across the full front office. Our proprietary methodology builds sustainable enabled ecosystems that maximize ROI and accelerate speed to market. By embedding AI into commercial workflows, we help clients move faster and stay ahead.

The Role

BPX is hiring a Senior Data Engineer as we build out a dedicated Data capability alongside our Intelligent Marketing practice. You will build and run the pipelines, models and data products that feed enterprise front-office programmes, turning raw customer, product and interaction data into clean, trusted, activation-ready data. Snowflake is the core platform on our largest current programmes, connected to Twilio Segment, Braze and Amplitude, and you will also work on Databricks, BigQuery, Azure and AWS as client needs demand. This is a hands-on engineering role: you work to designs set with our data architects, write and review production code, and own the quality of what you ship. The data you build is what marketers use to segment, personalise and measure, so you will see your work turn into live customer experiences.

What you'll do

  • Build and maintain ingestion pipelines from source systems, event streams and third-party platforms into the cloud data platform.
  • Develop and test transformation logic and data models, turning raw data into clean, documented, reusable customer and event datasets.
  • Prepare activation-ready data for CDPs and engagement platforms, including audience tables, traits and warehouse-native or zero-copy sync patterns.
  • Work with data architects to implement target-state designs, and raise practical issues early so the design holds up in production.
  • Build data quality checks, monitoring and alerting, and diagnose and fix pipeline and data issues quickly when they arise.
  • Re-test and update downstream flows when source systems or platform architecture change, so CDP, engagement and reporting keep working.
  • Apply security, access control and privacy standards in every build, including GDPR and consent data handling.
  • Use version control, CI/CD and code review as standard, and document pipelines so client teams can support them.
  • Contribute to BPX's Data capability through reusable pipelines, templates and engineering standards, and support scoping and effort estimates.

What you'll bring

  • Five or more years in data engineering, including building production pipelines on a cloud data platform.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Snowflake. SnowPro Core certification or above is an advantage.
  • Working knowledge of at least one other platform, such as Databricks, BigQuery, Azure or AWS.
  • Expert SQL and strong Python, with sound data modelling skills.
  • Experience with modern data tooling such as dbt, Fivetran, Airflow or equivalent, and with Git and CI/CD practices.
  • Experience working with customer, marketing or event data, ideally feeding CDPs such as Twilio Segment or engagement platforms such as Braze. Exposure to product analytics tools such as Amplitude is a plus.
  • Practical grasp of data privacy, security and GDPR. Experience in financial services or other regulated industries is an advantage.
  • Consulting or agency background, or the ability to work directly with clients and explain technical work in plain terms.
  • Fluent English and the right to work in an EMEA country where BPX operates.

Why this role, why now

Our clients' front-office programmes now stand or fall on the data underneath them, and BPX is building a dedicated Data capability to own that layer. This role is one of its first engineering hires, working on enterprise programmes where data flows from the warehouse through the CDP to live, cross-channel engagement. If you want to see your pipelines turn directly into customer outcomes, and help set the engineering standards of a new capability rather than inherit them, this is that seat.

Additional information

Interview date: week commencing 23rd November

At Cancer Research UK, we exist to beat cancer.


Our Legacy Partnerships team plays a vital role in protecting and growing one of Cancer Research UK's most important income streams. As Performance Operations Manager (Legacy Partnerships), you'll combine data expertise, operational excellence and stakeholder management to help shape how we engage with professional partners, including solicitors and will writers.


As our Performance Operations Manager, you'll be responsible for enabling the Legacy Partnerships team to deliver impactful professional engagement activity through excellent reporting, operational processes and performance management.


This is an exciting opportunity to drive performance, improve processes and deliver meaningful insight that enables strategic decision-making, helping us maximise future gifts in wills and accelerate progress towards our mission of beating cancer.

What will I be doing?

  • Lead performance reporting and analysis, providing meaningful data and insight to support strategy development, decision-making and continuous improvement.
  • Monitor and evaluate professional engagement activity, identifying trends, opportunities and areas for improvement to drive growth and efficiency.
  • Act as the key liaison between Legacy Partnerships, Operations, Insight & Performance, Marketing and Product teams to ensure aligned ways of working and successful project delivery.
  • Drive operational excellence by identifying process improvements, resolving data quality issues and improving forecasting accuracy.
  • Develop and maintain reporting tools, dashboards and resources that enable the Legacy Partnerships team to effectively manage regional performance and engagement activity.
  • Support the planning and delivery of national and regional professional engagement campaigns, events and initiatives, working collaboratively with internal stakeholders.

What are we looking for?

We're looking for a highly organised and analytical professional who can turn complex data into actionable insight while building strong relationships across a wide range of stakeholders. You'll bring:

  • Proven experience in performance reporting, operational management or business analysis within a complex organisational environment.
  • Strong analytical and data management skills, with the ability to interpret, present and explain complex information clearly to a variety of audiences.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively at all levels.
  • Experience managing multiple priorities and projects simultaneously whilst maintaining high standards and attention to detail.
  • A proactive and flexible approach, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing priorities.
  • A genuine interest in using data, insight and continuous improvement to deliver better outcomes and drive organisational success.

Our organisation values are designed to guide all that we do.

Bold: Act with ambition, courage and determination

Credible: Act with rigour and professionalism

Human: Act to have a positive impact on people

Together: Act inclusively and collaboratively

We’re looking for people who can believe in and embody these organisation values and can use them to drive forward progress against our mission to beat cancer.

If you’re interested in applying and excited about working with us but are unsure if you have the right skills and experience we’d still love to hear from you.


Eligibility criteria

Internal candidates should ideally have completed their 6-month ‘getting started’ period before applying for other roles. You should also advise your current line manager at the point you make an internal application, or at the latest, at the point of being invited for an interview.

All internal candidates applying for a secondment, must have:

o completed their getting started period

o discussed their intention to apply and gained approval to apply with their line manager

o been in their substantive (home) role for at least 6 months (this is only applicable if you have previously been on secondment)

If you do not confirm that you meet these requirements, we will not be able to progress your application.

For information about internal learning and development at Cancer Research UK please visit Fuse.

We create a working environment that supports your wellbeing and provide a generous benefits package, a wide range of career and personal development opportunities and high-quality tools. Our policies and processes enable you to improve your work-life balance, take positive steps in your career and achieve your personal wellbeing goals.

You can explore our benefits by visiting our careers web page.

CVs are required for all applications; but we won’t be able to view them until we invite you for an interview. Instead, we ask you to complete the work history section of the online application form for us to be able to assess you fairly and objectively.

For more information on this career opportunity please visit our website or contact us at .

For more updates on our work and careers, follow us on: Linked In, Facebook, Instagram, X and YouTube.

Our vision is to create a charity where everyone feels like they belong, benefits from and participates in, the work we do. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and cultures, in particular those from ethnic minority backgrounds who are currently under-represented.

Working collaboratively with the Technical Integration team, SaaS vendor, ERP/AZ360 team, Security, and Agency Leads, this role empowers state agencies with custom reporting and executive compliance dashboards.

  • Ensure backend data structures effectively support statewide reporting, audit requirements, public records, and future analytics
  • Build, publish, and maintain custom tabular, summary, and matrix reports in the native Grants Management Report Builder

The role
We're hiring our first dedicated UX/UI designer. You'll be a design partner to product, not only an executor of requirements: you'll help imagine and shape new experiences, products and interfaces for both our readers and our customers, then turn them into finished, buildable designs across web, email and SaaS. You'll work day-to-day with our Senior Product Manager, Audience & Data, alongside engineering, editorial and commercial teams.

The role starts as a 1099 contract as soon as possible, at about 22–28 hours a week. We plan to convert to a full-time position in Q1 2027. We're looking for someone who wants the full-time role. The contract start gets us working together sooner.

What you'll work on first
  1. Website UX across 15 sites. For our move to a new CMS, we have core page templates and a design system in Figma, and the matching components are already built in our Storybook component library on Chromatic. You'll redesign, refine and extend them: a sponsored "Related Content" sidebar for article pages, sponsor Storefront microsite pages, and a searchable supplier directory with tiers and filters. Then you'll roll the changes out across all 15 site themes.
  2. Email newsletter system. Design a modular email system and theme it into about 26 newsletter templates (editorial, sponsored and personalized "matched for you" sends). It has to render in Outlook, Gmail and Apple Mail, and work with mobile stacking, dark mode and images off.
  3. RFP Navigator. A UX refresh of our B2B SaaS platform for two audiences: drug developers who issue RFPs and the CDMOs and CROs who answer them. This covers the marketing site, onboarding and the core RFP workflows.

What you'll do
  • Partner with product to brainstorm and shape new experiences, products and interfaces for readers (the life science professionals who use our sites and newsletters) and customers (the sponsors and clients who buy our marketing, data and platform products).

  • Present options and iterate with the PM, usually two or three review rounds per page type.
  • Work within the existing design system (Figma plus our Storybook component library in Chromatic): reuse what's already built, and add new components back to the shared library.
  • Spec designs for developers: layout, spacing, type, color tokens, interactions, responsive rules, content and data rules, accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and analytics events.

  • AI fluency: you already use AI tools in your design workflow and can show how.

How we work

This position is FULL TIME and fully remote.


Apply today to become part of our team of experts dedicated to advancing equitable, safe housing solutions for vulnerable populations

jobs.excerpt: Senior Application Security EngineerWe are hiring a Senior Application Security Engineer to own application security across Product Engineering and make Treatwell's products secure by default.
jobs.description:
Senior Application Security EngineerWe are hiring a Senior Application Security Engineer to own application security across Product Engineering and make Treatwell's products secure by default. You own the security tooling, from SAST in the pipelines to DefectDojo, you are the first call when an application-layer incident needs a security engineer, and you work hands-on with the teams that build our products: pairing with their engineers to fix what the scanners, the annual pentest and real incidents find, closing the design gaps behind them, and sometimes picking up a specific security epic for a product such as Connect or Salonized. Each time, the team ends up able to do the next one without you.

This is a hands-on role. You will write code, read a great deal more of it, and own the security tooling in our pipelines. Our applications are Java and Spring Boot across Marketplace and Payments, Ruby on Rails in our SaaS products, React and TypeScript on the web, native iOS and Android apps in Swift and Kotlin, and a small amount of PHP. Marketplace and Connect ship through GitLab CI and ArgoCD onto Kubernetes (EKS) in AWS; Salonized ships through GitHub Actions. Everything is monitored in Datadog, and findings from secrets detection, dependency scanning and SAST flow into a self-hosted DefectDojo.

This is application security, not infrastructure security: cloud, Kubernetes and network controls sit with our Developer Experience and Platform Core teams, and you work alongside them. You report to the Head of Developer Experience and set your own security roadmap with the Heads of Engineering, aligned to the OWASP ASVS and the OWASP DevSecOps Maturity Model. We have no CISO: you present the security posture to the CTO and VP of Engineering on a fixed cadence, and your view carries weight because it comes from the code.
How you will work

  • Cross-area by default. The security tooling, the findings pipeline and application-layer incident support are yours across all of Product Engineering. When a product needs focused work, such as a security epic for Connect or Salonized, you pick it up with that team, agreed with its Head of Engineering. Infrastructure security stays with Developer Experience and Platform Core.
  • Fix with the team, not for the team. You pair on remediation and the team's engineers merge the fix, so the knowledge stays where the code lives.
  • Guardrails over gates. The default is a secure path that is quicker to use than to bypass: shared libraries, pipeline templates, pre-commit checks. Blocking is reserved for critical findings on new code and agreed with the area.
  • One queue. Findings land in DefectDojo and move into the team's backlog or Now/Next like any other work. There is no parallel security process.
  • Through the champions. You work with each team's Security Champion and the Security Champions guild. In eighteen months a threat model or an incident should not need you in the room.
  • Your own roadmap. You keep a short Now/Next/Later for security, agreed each quarter with the Heads of Engineering, separate from the DevX roadmap.
  • Posture, not paperwork. You present the security posture per area to the CTO and VP of Engineering on a fixed cadence, measured against the DevSecOps Maturity Model.

You will be responsible for:

  • Owning application security across Product Engineering and working hands-on with the teams to remediate vulnerabilities in our codebases, from authentication and session handling to payments flows and public APIs, including specific security epics for a product such as Connect or Salonized.
  • Owning the security tooling across all areas (secrets detection, dependency scanning, SAST, DefectDojo, threat modelling) and landing SAST in our pipelines: completing the proof of concept with the SAST vendors we are evaluating on two pilot teams, the Marketplace Checkout and Identity team and a SaaS team, tuning rules until engineers trust the output, and feeding every finding into DefectDojo rather than a new dashboard.
  • Making DefectDojo work without a human in the loop: team ownership synced from our service catalogue, every team's repositories covered, and an agreed rule for which findings block a pipeline and which only report.
  • Building secure defaults into the paved road so the secure way is the easy way: authentication and session libraries, input validation, secrets handling, dependency and container checks in the pipeline templates teams already use.
  • Running threat modelling with teams before the work is fully scoped, using and improving our AI-based threat modeller so that it answers an engineer's question plainly and produces backlog items with owners and dates.
  • Triaging findings from scanners, the annual penetration test and external reports, agreeing severity and ownership with the team, and tracking them to closure in DefectDojo against our severity SLAs.
  • Being the first security call for application-layer incidents across Product Engineering: leading the technical side, assessing with Legal whether personal data was exposed, writing the postmortem actions, and working with Customer Support and Payments on fraud and customer-flagged cases including phishing.
  • Owning our security vendor relationships: the annual penetration-test cycle with our testing partner (scoping, scheduling, remediation planning), the responsible-disclosure programme and the security@ inbox, and the SAST vendor once selected.
  • Acting as the security reviewer in our third-party risk process for new vendors and integrations, and answering the security questionnaires our partners send us.
  • Measuring the security posture per area against the DevSecOps Maturity Model and presenting it to the CTO and VP of Engineering on a fixed cadence.
  • Growing the Security Champions programme with the Head of Developer Experience: a named champion in every team, demo-led guild sessions, and two security improvements per area shipped through team backlogs each quarter.
  • Keeping a short, current security roadmap (Now/Next/Later), agreed with the Heads of Engineering each quarter and visible to Product Engineering.

About you

  • You have worked as an application security engineer, or as a backend engineer who owned security for a product, and you fix vulnerabilities yourself rather than only reporting them.
  • You read and write production code in at least one of our languages (Java, Ruby, TypeScript) well enough to pair on a fix, review a merge request and spot the second bug behind the first.
  • You know the OWASP ASVS and Top 10 from code rather than slides, and you can run a threat model that ends in backlog items rather than a document.
  • You have put SAST, dependency scanning or secrets detection into CI pipelines (GitLab CI or GitHub Actions) and tuned the rules so developers kept trusting them.
  • You have worked with a vulnerability management platform and you know how to keep a finding moving to closure without chasing people by hand.
  • You understand how authentication, sessions, authorisation and payments flows break in practice: IDOR, token and magic-link misuse, JWT validation mistakes, race conditions, injection, and the odd device-id collision.
  • You know enough AWS and Kubernetes to see where application security meets the platform, and when to hand a problem to the platform team instead.
  • You explain risk in plain language to engineers, Heads of Engineering and non-technical leaders, and you can say "this one is fine" as clearly as "this one is not".
  • You transfer skills on purpose: your measure of success is a team that does not need you for the next one.
  • You use AI tooling as a normal part of the work, for threat modelling, code review and reading unfamiliar codebases, and you know where it is wrong.

Nice to have

  • Experience in a marketplace, payments or SaaS business handling card data and personal data under PCI DSS and GDPR.
  • A bug bounty, CTF or penetration-testing background, or an offensive certification such as OSCP, OSWE or BSCP.
  • Running or scaling a Security Champions programme.
  • Familiarity with the OWASP DevSecOps Maturity Model or another maturity framework.
  • Hands-on time with WAF and bot protection, secrets management, and infrastructure-as-code scanning, ideally in AWS.
  • Spring Security or Rails security internals; writing custom SAST rules.

We’ll treat you with:

  • 28-days holiday, plus bank holidays
  • Monthly €40 Treatwell vouchers so you can treat yourself too
  • Mental health support through our partnership with Open-Up
  • Market-specific benefits that will be discussed in the interview process

Equal Opportunities

Treatwell is an 'Open to All' employer and warmly welcomes everybody to the team. We are committed to making reasonable adjustments to the recruitment process as required. Please add any adjustment requests to your application.

A FEW REASONS TO WORK WITH US

Job Description Summary

The Director, Infrastructure & Platform leads the team that creates standard, reliable environments on which Defense & Systems builds, tests, and delivers software. The team owns the secure platforms, shared services, and the single golden-path delivery pipeline that the organization's software developers depend on, so that delivery is dependable, on time, and to standard. The role runs the platform as a product, not as a help desk.

This is a people-leadership role accountable for both the operating model and the people who run it. The Director sets the platform roadmap and service standards, mandates the golden path that product teams adopt, and holds the team to FLIGHT DECK standard work and a bias toward flow. Success improves Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost by removing undifferentiated infrastructure work from every software team and replacing ad-hoc environments with a governed, consumable platform.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

Team leadership and talent

  • Lead and develop the Infrastructure & Platform team — technical program management, platform and infrastructure engineering, and infrastructure architecture — with clear role clarity, objectives, and standard work for each seat
  • Own the team’s performance and development; build a culture of ownership, flow, and continuous improvement
  • Identify and remove obstacles on behalf of the team, and coach problem-solving at the point of work

Platform operating model and governance

  • Own and mandate a single golden-path delivery pipeline — CI/CD, environments, and shared services — that all product teams adopt, and govern the exception process when a team cannot
  • Operate the platform as a product: a named backlog, a published roadmap, and service standards for availability, support, change management, and SLAs
  • Establish how platform change is requested, prioritized, approved, and released, and make that governance visible to the teams it affects
  • Partner with Cyber Security to build security best practice into the platform by default, and scope the DevSecOps capability gap as an explicit Phase 2 headcount ask

Delivery and reliability

  • Ensure secure, reliable, and scalable infrastructure across cloud, on-premises, and edge environments in a defense context
  • Set the operating rhythm — daily management, WOR, and MOR — that keeps reliability and delivery managed, not merely reported
  • Partner with the four product-development software teams so the platform meets their current needs and anticipates their future ones

Cross-organization alignment

  • Represent Infrastructure & Platform in the Tech Ops leadership cadence and align the platform roadmap to the enterprise and CDAIO baseline
  • Partner with the Director, Architecture & Data so platform patterns and architecture guardrails stay coupled

Basic qualifications (required)

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or college with a minimum of 7 years of professional experience OR Associate's degree with a minimum of 10 years of professional experience OR High School Diploma with a minimum of 12 years of professional experience.

Eligibility requirement

Desired characteristics (preferred, not mandatory)

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or Engineering.
  • Experience building and running an internal platform or paved-road capability as a product, with defined service levels.
  • Platform engineering and site reliability engineering (SRE) background: CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, observability, and on-call operations.
  • Working knowledge of cloud (AWS or Azure), hybrid, and edge environments.

  • Ability to drive adoption of a shared standard across teams that do not report to you.
  • Defense, aerospace, or other regulated or export-controlled environment background.

Success metrics

  • Product teams on the golden-path pipeline — adoption rate across the four software teams

  • Change failure rate and time-to-restore for platform services

Why this role

We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting.

About the Role

You will own the systems, processes and frameworks that drive performance across the company. You will lead company-wide OKR planning and review cycles, design scalable performance management processes, analyze organizational data, and ensure our culture and values are consistently reflected in how we hire, evaluate and develop people.

You will work closely with leadership across the business to improve execution, increase accountability and help teams perform at their highest level.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Own and continuously improve the company's performance management framework.

  • Lead company-wide OKR planning, tracking and quarterly review cycles.

  • Design and implement scalable people processes that improve organizational effectiveness.

  • Analyze people, performance and operational data to identify trends, measure outcomes and recommend improvements.

  • Build dashboards and reports that provide meaningful insights into organizational performance.

  • Define business requirements for HR systems, reporting tools and workflow automation.

  • Partner with leaders across the company to improve team performance and execution.

  • Develop frameworks for performance reviews, calibration, promotions and career development.

  • Drive initiatives that strengthen accountability, ownership and a high-performance culture.

  • Ensure company values are embedded throughout employee programs, performance evaluations and day-to-day operations.

  • Continuously identify opportunities to simplify processes, eliminate inefficiencies and improve the employee experience.

  • Support strategic people initiatives and organizational projects as the company grows.

What You Will Need

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience in People Operations, People Analytics, Organizational Effectiveness, HR Strategy, Business Operations, Management Consulting or a related field.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and translate insights into action.

  • Experience designing or improving performance management frameworks, OKRs or organizational processes.

  • Excellent problem-solving and structured thinking skills.

  • Ability to write clear business requirements and improve operational workflows.

  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, high-growth environment with evolving priorities.

  • High ownership, attention to detail and a bias toward execution.

How We Work

The best products in the world are built by small, highly capable teams.

We operate with high talent density, high ownership and high standards. We value people who can think independently, move quickly and solve problems without waiting for instructions.

This is a hands-on environment. Everyone is expected to contribute directly to the company's success.

Interview Process

If there appears to be a fit, we will schedule up to 3 interviews.

Applications are reviewed by members of our leadership and hiring teams. Interviews may be conducted virtually or onsite.

We value speed, transparency and decisiveness throughout the process.

jobs.excerpt: Please review the job details below. Intuitive Machines – West is seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to help build and manage a supply chain capable of flexing across two very different operating modes: high-volume, cost-efficient, and schedule-driven commercial production, and traditional, low-volume, high-reliability government and legacy space programs.
jobs.description:
Please review the job details below.

Intuitive Machines – West is seeking a Strategic Sourcing Manager to help build and manage a supply chain capable of flexing across two very different operating modes: high-volume, cost-efficient, and schedule-driven commercial production, and traditional, low-volume, high-reliability government and legacy space programs. This position is located in Palo Alto, CA or Houston, TX - (remote considered).


Intuitive Machines is a world leader in delivering powerful and innovative spacecraft. That legacy is adapting to include high-volume production capability for advanced spacecraft, while preserving the rigorous, mission-critical sourcing needs of traditional space programs. This role sits at the center of that dual mandate- the ideal candidate will have the skill and agility to support production environments optimized for throughput and cost-efficiency, as well as strategic, high-stakes programs that focus on lower-rate production, reliability, and risk mitigation.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead procurement and supplier partnership initiatives, tailoring sourcing strategy to the specific risk, cost, and schedule profile of each program
  • Conduct comprehensive supplier analysis to identify new and existing suppliers, optimize cost structures, and ensure continuity of supply
  • Lead cross-functional teams to assess supplier technical capability, industrial capacity, and quality systems to determine fit for either high-rate production or low-volume, high-reliability work
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to address supplier quality, cost, delivery, lead-time, and risk compliance
  • Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders (business development, contracts, program management, engineering, quality) to translate customer requirements into the right procurement strategy
  • Partner with engineering on design decisions that support an efficient and resilient supply plan, including designing for manufacturability at scale or designing for mission assurance on a one-off build

High-Volume Program Focus:

  • Architect and scale a repeatable, agile supply chain capable of supporting serial production of spacecraft and subsystems
  • Qualify suppliers for industrial-scale output while managing cost-down roadmaps and lead-time compression
  • Traditional/Low-Volume Program Focus:
  • Manage sourcing for custom, mission-specific hardware with extended qualification and traceability requirements
  • Navigate government contracting requirements (e.g., FAR/DFARS flow-downs) and long-lead procurement cycles typical of legacy space programs

What We're Looking For:

  • A solid understanding of the space industry's evolution over the past decades, along with general technical familiarity with satellite systems and subsystems
  • The judgment to know when to apply traditional, risk-averse sourcing practices versus when to challenge legacy approaches to solve cost and schedule problems
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity- able to toggle between structured, compliance-heavy sourcing and fast-moving, scale-focused sourcing
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills with business development, product, program management, engineering, and quality teams

Your Career:

Intuitive Machines takes professional development seriously. You'll have the opportunity to define your own career trajectory, working with a manager or mentor to set goals and build a development plan.


What We Offer:

Dedicated time for professional development, conference attendance, industry training, peer group collaboration, paid certifications, and education reimbursement.


Minimum Requirements:

  • Must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
  • Bachelor's degree in business, engineering, supply chain, or a related field. Four additional years of related experience may be substituted for degree.
  • Minimum of 8 years of experience sourcing from a global supply base, using a variety of contractual models (development, supply, licensing, and service agreements)
  • Minimum of 2 years of functional lead, supervisory, or management experience, or equivalent experience leading multifunctional/cross-functional teams
  • Proven success working on cross-functional new product introduction (NPI) projects
  • Technical knowledge of high-volume manufacturing products and industry practices
  • Ability to travel up to 20% and communicate outside of standard work hours as needed
  • Demonstrated ability to work in a changing environment and adapt across different projects and situations, directly relevant to toggling between high-volume and traditional low-volume programs

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification
  • Government procurement experience
  • Lean Six Sigma process improvement experience
  • Space products procurement and supply chain experience
  • Industrialization in automotive experience
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders, including suppliers, engineering, legal, finance, manufacturing, and logistics
  • Detail-oriented, self-motivated, and able to respond quickly in a fast-moving, ever-changing environment

The position is accountable for ensuring scalable support for production and development customers, driving consistent service standards worldwide, improving operational efficiency, and partnering closely with Engineering, Operations, Sales, Product Management, Quality, and Service Centers to deliver exceptional customer outcomes.


The Director will lead a global team of Field Service Engineers and regional service leaders while driving continuous improvement initiatives that improve uptime, reduce repair cycle times, increase customer satisfaction, and support revenue growth.

jobs.title: Assistant Controller, Client Success
jobs.excerpt: Update, September 22, 2026 Our original application deadline was September 17.
jobs.description:
Update, September 22, 2026

Our original application deadline was September 17. We're currently reviewing applications and conducting interviews for this role. We're still glad to receive applications, if this role remains open or another opportunity arises, we'll be in touch.

The Opportunity

At Humanity Financial, you can use your accounting expertise in service of organizations working toward meaningful change. Our work is guided by the Five Stages of Financial Wellness, a framework that recognizes that financial wellness is not simply about whether reports, budgets and processes exist, it is about whether they are reliable and useful under pressure.

As an Assistant Controller, Client Success - you will contribute to the foundations of this journey by strengthening financial visibility, reporting, processes and organizational capacity. You will work alongside clients to understand where they are, address immediate financial needs and build the conditions for more confident decision-making and long-term financial transformation.

Who We Are

Humanity Financial was founded on the traditional, ancestral, and stolen lands of the xwmethkwey'em (Musqueam), Skwxwu7mesh (Squamish), and selilwetalh (Tsleil-Waututh) Nations. Our team is fully remote, working from home and live on many Indigenous territories throughout what is now called Canada.

We are a CPA firm that works exclusively with social purpose organizations, including First Nations, Indigenous communities and charities and nonprofits. We are a certified B Corporation and the first CPA firm in British Columbia to become a Benefit Company.

We are pleased to be a PAIR Bronze Certified organization through the Canadian Council for Indigenous Business and are also certified carbon neutral, a certified Caring Company, a certified Great Place to Work.

Position Summary

Position: Assistant Controller, Client Success

Reports to: Associate Director, Client Success and Finance Transformation

Status: Permanent, full-time (40 hours per week)

Location: Work from home within Canada

Reporting to the Associate Director, Client Success and Finance Transformation, the Assistant Controller works within a team of accountants and bookkeepers to support a portfolio of social purpose clients on their financial wellness journeys.

The Assistant Controller, Client Success helps ensure the accuracy and completeness of clients’ financial information and reporting and supports regulatory compliance, budgeting, forecasting, cash-flow management and audit coordination. The role also reviews the work of other team members and provides coaching, training and mentorship that strengthens the capacity of both the client service team and the organizations we serve.

This position combines strong technical accounting skills with sound judgment, curiosity, clear communication and a genuine commitment to client success. Because our services are delivered remotely, the successful candidate must have an appropriate home workspace and be comfortable building relationships and collaborating with clients and colleagues virtually. Occasional travel within Canada may be required.

Who You Are

You are a CPA with several years of progressively responsible accounting experience, whether gained in public practice, industry or the social purpose sector. You are looking for work that combines strong technical accounting with authentic client relationships and lasting organizational impact.

You enjoy solving puzzles, rolling up your sleeves and putting the pieces together in practice, not only in theory. You understand that getting into bookkeeping details is sometimes part of the work and can be essential to understanding what is happening in a client’s financial systems.

You care about client success and want your work to support organizations advancing important missions. You understand that financial transformation can be complex and are prepared to approach challenging situations with patience, sound judgment and persistence.

What You Bring

We recognize that strong candidates may have gained their experience through different career paths. You do not need to meet every item under “Nice to have” to apply.

Required

  • A Canadian CPA designation in good standing.
  • Several years of progressively responsible accounting experience, including experience with audit or assurance engagements in public practice.
  • Hands-on, full-cycle accounting experience, including journal entries, reconciliations, month-end processes and preparation or review of financial reports.
  • Experience managing competing priorities and deadlines across multiple clients, organizations or business units.
  • Experience reviewing the work of junior team members and providing clear instructions, coaching and constructive feedback.
  • Strong client-facing communication skills and the ability to build respectful, collaborative relationships.
  • Sound professional judgment, attention to detail and the ability to investigate and resolve accounting issues.
  • Confidence learning and working across different accounting systems and digital tools in a remote environment.
  • Cultural awareness, humility and a commitment to continuous learning when working with people from different communities, backgrounds and lived experiences.

Nice to Have

  • Experience working with charities, nonprofits, First Nations governments, Indigenous communities or Indigenous organizations.
  • Knowledge of fund accounting, restricted contributions, funder reporting or the financial and reporting environments in which social purpose organizations operate.
  • Experience preparing budgets, forecasts, cash-flow projections and budget-to-actual reporting.
  • Experience working directly with executive directors, senior leaders, boards of directors or finance committees.
  • Experience strengthening financial policies, internal controls, procedures or finance-team structures.
  • Experience onboarding new clients or managing client engagements, projects, scope and budgets.
  • Experience working successfully as part of a fully remote team.
  • Familiarity with a range of cloud-based accounting, reporting and workflow systems.

We know that many technical skills can be taught. We have built a learning library and an onboarding process to support your success. What matters to us is your desire to learn and grow, your openness to change and the perspective you bring to our team.

What We Offer

Humanity Financial is unlike most accounting firms. We do not complete year-end corporate tax returns or audits, so there is no traditional tax season. We fully support work-life balance and provide opportunities to build a meaningful career without a conventional track to partnership.

Our team members care deeply about one another and our clients. We foster collaborative relationships, lead with kindness and do not shy away from courageous conversations. We support and celebrate one another in doing our best work; ego and internal competition are not particularly valued here.

Total Compensation

The starting salary for the Assistant Controller, Client Success is $88,474, with the salary band extending to $127,181 per year. Assistant Controllers, Client Success typically start at (or near) the beginning of the salary band and receive three weeks of annual vacation plus additional paid time off. Other highlights of our total rewards package include health and dental benefits from the first day of employment, an RRSP matching program, paid volunteer time and an annual professional development allowance.

Commitment to Equity, Diversity and Inclusion

Equity, diversity and inclusion are central to Humanity’s vision, mission and values. We are committed to identifying and removing barriers in our employment practices and creating a workplace where people from different backgrounds, identities and lived experiences can contribute and thrive.

We encourage applications from Indigenous Peoples, racialized people, women, people with disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ people, newcomers and others who experience structural barriers to employment. We believe that a workforce reflecting the diversity of the communities we serve strengthens our work.

Accommodation is available throughout the recruitment process. Please let us know what you need from us to participate fully and we will work with you to make appropriate arrangements.

Our Recruitment Process

We strive to be consistent in how we assess applicants and transparent about what candidates can expect.

  • We do not use an automated applicant tracking system. A person will read your resume and application email.
  • Following a successful application review, the first step is a phone conversation to establish a connection, learn more about your experience and discuss administrative details.
  • The next step is a 45-60 -minute video interview with one or two members of our team. This discussion explores your experience, approach and alignment with our work and culture.
  • Candidates who continue will participate in a 60-minute video interview with two Associate Directors, Client Success and Finance Transformation. This is a further opportunity to explore mutual fit and learn about the day-to-day work.
  • You are encouraged to ask questions at every stage.
  • Before making an offer, we will request three references and expect to speak with at least two people who have recently worked directly with you, including someone who supervised or evaluated your work.

How to Apply

Apply through the Join Us section of our website by clicking on the Assistant Controller opportunity. Please include:

  1. An updated resume showing how your skills and experience align with the role.
  2. A paragraph (or two) response to the following two questions:
    1. What makes Humanity Financial the right place for you?
    2. Our culture is closely connected to our mission and purpose. How would you contribute to our team culture, and what would you bring?

You are welcome to tell us about any accommodation you may need during the recruitment process. If what you have read resonates with you, we would be grateful to hear from you.

Detailed Overview of Responsibilities and Duties

Client Reporting & Compliance: The Assistant Controller, Client Success oversees a client’s daily accounting operations and ensures accurate, complete, and high-quality financial reporting. This role develops positive and productive relationships with clients, working closely with them to understand their financial needs and develops financial solutions that support their mission.

  • Meet with new and current clients to review and document their existing financial processes and policies, making recommendations for change where they can be improved
  • Review monthly bookkeeping, working papers, and journal entries prepared by bookkeepers and preparers for accuracy and completeness
  • Review year-end working papers and financial statements prepared by bookkeepers or preparers
  • Prepare more complex working papers and provide oversight and direction for bookkeepers or preparer team
  • Develop more complex financial reports in accounting software, and related working papers in preparation for year-end filing
  • Provide support, training, and direction throughout the year to our clients’ bookkeepers as required
  • Prepare financial funder reports for non-profit and charity clients
  • Monitor client compliance deadlines, including corporate tax instalments, GST returns, PST returns, all payroll-related remittances, and year-end corporate
