Senior Privacy Consultant / Data Protection Officer

Remote

Harper James is growing its data protection team. We’re looking for an experienced privacy professional to help deliver our outsourced DPO service and support ambitious businesses with their day-to-day data protection needs.

You’ll manage client relationships, provide practical advice and help businesses put effective privacy processes into practice. You do not need to be a qualified solicitor or hold a law degree to apply.

About Harper James

We’re a national commercial law firm supporting entrepreneurial businesses throughout their growth. Our approach combines experienced people, accessible advice and flexible ways of working.

Our data protection service helps clients understand their responsibilities and manage risk in a way that works for their business. You’ll work alongside our specialist solicitors, bringing your own experience of managing privacy programmes and delivering ongoing support.

Remote working

You’ll work remotely as part of a connected and supportive team, with access to our regional meeting spaces.

We share knowledge, work together on client matters and make time to build relationships with colleagues. You’ll have the flexibility to organise your work responsibly, with support available when you need it.

What we’re looking for

You’ll have substantial experience in data protection, typically gained over five or more years, and a track record of taking responsibility for a privacy programme or a portfolio of clients.

Your background might be in an outsourced DPO service, privacy consultancy, an in-house data protection team or information governance. We’re interested in the experience and judgement you bring, and your ability to help clients make progress.

You’ll be confident in areas including:

  • Assessing privacy compliance, identifying gaps and developing practical improvement plans.

  • Advising on data protection impact assessments and monitoring resulting actions.

  • Maintaining records of processing, privacy notices, policies and retention schedules.

  • Supporting data subject access requests and other individual rights requests.

  • Assessing suppliers, data-sharing arrangements and international transfers.

  • Supporting breach assessment, incident response and engagement with regulators.

  • Delivering training and explaining data protection requirements to different audiences.

You’ll have a strong working knowledge of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act and PECR, alongside an understanding of relevant European requirements. Experience of AI governance or technology projects would also be valuable.

A qualification such as CIPP/E, CIPM or an equivalent is desirable. We place particular value on evidence that you can apply your knowledge effectively.

Your role

You’ll become a trusted point of contact for a portfolio of clients, acting as their appointed DPO where appropriate and helping them maintain an effective privacy programme.

That means understanding each business, agreeing priorities, reviewing progress and providing clear advice when questions arise. You’ll be comfortable working with founders, senior managers, HR and IT teams, and constructively challenging decisions where necessary.

You’ll manage competing demands, maintain clear records and recognise when specialist legal or technical input is needed. Our data protection solicitors will work alongside you on complex legal issues, and you’ll help develop our processes and resources as the service grows.

The Harper James difference

We give people responsibility and trust them to deliver. You’ll be supported by colleagues who share their expertise and value straightforward communication.

You’ll enjoy working here if you:

  • Take ownership and follow through on commitments.

  • Explain complex issues clearly and without unnecessary jargon.

  • Balance commercial understanding with sound professional judgement.

  • Work confidently with Microsoft 365 and learn new systems readily.

  • Explore responsible ways to use technology and AI to improve your work.

  • Contribute to a friendly team where people support each other.

What we offer

  • A competitive salary.

  • Flexible remote working.

  • 33 days’ annual leave, including public holidays, with the option to purchase up to five additional days.

  • Private healthcare and life assurance.

  • Access to our electric vehicle scheme.

  • Varied work with growing businesses and the opportunity to help shape our expanding privacy service.

NO AGENCIES PLEASE

jobs.excerpt: Our MissionAt Palo Alto Networks®, we’re united by a shared mission—to protect our digital way of life.
jobs.description:
Our Mission

At Palo Alto Networks®, we’re united by a shared mission—to protect our digital way of life. We thrive at the intersection of innovation and impact, solving real-world problems with cutting-edge technology and bold thinking. Here, everyone has a voice, and every idea counts. If you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career alongside people who are just as passionate as you are, you’re in the right place.

Who We Are

In order to be the cybersecurity partner of choice, we must trailblaze the path and shape the future of our industry. This is something our employees work at each day and is defined by our values: Disruption, Collaboration, Execution, Integrity, and Inclusion. We weave AI into the fabric of everything we do and use it to augment the impact every individual can have. If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us!

This role is remote, but distance is no barrier to impact. Our hybrid teams collaborate across geographies to solve big problems, stay close to our customers, and grow together. You will be part of a culture that values trust, accountability, and shared success where your work truly matters.

Job Summary

The Team

Unit 42 - Unit 42 is our global threat intelligence team, and our mission is to provide customers with the context, analysis, and assistance they need to protect themselves from the most sophisticated cyber threats. We are on the front lines of cyber security, researching and hunting for the latest threats and providing that intelligence to our customers and the broader community. Our team is a group of world-renowned security researchers, incident responders, and security consultants who are at the forefront of the fight to prevent successful cyberattacks.


Job Summary

As a Principal Consultant on the Offensive Security team, you will be a key leader in assessing and challenging the security posture of a diverse client portfolio. You will leverage a variety of advanced tools and methodologies to act as the client's advocate for cybersecurity best practices. This role is critical in providing strong, actionable recommendations to enhance our clients' defenses against sophisticated threats.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead conducting comprehensive penetration tests (network, web application, cloud, mobile) to identify and exploit vulnerabilities.
  • Deliver assessments using Palo Alto Networks Frontier AI Defense test harnesses and platforms using the latest frontier models.
  • Develop custom scripts, tools, and methodologies to automate and enhance offensive security engagements and internal processes.
  • Lead client engagements, clearly articulating testing approaches and methodologies to both technical and executive audiences.
  • Generate detailed reports that communicate test results, identified risks, and concrete remediation recommendations to clients.
  • Proactively collaborate with internal teams and clients, exchanging information to ensure alignment and accomplish shared security objectives.
  • Lead in scoping new opportunities and developing internal infrastructure for offensive security research and development.
  • Ability to travel as needed to meet business demands

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Information Security, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 6+ years of professional experience in information security, with a focus on penetration testing and vulnerability assessments.
  • Expertise with security assessment tools such as Metasploit, Burp Suite Pro, Cobalt Strike, Nessus, and Bloodhound.
  • Proficiency in scripting or programming with languages like Python, PowerShell, Ruby, or C++.
  • Demonstrated experience in conducting penetration tests across various environments including Windows, Linux, and cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing or mentoring junior consultants on security engagements.
  • Demonstrated interest in LLM driven offensive security
  • Certifications such as OSCP, OSCE, GPEN, GWAPT, or GXPN.
  • Experience with public speaking, publishing research, or contributing to the security community.

POSTING DETAILS:

Make an Impact

Trillium Health Resources is a Tailored Plan and Managed Care Organization (MCO) serving 46 counties across North Carolina. We manage services for individuals with serious mental health needs, substance use disorders, traumatic brain injuries, and intellectual/development (IDD) disabilities. Our mission is to help individuals and families build strong foundations for healthy, fulfilling lives.

Why Work for Us?

Trillium believes that empowering others begins with supporting our team. We offer our employees:

  • A collaborative, mission-driven work environment
  • Competitive benefits and work-from-home options for most positions
  • Opportunities for professional growth in a diverse inclusive culture

Every day, our work changes lives – from children thriving through early intervention and school-based therapies, to adults with severe mental illness living independently and contributing to their communities.

If you are looking for a unique opportunity to make a tangible impact on the lives of others, apply today!

What We’re Looking For

Trillium Health Resources has a career opening for a Care Management Specialist I to join our Care Management team. This position will be instrumental in providing key support to Care Managers in delivering appropriate services to meet members’ needs. A Care Management Specialist I assists Care Managers with their duties, augmenting the team’s workforce capacity and delivering most Tailored Care Management member required contacts. This work may include meeting with members virtually or in person, recording member health updates, suggesting changes to the Care Manager for current care plan efficacy, and assisting the member in finding additional medical or community-based resources, among others. The Care Management Specialist I would be expected to work and be available at their remote location between the hours of 8:30am – 5:00pm and be flexible to travel within the community to meet with members as well as attend other meetings as needed.

On a typical day, you might:

  • Perform supportive outreach, follow-up, and engagement with members.
  • Facilitate programs and activities that promote holistic health and improve members’ health literacy/education (teaching self-management skills, sharing self-help recovery resources, distributing educational materials on chronic conditions, etc.
  • Arrange/schedule various member services, including appointments, wellness reminders, and non-emergency medical transportation needs.
  • Collaborate with the Care Manager and other personnel of the care team to communicate information regarding the members’ care, including health updates and changes.
  • Participate in relevant educational case conferences.
  • Ensure the proper storage and transmission of sensitive health records.

Employee Benefits:

Trillium knows that work/life balance is essential. That’s why we offer:

  • Typical working hours: 8:30 am – 5:00 pm; flexible work schedules with some roles with management approval.
  • Work-from-home options available for most positions
  • Health Insurance with no premium for employee coverage
  • Flexible Spending Accounts
  • 24 days of Paid Time Off (PTO) plus 12 paid holidays in your first year
  • NC Local Government Retirement Pension (defined-benefit plan)
  • 401k with 5% employer match and immediate vesting
  • Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) qualifying employer
  • Quarterly stipend for remote work supplies

Qualifications

Required:

  • High school diploma or GED and one (1) year of lived experience with an intellectual/developmental disability (I/DD) or a traumatic brain injury (TBI) with demonstrated knowledge of and direct personal experience navigating the North Carolina Medicaid delivery system; OR
  • High school diploma or GED and one (1) year of lived experience with a behavioral health condition and certification as a Peer Support Specialist; OR
  • High school diploma or GED and one (1) year of direct experience as a parent or guardian providing care for an individual with an I/DD, TBI, or behavioral health condition and navigating the Medicaid delivery system on behalf of that individual (parent/guardian cannot serve as a specialist for their family member); OR
  • High school diploma or GED and one (1) year of paid experience performing the duties described in the “Essential Duties” in the job description, with at least one (1) year of paid experience working directly with the Tailored Care Management eligible population.
  • Must have a valid driver’s license.
  • Certified Peer Support Specialist if used for qualifying as noted above.
  • Must reside within Trillium’s South Central Region, which includes the following counties: Carteret, Craven, Duplin, Jones, Lenoir, Onslow, Pender, Sampson, and Wayne.
  • Must be able to travel within catchment as required.
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship for employment now or in the future (ex: OPT F-1, J-1).

Preferred:

  • Two (2) years of paid experience performing the duties described in the “Essential Duties” section listed in the job description.

Deadline for Application:Thursday November 5, 2026, at 11:59PM

How to Apply

To be considered, submit your application and resume through our ADP Career Center. Your resume must include:

  • Employer name, dates of service (month/year), average hours worked per week, and essential job duties
  • Education details (degree type, date awarded, institution, field of study)
  • Licensure/certification information, if applicable

After submission, your resume will be reviewed to ensure it meets the essential criteria for the position. You’ll be notified by HR regarding your application status as appropriate. All applicants will receive a final update once the recruitment cycle closes.

Join our Talent Community through ADP to stay informed about future opportunities. Be sure to keep your resume updated in your profile.

Trillium Health Resources is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer and a drug-free workplace. All candidates must pass a drug test as a condition of employment.

jobs.description:
About TalkingPoints

TalkingPoints is an award-winning education technology nonprofit on a mission to unlock every student’s potential by activating one of the most underutilized forces in education - families. We believe that when families and schools work together, students thrive - and we’re building the tools to make that partnership possible for every family.

Our platform helps schools reach and engage every family - including those historically underserved - through accessible, two-way communication in 150+ languages, along with data, insights, and supports that strengthen relationships and drive student success.

Today, millions of educators and families are using TalkingPoints in their classrooms, schools, and districts across the U.S. to build stronger partnerships and improve outcomes for students. Our work is grounded in research and has been shown to meaningfully impact attendance, learning, and more.

We partner with leading school districts nationwide and are supported by a strong community of philanthropic and strategic partners, including major foundations, technology leaders, and education organizations.

TalkingPoints is at an exciting stage of growth and impact. As we continue to expand our reach and deepen our impact, we’re looking for passionate, mission-driven team members who want to help schools and families succeed - together. Learn more at .

The Opportunity

The Research and Learning Scientist drives rigorous, actionable research on how TalkingPoints improves student outcomes through family-school partnerships. They support R&D for our family learning products, making sure the home practices we promote match how children build literacy and numeracy skills. They also contribute to studies across our broader research agenda. Reporting to the Director of Research, they own projects from design to dissemination and work cross-functionally on a team that values rigor and rapid iteration.

You will:

  • Drive research for our at-home learning and personalized recommendation products, and contribute to studies across the research agenda
  • Support product R&D by applying learning science and behavior-change principles and testing whether features strengthen family practices and student learning
  • Advise on AI-powered family recommendations, including which data signals to use, how they map to skills, where data is too thin to personalize, and how good the outputs are
  • Design and run mixed methods studies from rapid-cycle, descriptive, and correlational analyses to quasi-experimental designs and randomized trials
  • Manage, clean, and analyze quantitative and qualitative platform, partner, and public data (e.g., NCES, state systems)
  • Develop and administer measures of family and educator outcomes linked to student outcomes
  • Turn findings into impact stories and strategic recommendations for product, partnerships, and fundraising
  • Represent our research with districts, funders, and external researchers, lead long-term district research partnerships, and informally mentor other researchers as needed

Who You Are

Required

  • PhD in education, learning sciences, developmental or educational psychology, or a related field
  • 8+ years of applied research experience, including product, R&D, and funder-facing work
  • Learning science expertise in literacy and/or math, home learning, and families as learning partners
  • Expertise in mixed methods, experimental and quasi-experimental design, and measure validation, with honest communication of tradeoffs
  • A record of translating evidence for non-research audiences and delivering with little oversight
  • Proficiency in R, working knowledge of SQL and/or Sigma, comfort using AI tools, and experience with public education datasets and PII

Nice to Haves

  • Family engagement or attendance research expertise
  • Evaluating AI-powered or personalized recommendation tools

Overall fit with our org culture - we look for team members who are:

  • User and Mission-Oriented: we are devoted to our mission with empathy towards the communities we serve.
  • All-in Together: we go above and beyond the job description, working together as a team.
  • Agile & Action-Oriented: we get things done, knowing that our progress is urgent to our communities.
  • Always Learning: we are always learning, with a growth mindset, to reach our full potential.
  • Boldly Courageous: we take risks in order to achieve big things.
  • Resourceful: we are creative, solution-oriented, and scrappy.

What We Offer

  • An incredible opportunity to build a mission-driven, rapidly growing startup tech nonprofit
  • 401K match
  • Flexibility to work remotely
  • Fun, smart, dynamic, motivated team focused on working together to transform family engagement to serve the families who need it most

Compensation

The base salary range for this role is $120,000 – $130,000, commensurate with experience. The actual base compensation may vary depending on factors such as relevant experience, location, market conditions, education/training, and skill level. This range does not include bonuses, other forms of compensation, or benefits.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume, a brief paragraph describing your interest, and a link to your LinkedIn profile.

About the job

We are seeking a visionary and highly experienced AI Architect to lead the design and delivery of next‑generation intelligent solutions across our enterprise. This role is central to our digital transformation strategy and will focus on architecting robust, scalable, and secure AI-driven platforms and capabilities.

As an AI Architect, you will bring deep expertise in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Generative AI, Coding Assistants, AI Assistants, and Agile software engineering practices. You will guide the full AI lifecycle from conceptualization and solution design to model development, testing, and successful deployment into production environments. The ideal candidate will have a proven architectural background, hands‑on experience with modern AI platforms, and a strong track record of delivering complex, enterprise‑grade intelligent systems. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional technology and business teams to shape the future of our AI ecosystem and accelerate innovation across the organization.

Must Have Skills:

  • Strong hands-on programming expertise in at least one modern language such as Python, C#, Java, or JavaScript, with the ability to guide engineering teams on best practices.
  • Deep proficiency with AI/ML frameworks and libraries including TensorFlow, PyTorch, and Keras, with the ability to architect scalable training and inference pipelines.
  • Advanced understanding of Generative AI architectures, including GANs, VAEs, transformer-based models, and experience applying these techniques to real-world enterprise use cases.
  • Practical experience using AI Coding Assistants
  • Hands-on expertise with Agentic AI platforms, including Microsoft Copilot Agents, AutoGPT, CrewAI, Anthropic Claude, and other autonomous workflow systems.
  • Strong command of Cloud & MLOps platforms, such as AWS SageMaker, Azure Machine Learning, Google AI Platform, including experience building automated model deployment, monitoring, and retraining pipelines.
  • Solid experience architecting solutions on major cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), including familiarity with cloud-native AI, data, and security services.
  • Proven ability to mentor, guide, and provide architectural direction to junior and mid-level AI/ML engineers across multiple projects.
  • Ability to conduct AI/ML and Generative AI code reviews, ensuring adherence to architectural standards, performance benchmarks, and responsible AI practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills, including the ability to rapidly diagnose and resolve complex issues in AI systems, ML pipelines, and application runtimes.
  • Excellent communication skills, capable of translating complex AI concepts for both technical teams and business stakeholders.
  • Experience defining enterprise AI architectures, reference models, reusable design patterns, and establishing organization-wide architectural standards.
  • Ability to define and implement AI governance frameworks, including Responsible AI guidelines, compliance controls, model guardrails, safety protocols, and risk-mitigation practices.

Responsibilities:

AI & Machine Learning Architecture

  • Architect, design, and guide the implementation of enterprise grade AI and ML solutions that solve complex business problems and power intelligent applications.
  • Lead collaboration with data scientists, ML engineers, platform engineers, and software teams to integrate AI capabilities into products, platforms, and enterprise workflows.
  • Provide hands-on technical leadership in Python, including proficiency with ML, GenAI, and LLM frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, HuggingFace, LangChain, etc.).
  • Oversee end-to-end data preparation, feature engineering, vectorization, and model development, ensuring data quality and readiness for LLMs and Generative AI workloads.
  • Continuously evaluate emerging advancements in AI, ML, LLMs, Agentic Systems, and incorporate relevant innovations into architectural roadmaps and solution designs.
  • Optimize AI and Generative AI models for performance, latency, scalability, observability, and cost efficiency, leveraging cloud-native and distributed compute environments.
  • Conduct and drive technical design reviews, code reviews, and architecture assessments to ensure high standards of quality and engineering rigor.
  • Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve complex AI system issues to maintain the reliability, accuracy, and security of production AI applications.

Generative AI, Copilots & Coding Assistants

  • Design and architect enterprise-wide capabilities leveraging AI coding assistants, copilots, and developer productivity tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Azure AI Studio assistants).
  • Lead the development of extensions, plugins, and integrations for IDEs like Visual Studio Code, IntelliJ IDEA, and Eclipse to embed AI-driven developer workflows.
  • Apply deep understanding of prompt engineering, LLM behaviour, context-window optimization, fine‑tuning, and agentic workflows to enhance solution performance.
  • Design, train, and evaluate custom generative models, exploring architectures such as GANs, VAEs, diffusion models, and transformer-based architectures.
  • Architect pipelines for data acquisition, cleaning, text chunking, retrieval augmentation (RAG), and ingestion into vector stores.
  • Integrate enterprise solutions with AI platforms and APIs such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, LangChain, and other orchestration frameworks.
  • Design and maintain the LLM data layer using technologies like Azure Cosmos DB, Azure AI Search, vector stores, and embedding indexes.
  • Develop agentic automation solutions using frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, Semantic Kernel, and AutoGen, and integrate them with enterprise systems.
  • Apply strong DevOps practices using CI/CD pipelines, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and modern testing frameworks to maintain robust and automated AI development workflows.
  • Contribute to or lead copilot initiatives across domains such as application development, customer support, operations, and productivity automation.

Prompt Engineering

  • Design, test, and refine high‑quality prompts, prompt templates, and generative AI interaction models tailored to organizational use cases.
  • Work closely with product, content, and data teams to align prompt behaviour with business outcomes, brand voice, and user experience requirements.
  • Continuously improve prompt structures to enhance accuracy, relevance, safety, and contextual understanding within AI/LLM systems.
  • Experiment with novel prompting strategies—chain-of-thought, retrieval-augmented prompts, tool-augmented prompts, system message optimization—to improve AI performance.
  • Build and maintain an enterprise prompt library, ensuring versioning, governance, reuse, and integration into automated workflows and applications.
  • Participate in fine-tuning and reinforcement learning processes by designing ground‑truth prompts, evaluation prompts, and tuning datasets.
  • Diagnose and refine prompts that yield suboptimal or incorrect results, ensuring predictable and aligned LLM behaviour across use cases.

Manoj Goud

jobs.description:
Fidus is a global high-tech design firm headquartered in Ottawa, with additional design centres in Kitchener-Waterloo and San Jose. We specialize in leading-edge electronic product development, with hardware, embedded software, FPGA/ASIC, and signal integrity teams working together to design and deliver next-generation products for clients in emerging technology markets.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Solutions Architect, DSP/Algorithms that will have a critical role in understanding technical project requirements, for existing and potential clients, to assess whether the opportunity will be a good fit. Once an opportunity fit is assessed, the Solutions Architect will be responsible for developing a solution path, preparing an estimate for the work, and highlighting the risks and mitigation strategies.

Make an Impact with US:

At Fidus, you’ll work on high-speed, high-complexity electronic systems, often using emerging technologies before they reach the broader market. You’ll collaborate across FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical/thermal design as part of cross-functional teams delivering real products for our clients.

In practice, that means contributing to projects across Communications, Aerospace & Defence, Life Sciences & Medical Devices, Space & Satellite, Industrial Automation, Automotive, and Semiconductor engagements. You won’t be limited to a single product or industry—your work will follow the technology, not just one roadmap.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Work directly with potential and existing clients to understand their needs, then develop their requirements;
  • Architect a solution that meets the Client’s needs;
  • Develop a plan, identify risks and mitigation strategies, and estimate the work required, to deliver a client solution;
  • Write the technical content for proposals;
  • Understand and present Fidus’ resource skill capabilities and work approach;
  • Discuss, promote, defend, and, if necessary, refine, the work approach and estimate;
  • Evaluate and understand solutions, to partition programs into logical segments;
  • Undertake project work as required;
  • Assist in identifying and developing new Fidus products;
  • Assist in identifying new areas of investment and research & development.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in either Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or the equivalent;
  • Ideally at least seven (7) years of design background in a Signal Processing or Algorithms Designer role;
  • System Level design experience and interest, including identifying architectural approaches and tradeoffs;
  • An expert level of knowledge in MATLAB/Simulink based system modeling;
  • Experience designing and analyzing digital filters and multirate signal chains, including FIR/IIR synthesis, decimation and interpolation, DUC/DDC, and sample rate conversion;
  • Fluency in fixed-point implementation tradeoffs, including quantization, bit growth, and the resulting precision and resource impacts;
  • Experience mapping algorithms onto FPGA fabric, DSP slices, adaptive SoC, or GPU targets against throughput, latency, and resource targets;
  • In-lab experience verifying signal processing performance;
  • Knowledge of FPGA’s;
  • Exposure to communications, radar, or imaging algorithm domains — synchronization, equalization, error correction, or beamforming — is an asset;
  • Control systems experience is an asset;
  • Ability to undertake designs with ITAR restrictions or Classified information;
  • Concise communication and writing skills;
  • Excellent listening, understanding, and extrapolation skills;
  • Professional and personable;
  • Enjoys travel, which is anticipated to be up to 6 weeks per year, typically within North America;
  • Proven experience with giving presentations to small-to-medium sized groups.

Location and travel: Position is based in the United States. Travel will be required typically within North America for up to 6 weeks per year.

This position may require access to export-controlled information. Candidates must be a U.S. person as defined under 22 CFR 120.62, or be eligible for an export license. Candidates will be required to complete background checks.

Our competitive compensation package also includes a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k) plan contributions, annual profit-sharing bonus, along with other supplementary benefits

We also recognize that candidates show interest throughout different career stages and welcome all applications. When there is a great fit, the level of the role may be shifted as applicable.

Since 2001, Fidus has completed over 4,000 projects for more than 400 customers across industries including Telecom/Datacom, Aerospace & Defence, Consumer, Semiconductors, Industrial/Automotive Controls, and Medical. As a Premier Adaptive Computing Partner for AMD North America, we combine deep technical expertise with industry-leading tools to solve complex design challenges.

Fidus designs high-speed, high-complexity electronic systems using emerging technologies, often well before they reach the broader market. Our teams work across FPGA/DSP, hardware, embedded software, verification, SI/PI, PCB layout, and mechanical/thermal design to deliver real products for our customers.

At Fidus, collaboration is at the core of how we work. We value openness, trust, and shared ownership, and we create an environment where people are encouraged to contribute ideas, learn from one another, and have a meaningful impact through the work they do.

If all of this excites you, has your attention, and you can’t wait to join our amazing team and work environment, then we want to hear from you!

Thank you for your interest in Fidus. We welcome and encourage diverse candidates to apply. Emerging Risk & Regulatory Strategy

  • Monitor, analyze, and interpret evolving regulatory requirements and industry trends across U.S. and international jurisdictions.

    • AI and automated decision-making in hiring and other employment-related processes
    • Restrictive covenants and worker classification
    • Wage and hour regulations
    • Employee data privacy, accessibility, and recording keeping obligations
    • FCRA and background check compliance
    • Translate complex regulatory requirements into practical policies, controls, and operational guidance

Client Compliance & Risk Mitigation

  • Partner with Legal, Client Services, and business stakeholders to review and assess client-driven compliance requirements, including background check standards, contract language review, and contractual obligations.
  • Review client contracts, RFPs, and regulatory flow-down requirements to identify People-related compliance obligations and operational impacts.
  • Assess client requirements against applicable federal, state, and local employment laws and advise on compliant implementation strategies.
  • Support audits, client inquiries, and compliance attestations by maintaining documentation, controls, and evidence of compliance.
  • Assess complex or high-risk compliance matters and propose practical solutions to mitigate legal, operational, and contractual risk
  • Analyze root causes of compliance issues and implement sustainable, scalable processes for remediation

  • Contribute to the design of People compliance frameworks, including policies, standards, and internal controls
  • Evaluate existing People processes (e.g., hiring, onboarding, transfers, terminations, and other data management processes) to identify compliance risks and control gaps
  • Promote standardization, documentation, and control design aligned to audit requirements

  • Coordinate assigned cross-functional compliance initiatives under the general direction of People Operations Compliance leadership by completing tasks such as:
    • Support the development and implementation of updates to policies and processes across applicable jurisdictions
    • Coordinate enhancements to existing compliance programs and policies.
    • Conduct assigned risk assessments across People processes and geographies
    • Track deliverables, document findings, and escalate issues that require leadership review
  • Partner with the People Team, TA, Legal, and business leaders to ensure consistent interpretation and application of compliance standards
  • Contribute to the creation and maintenance of global People policies and procedures to ensure clarity, consistency, and compliance with legal requirements.
  • Promotes consistent implementation of People Team policies across all business units and locations, identifying discrepancies and resolving gaps as appropriate.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree required or equivalent experience. Focus in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field highly preferred.
  • 5-7 years of progressive experience in People compliance, employment law, or related governance/risk roles
  • PHR/SPHR, SHRM-CP/SHRM-SCP certifications are highly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience leading complex compliance initiatives, regulatory implementations, or audit engagement support.
  • Demonstrated experience of laws across all 50 US states; working knowledge of Canada, Mexico, and Australia with exposure to global compliance strongly preferred.
  • Experience working with HRIS and Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS); UKG Pro and iCims preferred.
  • Project management skills with ability to manage stakeholders and work cross-functionally through influence.
  • Highly effective communication, collaboration, facilitation, and presentation skills, with the ability to engage and influence stakeholders at all levels.
  • Presents information and ideas in a thoughtful and compelling manner; is clear and concise in verbal and written communications.

Position Objective:

The Referral Coordinator facilitates the timely and accurate coordination of patient referrals, supporting continuity of care and a positive patient experience. Depending on the assigned location and business needs, the incumbent may manage outbound referrals for multiple VIPcare primary care clinics within a designated geographic area or coordinate inbound referrals received by a specialty practice.

The position is responsible for coordinating appointments, communicating with patients and healthcare providers, verifying referral requirements, and ensuring necessary medical records and documentation are exchanged and maintained. The Referral Coordinator works proactively to identify and resolve barriers to scheduling and referral completion, collaborating with internal and external stakeholders to support timely access to care and deliver an exceptional patient experience.

Position Location: Florida / Brevard County / Cocoa, Palm Bay, Rockledge, Titusville, Melbourne.

Must possess working knowledge of the geographic area served and comply with BHG's Remote Workers Policy, including maintaining a private and secure workspace, adhering to HIPAA and confidentiality requirements, ensuring reliable electricity and internet connectivity, and, for nonexempt positions, complying with all applicable timekeeping requirements.

Responsibilities:

  • For inbound referrals, receive and review referral requests from referring providers, obtain required information, and coordinate patient scheduling within the assigned specialty practice.

  • Follow established documentation, privacy, and regulatory requirements, including HIPAA, when handling patient information and coordinating referrals.
  • Identify recurring referral challenges and recommend opportunities to improve workflows, communication, and the patient experience.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

  • 3+ years of administrative, scheduling, customer service, or related experience.

  • Proficiency in Google Workspace (Drive, Docs, Sheets), including the ability to maintain spreadsheets, navigate operational reports, and track referral activity.
  • Strong attention to detail, follow-through, and accountability for completing assigned tasks accurately and efficiently.

  • Appreciation of cultural diversity and sensitivity toward the patient populations served.

As a Site Reliability Engineer, you’ll join the global Platform SRE team responsible for building, operating, and scaling Kong’s multi-region SaaS platform that powers the world’s API connectivity.

You’ll design, automate, and run production systems serving thousands of customers across AWS, GCP, and Azure. You’ll work on everything from multi-region Kubernetes clusters to service mesh and gateway architectures, ensuring the reliability, scalability, and security of Kong’s SaaS offerings.

This is a hands-on role ideal for engineers who thrive on running production SaaS systems at scale, automating operations, and continuously improving performance, resilience, and deployment pipelines.

What You’ll Do:

  • Operate and scale Kong’s global SaaS platform (Konnect), ensuring reliability, availability, and performance across regions and clouds.

  • Build, automate, and maintain Kubernetes-based infrastructure and deployment workflows using Terraform/Terragrunt, Helm, and ArgoCD.

  • Design, maintain, and optimize multi-region data and caching layers — including PostgreSQL, Redis, ClickHouse, and Druid — for high availability and low latency.

  • Operate and improve Kong Gateway and Kong Mesh environments supporting hybrid and distributed architectures.

  • Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines and GitOps workflows to automate service delivery and ensure consistent infrastructure changes.

  • Enhance observability and incident response readiness through systems like Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, and Thanos, defining and tracking SLOs.

  • Collaborate closely with development and security teams to ensure smooth operation of SaaS services in compliance with reliability, security, and regulatory standards.

  • BS in Computer Science or equivalent practical experience.

Overview

Our client is a growing U.S.-based healthcare education company that trains future MRI technologists through online learning, simulation, and hands-on clinical training. Their students need strong clinical placements to graduate, and their healthcare partners need reliable talent pipelines — this role is the connective tissue between the two.

Your Role

This role sits at the intersection of healthcare relationship management, account management, and inside sales. You'll support existing hospital and imaging-center partners, reactivate relationships that have gone quiet, help sites resolve student and placement issues, and open new opportunities for partners to host students or send their own employees through the program.

It's phone-first work: expect a mix of warm partner check-ins, the occasional difficult service-recovery call, outbound prospecting, and the detailed follow-through it takes to move an affiliation agreement or student placement to completion. Success looks like a portfolio where nothing falls through the cracks, dormant sites come back online, and new placement capacity keeps opening up.

You’ll:

  • Manage a portfolio of relationships with hospitals, imaging centers, and healthcare organizations, from site-level managers up to divisional and senior leaders

  • Run a consistent outreach cadence of calls, meetings, and personalized emails based on each partner's priority and activity level

  • Lead partner check-ins that turn into decisions, making sure every commitment has a clear next step

  • Support partners through student placements, upcoming cohorts, program questions, and relationship issues, including sensitive situations that need internal coordination

  • Reactivate affiliated or previously engaged sites that aren't currently hosting students or sending employees into the program

  • Develop new clinical-site relationships through outbound calls, referrals, and persistent multi-contact follow-up, and spot opportunities to expand existing partnerships into new locations, cohorts, or sponsored employees

  • Keep contacts, notes, activities, and relationship statuses accurate in the internal platform, and give leadership a clean weekly view of partner health, pipeline movement, and risk

You Bring:

  • We're looking for someone who already works close to this kind of relationship-building, in one of two ways. You might currently work in healthcare staffing, placing candidates into healthcare roles or bringing hospitals and health systems on board as clients. Or you've worked at the intersection of healthcare and education, managing clinical sites, student placements, workforce programs, or similar partnerships.

    • 2+ years owning relationships with hospitals, clinics, imaging centers, or other healthcare sites; experience in an education, training, or workforce-development setting is a strong plus

    • Experience managing 30 or more active organizational relationships at once, with a clear system for prioritizing them and following through

    • Direct outbound experience: cold calling, prospecting, reactivating stalled relationships, or opening new healthcare-site relationships from scratch

    • Comfort using a CRM to manage a relationship pipeline, log activity, and report on portfolio status

    • Experience working inside multi-location healthcare organizations, with relationships that run from site-level contacts up to senior leadership

    • Excellent spoken and written English with a confident, professional phone presence

    • Sound judgment in sensitive customer situations, including knowing when to escalate, plus the initiative to work independently and report progress without being asked

    Bonus Points:

    • Additional experience in B2B inside sales, account management, or partnership development outside of healthcare

    • Familiarity with clinical affiliation agreements or academic-clinical partnership structures

What’s Offered:

  • Fully remote role, full-time, working U.S. business hours

  • Compensation based on experience, location, and hiring arrangement

  • Real ownership over a portfolio that directly determines the company's training capacity

jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Senior Data Quality & Test Automation Engineer to independently validate data pipelines, schemas, calculations, datasets, and reporting outputs supporting the USMEPCOM ENLIST program’s AI integration and data analysis activities.

This position will develop SQL reconciliation tests, automated regression checks, access tests, and data freshness and performance tests. The engineer will verify that data remains accurate, complete, consistent, appropriately accessible, and traceable as it moves from source systems through transformations, warehouses, analytical models, dashboards, and reports.

The Data Quality & Test Automation Engineer will work with data engineers, AI/ML engineers, business analysts, developers, cybersecurity personnel, and Government stakeholders to identify defects, document evidence, verify corrections, and provide independent assessments of data and reporting quality.

This position is remote, with Chicago-area candidates preferred.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Data Quality & Test Automation Engineer will:

  • Independently validate data pipelines, schemas, transformation logic, calculations, datasets, and reporting outputs against documented requirements and business rules.
  • Develop SQL reconciliation tests comparing source data with intermediate datasets, warehouse tables, analytical outputs, dashboards, and reports.
  • Verify record counts, totals, aggregations, joins, mappings, calculated fields, and source-to-target completeness.
  • Test data schemas, field types, required values, relationships, referential integrity, and handling of schema changes.
  • Build automated regression checks to detect unintended changes following pipeline, schema, calculation, application, or reporting updates.
  • Validate data-quality controls for accuracy, completeness, consistency, uniqueness, validity, and timeliness.
  • Develop access tests to verify authorized access, role restrictions, data visibility, and expected behavior for unauthorized users.
  • Test data freshness, refresh schedules, processing latency, pipeline execution times, and reporting performance.
  • Validate error handling for missing, duplicate, malformed, late-arriving, or otherwise invalid data.
  • Maintain repeatable test datasets, expected results, reconciliation rules, and automated dataset checks.
  • Verify that training, validation, testing, and analytical datasets meet their documented quality and preparation requirements.
  • Maintain traceability among requirements, business rules, test cases, test data, execution results, defects, and retest evidence.
  • Integrate automated data-quality and regression checks into approved delivery pipelines and scheduled validation processes.
  • Document test procedures, execution results, supporting queries, discrepancies, and reproducible evidence.
  • Record and track defects, coordinate investigation with responsible teams, and verify corrections through retesting.
  • Assess the effect of data or calculation defects on downstream models, dashboards, reports, and mission decisions.
  • Support user acceptance testing by preparing validated datasets, reconciling expected results, and investigating reported discrepancies.
  • Provide test status, defect trends, unresolved risks, and release-readiness findings to technical teams and Government stakeholders.
  • Maintain test documentation, defect records, dataset checks, and retest results for program reviews and inspections.
  • Improve test coverage and automation based on recurring defects, production findings, and lessons learned.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

The following must-have qualifications are drawn from the supplied position requirements:

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Minimum of eight years of relevant professional experience.
  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, data analytics, or a related field, or a permitted equivalent.
  • Experience developing and executing SQL reconciliation tests.
  • Experience validating data pipelines.
  • Experience developing or maintaining automated regression tests.
  • Experience performing access testing.
  • Experience implementing or validating data-quality controls.
  • Ability to independently validate schemas, calculations, datasets, and reporting outputs.
  • Ability to develop and execute data freshness and performance tests.
  • Ability to maintain test evidence, defect records, dataset checks, and retest results.
  • CompTIA Security+ CE or another approved IAT Level II certification when applicable to assigned duties.

Preferred Qualifications

The following qualifications are preferred but are not required:

  • ISTQB test automation certification or Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP) certification.
  • Experience supporting federal or Department of Defense data, analytics, or software programs.
  • Experience testing data warehouses, ETL/ELT processes, data integrations, or analytical platforms.
  • Experience validating Power BI or comparable dashboards, semantic models, calculated measures, and self-service reports.
  • Experience with Python or another scripting language used for data testing and automation.
  • Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Familiarity with data lineage, metadata management, data governance, and controlled test environments.
  • Experience validating datasets used by AI or machine learning systems.
  • Strong analytical troubleshooting, technical documentation, and cross-team communication skills.

Job Description:

Commercial Insurance Account Manager

Please note: If this position is posted as either fully remote and/or hybrid, in accordance with company policy, individuals residing within a 50-mile radius of a branch location may be required to work onsite in a hybrid capacity as there may be occasions when on-site presence is necessary to meet specific business needs. Additionally, our remote work policy includes having a dedicated, distraction-free workspace. Remote work is not a substitute for childcare, elder care, or other personal responsibilities during working hours. To view our branch locations, please visit: ioausa.com/locations

About the Role:

We are seeking insurance professionals with 5 to 10+ years of commercial insurance experience and an active P&C license, for current and future opportunities within our Account Management career path based on experience and licensing. Multiple experience levels considered, including Account Manager, Senior Account Manager and Senior Account Executive opportunities.

The Commercial Lines Account Management team is responsible for managing and retaining client relationships, supporting new business opportunities, delivering exceptional service, and ensuring operational excellence across an assigned book of business. As team members advance through the career framework, responsibilities expand from account servicing and renewal management to technical leadership, strategic client consulting, business development, and team oversight.

Book Focus: Construction, Contractors

Account Manager

Primary Purpose

Manage an assigned book of business by providing day-to-day client service, supporting account retention efforts, coordinating policy administration activities, and ensuring accurate and timely execution of service deliverables.

Key Responsibilities

Client Service & Account Administration

  • Respond to client service requests and inquiries.
  • Process policy changes, endorsements, billing requests, and claims support.
  • Conduct coverage analysis and assist clients with policy-related questions.
  • Maintain positive client relationships through responsive service.

Renewal & Retention Management

  • Manage policy expirations and renewal timelines.
  • Gather underwriting information and prepare renewal submissions.
  • Support renewal marketing efforts and proposal development.
  • Assist with account retention initiatives.

Operational Excellence

  • Maintain agency management systems and carrier/vendor platforms.
  • Ensure account documentation is accurate and complete.
  • Monitor activity and suspense systems to ensure timely completion of tasks.
  • Follow company policies, procedures, and compliance requirements.

Financial Management

  • Assist with accounts receivable monitoring and collection efforts.
  • Resolve billing and payment issues as needed.

Professional Development

  • Maintain technical insurance knowledge and industry awareness.
  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Demonstrate company values and a commitment to client service excellence.

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of account management experience or 5+ years of insurance industry experience.
  • Active insurance license.
  • Strong knowledge of insurance products and brokerage operations.
  • Excellent customer service, communication, organizational, and analytical skills.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent.
  • CIC or equivalent designation preferred.

Senior Account Manager

Primary Purpose

Manage a complex book of business while serving as a technical resource and workflow leader for the account management team. Provide guidance on complex service matters and support operational excellence across the department.

Additional Responsibilities Beyond Account Manager

Technical Leadership

  • Serve as a subject matter expert for insurance products, coverages, and account management processes.
  • Provide guidance on complex client service, coverage, billing, and claims issues.
  • Support escalation resolution and risk management discussions.

Team Leadership & Coordination

  • Direct daily account management workflows and priorities.
  • Monitor team workloads and service standards.
  • Coordinate activities to meet quality, productivity, and service expectations.
  • Communicate proactively regarding workload, priorities, and operational challenges.

Mentorship & Development

  • Share technical expertise and best practices with team members.
  • Support training and development initiatives.
  • Promote process improvements and operational efficiencies.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of account management experience or 7+ years of insurance industry experience.
  • Active insurance license.
  • Advanced knowledge of insurance brokerage operations.
  • Demonstrated leadership, mentoring, and problem-solving skills.
  • CIC or equivalent designation preferred.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent.

Senior Account Executive

Primary Purpose

Provide strategic leadership for a complex portfolio of clients by coordinating marketing, servicing, risk management, and sales activities. Serve as a trusted advisor to clients, Producers, and account teams while driving retention, growth, and client advocacy efforts.

Additional Responsibilities Beyond Senior Account Manager

Strategic Client Leadership

  • Manage executive-level client relationships.
  • Conduct client meetings and strategic business reviews.
  • Prepare and present account summaries, risk management recommendations, and coverage strategies.
  • Serve as the primary advisor on complex insurance and risk management matters.

Business Development & Growth

  • Identify cross-sell and up-sell opportunities.
  • Support Producers in new business development and client retention efforts.
  • Negotiate and close new business opportunities and renewals.
  • Develop growth strategies within assigned accounts.

Producer Partnership

  • Act as the primary communication liaison between Producers and account teams.
  • Coordinate strategic account planning and execution.
  • Support sales and marketing initiatives.

Advanced Technical & Account Management

  • Lead complex renewal and marketing processes.
  • Conduct loss run analysis and evaluate underwriting information.
  • Negotiate coverage terms, conditions, and pricing.
  • Oversee binding, issuance, billing, delivery, and servicing activities.
  • Manage complex policy forms, endorsements, contracts, audits, certificates, evidences, and cancellations.

Team Leadership & Decision Making

  • Exercise independent judgment and discretion in client and business decisions.
  • Direct account team activities to ensure service standards and deadlines are achieved.
  • Lead problem-solving efforts for highly complex client situations.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of insurance industry experience or 10+ years of client relationship, sales, or marketing experience.
  • Active insurance license.
  • CIC or equivalent professional designation required.
  • Strong strategic consulting, negotiation, and relationship management skills.
  • Demonstrated success managing complex client portfolios.
  • Excellent communication, delegation, leadership, and customer advocacy skills.
  • High School Diploma or equivalent.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salaries and bonus potential
  • Company-paid health insurance
  • Paid holidays, vacations, and sick time
  • 401K with employer match
  • Professional growth and career progression opportunities
  • Respectful culture and work/family life balance
  • Community service commitment
  • Supportive teammates and a rewarding work environment

What to Expect (Application Process):

  • 30-Minute Phone Screen, Online Assessments, and Interview(s)

Salary Range

The expected pay range for this position is $60,000 - 115,000 annually, depending on role, experience, relevant skills, and geographic location.

Insurance Office of America is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Working with marketing leaders, channel specialists, creative and content teams, and business stakeholders, you will connect the people, processes, and information needed to keep work moving. You will maintain a reliable view of active work, establish efficient workflows, and help teams meet commitments.

  • Administer Wrike, including request forms, project templates, workflows, custom fields, automation, permissions, dashboards, and reports.
  • Establish standards for project setup, task updates, documentation, and closeout to keep platform information accurate and consistent.

  • Planning and process improvement

What you’ll bring:

  • Preferred experience
  • Enterprise B2B marketing, professional services, or regulated industries.
  • Supporting teams across complex and differentiated business units, regions, and time zones.
  • Familiarity with HubSpot, Salesforce, ON24, or social media management platforms.
  • Relevant Wrike training or project management certification.

What success looks like:

  • Wrike provides an accurate view of marketing work, teams understand their responsibilities and deadlines, and leaders can make informed prioritization decisions. Projects move through clear processes, with fewer avoidable delays and more predictable delivery.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

The Constructive Dialogue Institute (CDI) is a non-partisan, non-profit dedicated to equipping the next generation of Americans with the skills to communicate and collaborate across lines of difference. We work with U.S. colleges and universities by providing co-curricular programming for students, professional development for faculty and staff, and strategic guidance to leadership. Our goal is to foster constructive dialogue at every level of the institution and to create the conditions for lasting organizational change. CDI was co-founded by psychologist Jonathan Haidt, the bestselling author of The Righteous Mind and The Anxious Generation.

The Role

The Associate Director of Program Implementation will report to the Senior Director of Program Implementation and work closely with the Program Managers to support the successful implementation of CDI’s offerings, tools, and resources on college campuses across the country. This position will focus on relationship management of an assigned portfolio of partner campuses, guiding each campus through the stages of implementation (planning, implementation, learning and refining, retention and renewal, and contracting). The Associate Director of Program Implementation will also be a skilled project manager, ensuring on-track execution and communications for internal and external audiences, and play a key role in data tracking and processes.

The position may require some travel, approximately 3-5 days per quarter.

What You’ll Do

Implementation and Relationship Management:

  • Serve as the relationship owner for an assigned portfolio of confirmed campus package institutions.

  • Leverage subject matter expertise to manage the implementation cycle for assigned portfolio of partners, leading each partner through a planning process that results in a clear, concrete implementation plan for embedding CDI’s suite of offerings and resources within their campus community.

  • Provide consistent stewardship and support to each partner to ensure they are able to effectively implement CDI’s programs, identify and address challenges, and promote engagement, completion, and saturation.

  • Develop, in collaboration with other teams, and distribute resources that support partners in deepening their work with constructive dialogue.

  • Track per cycle and year-over-year implementation progress for partners using internal tools, such as HubSpot and Asana, ensuring data is accurate and accessible, and able to be monitored against OKRs and growth strategies.

  • Provide timely, professional, and tailored communications to partners, in the form of emails, newsletters, and other media.

  • Lead renewal strategy and contracting for individual portfolio of partners, contributing to an annual average of 85% retention for all partner accounts.

  • As needed, lead Professional Learning Communities and other Communities of Practice for partners.

  • At the direction of the Senior Director of Program Implementation, provide implementation support, including logistical and product support, for other partners within the Growth portfolio, such as workplaces, high schools, etc.

Strategy and Growth:

  • Gather and analyze feedback, learnings, and data from partners throughout the year to provide a holistic view of assigned portfolio and recommendations for future work.

  • Develop subject matter expertise on higher education, particularly in the pathways in which CDI works, and constructive dialogue, and stay abreast of trends and developments in the field.

  • Support retention, renewal, and expansion efforts including contributing to the build and execution of renewal and partner retention strategies

  • Identify process inefficiencies and areas for optimization in partnership management, implementation procedures, and implementation resources, and contribute to the development of resources and optimizations.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

  • Coordinate implementation needs across multiple team members and departments, fostering collaboration, alignment, and shared understanding of processes, projects, and objectives.

  • Collaborate closely with Growth team members (Partnerships, Live Programs) and Product, Education, Research, and Operations teams to ensure seamless alignment of goals and effective execution of CDI programming.

  • Represent the voice of the partner and partner themes with other teams at CDI.

Requirements

About You

  • Relevant experience: 5+ years in partnership management, program implementation, or related roles across nonprofits, higher education, or EdTech; including at least 1 year working directly in or with higher education.

  • Relationship builder: Exceptionally strong at building authentic, durable relationships with partners and stakeholders.

  • Comfort with complexity: Able to navigate large, complex organizations while balancing multiple priorities.

  • Clear communicator: Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to explain complex ideas, say no with tact, and build rapport virtually.

  • Confident presenter: Skilled at developing and delivering presentations for diverse audiences.

  • Organized project manager: Proven ability to manage multiple tasks, priorities, and stakeholders simultaneously, with an eye to detail.

  • Analytical thinker: Able to extract meaningful insights from data to inform decisions.

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

  • Bonus: Experience with CRM tools (e.g., HubSpot) and project management software (e.g., Asana).

What We Offer

  • Remote Work Support — up to $500 reimbursed for home office equipment and up to $50/month reimbursed for home internet or cell phone expenses

  • Schedule: Full-time, flexible within U.S. time zones

CDI seeks an Associate Director of Program Implementation to partner with colleges and universities to embed CDI’s programs through thoughtful planning and strong implementation.

jobs.description:
Our Mission

At Palo Alto Networks®, we’re united by a shared mission—to protect our digital way of life. We thrive at the intersection of innovation and impact, solving real-world problems with cutting-edge technology and bold thinking. Here, everyone has a voice, and every idea counts. If you’re ready to do the most meaningful work of your career alongside people who are just as passionate as you are, you’re in the right place.

Who We Are

In order to be the cybersecurity partner of choice, we must trailblaze the path and shape the future of our industry. This is something our employees work at each day and is defined by our values: Disruption, Collaboration, Execution, Integrity, and Inclusion. We weave AI into the fabric of everything we do and use it to augment the impact every individual can have. If you are passionate about solving real-world problems and ideating beside the best and the brightest, we invite you to join us!

This role is remote, but distance is no barrier to impact. Our hybrid teams collaborate across geographies to solve big problems, stay close to our customers, and grow together. You will be part of a culture that values trust, accountability, and shared success where your work truly matters.

Job Summary

The Technical Services Center of Excellence (CoE) builds the platforms, tooling and AI capabilities our engineers use to deliver security outcomes for customers. As Global Solutions Architect for AI Network Security, you will own the automation strategy for network security delivery. That spans traditional automation (scripting, API integrations, configuration management and workflow orchestration) as well as AI, which now plays a central role in the work. That includes assessing deployments, prescribing improvements, automating migrations, and providing conversational and agentic tools to consultants worldwide.

This is a full-stack role in the broadest sense. You are expected to be deeply fluent across the entire stack: frontend, backend, data, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, networking and cybersecurity. You also need to understand how modern AI systems work and how they fail. You design zero trust into everything you build, you understand the threat landscape for LLMs and autonomous agents, and you know the controls that address it. You reason from first principles, ship to production, and raise the engineering standard of the people around you.

The role sits where business leadership, thought leadership and technical depth meet. You turn leadership priorities into technical direction, shape how the organization thinks about AI and security, and deliver working capabilities to our field teams in Customer Success and Professional Services. We are seeking an experienced CMC regulatory professional to join our team as a Senior Regulatory Affairs Consultant, supporting post-approval vaccine products to join our team in remote capacity. You'll collaborate with senior leaders across R&D, Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, and Clinical Development, and shape CMC strategy from product development through registration and lifecycle management. Responsibilities include developing and overseeing CMC strategies for complex regulatory submissions and leading interactions with health authorities, with opportunities to deepen your expertise and influence program outcomes.


You'll join a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment focused on making a meaningful impact through strategic regulatory CMC leadership, health authority engagement, and high-quality regulatory submissions.   • Work closely with senior leaders across R&D, Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, and Clinical Development, and facilitate effective communication between internal teams, external partners, and regulatory authorities
  • Provide regular updates to senior management on project status, risks, and key milestones, and provide expert CMC regulatory guidance to support critical business decisions and product lifecycle management
  • Mentor and develop team members in Regulatory CMC practices and strategic thinking
  • Stay at the forefront of evolving CMC regulations, guidelines, and industry best practices, drive the development and implementation of innovative CMC regulatory strategies, and participate in or potentially lead relevant industry groups and regulatory authority initiatives

Candidate Profile

You'll thrive in this role if you bring:

  • Strengths in CMC regulatory strategy, complex regulatory submissions, and health authority interactions
  • Experience working in a regulated pharmaceutical environment, with a focus on CMC for late-stage and marketed products
  • The ability to collaborate across senior leadership teams, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and communicate clearly at every level
  • A patient-focused mindset, strong attention to detail, and a big-picture perspective
  • Comfort working with global regulatory submission processes, health authority expectations, and quality systems

Required Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
  • Minimum of 10+ years of experience in Regulatory Affairs, with a strong focus on CMC for late-stage and marketed products
  • Extensive knowledge of global CMC regulatory requirements, submission processes, and health authority expectations, along with a deep understanding of pharmaceutical development, manufacturing processes, and quality systems
  • Proven track record of successful regulatory submissions and positive health authority interactions
  • Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills, with excellent project management and the ability to influence and lead at senior levels

Preferred Qualifications

  • Ph.D. in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
  • Experience with both small molecules and biologics
  • Experience with a regulatory agency, such as the FDA or MHRA

  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Vacation/Holiday/Sick Time
  • Flexible Spending & Health Savings Accounts

  • 401(k) with Company match

For a complete list of benefits, please visit www.parexel.com/us-benefits.

jobs.description:
Meaningful work. Rewarding career.

Make an impact providing expert financial advice with heart. Thrivent is a different kind of financial services firm, one that puts generosity at the center of saving and investing. Here, you’ll make an impact in the lives of the people you serve, helping them build, grow and protect financial well-being through purpose-based advice, investments, insurance, banking and generosity.

At Thrivent, you’ll receive the support, stability and opportunity of a Fortune 500 leader. We offer up to 14 weeks of paid training and coaching as you obtain your state insurance licenses (life, health & variable contracts), Series 7 and 66 registrations, and complete Thrivent’s comprehensive advisor onboarding program. After onboarding, you’ll have control over the income you earn, as you’ll be paid through commissions and incentives based on your success.

As a Thrivent Financial advisor, you will:

  • Build a financial practice guiding Christians on their journeys to financial clarity, empowering lives of service and faith.
  • Provide personal, actionable and achievable advice and connect clients to Thrivent products and programs.
  • Develop and maintain genuine, long-term relationships throughout generations based on trust and understanding, with the ability to serve clients in your chosen community.
  • Make client appointments by leveraging your network and Thrivent’s reputation, delivering award-winning financial workshops and marketing your practice.
  • Have the flexibility to control your schedule, allowing for work-life balance.
  • Find a collaborative culture with colleagues who want you to be successful and are willing to help you do so.
  • Get the support of specialists from every facet of the organization—such as business development, marketing, technology, engagement, and experienced advisors—as you build your business.

Desired Characteristics

Our culture and our people are special. We’re looking for people who are – or want to become – part of the communities where clients live, work and worship. Whether you’re a seasoned financial professional or looking for a career change, you could be a successful Thrivent Financial advisor if you’re:

  • Self-disciplined, independent and driven to succeed.
  • Motivated by helping others and seeing them achieve their goals.
  • A natural coach or guide with strong interpersonal skills.
  • Passionate about living a life of generosity by serving others, not just selling products.

Successful Thrivent financial advisors have come from a variety of career backgrounds, including outside sales, business management, education, ministry, hospitality, military and more. Skills acquired in these fields transition well into the financial advisor role.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience. Military veterans are encouraged to apply.
  • Attainment of FINRA SIE, life and health licenses (licensed role only) before contracting.
  • Satisfactory background check, fingerprinting and securities registration and/or insurance licensing verification, if applicable.

Compensation and Benefits
You’ll get all the benefits of a Fortune 500 organization and more. Here, you’ll enjoy:

  • Unlimited earning potential through biweekly base commissions, bonus opportunities and incentive pay structures, recurring revenue streams, and dedicated planning fees for those who qualify.
  • Medical, dental, vision, disability and accidental death and dismemberment insurance.

  • Ongoing support, training and opportunity for professional growth as you build your business.

  • Membership programs that help you connect with your clients and engage Christians to make a real impact in your community.

Thrivent is a diversified financial services organization that, with its subsidiary and affiliate companies, serves more than 2.4 million clients, offering advice, insurance, investments, banking and generosity products and programs. For more than 100 years, Thrivent has been helping Christians build their financial futures and live more generous lives. Today, Thrivent is a not-for-profit, membership-owned Fortune 500 company with $179 billion in assets under management/advisement (as of 12/31/23). Your work will directly support tax compliance, liquidity, financial risk management, payment integrity, operational resilience, and better enterprise decisions through technology, data, AI, and process excellence. Deep hands-on and strategic experience with: Tax provision, tax accounting, direct tax compliance, indirect tax, transfer pricing, and statutory reporting technologies Treasury management systems supporting cash, liquidity, payments, bank account management, debt, investments, foreign exchange, hedging, and reconciliation Bank connectivity and payment technologies, including SWIFT, host-to-host, APIs, payment files, bank portals, and fraud-control capabilities ERP, consolidation, sub ledger, payroll, procurement, billing, market data, data platform, and regulatory integrations that support Tax and Treasury processes Data architecture, master and reference data, data lineage, reporting, analytics, and data product operating models AI, machine learning, workflow automation, document intelligence, and agentic solutions, with responsible AI and governance controls Proven success leading complex, multi-year transformations, global deployments, process standardization, platform rationalization, and operating model change across Tax and Treasury. Experience establishing reliable application support and service management for time critical close, filing, payment, cash, and market-facing processes. Experience driving adoption of AI, automation, and analytics in Tax and Treasury while maintaining appropriate human review, security, auditability, and regulatory compliance. Solid background partnering with senior business collaborators to translate Tax/Treasury strategies, risks, controls, and performance measures into technology roadmaps and investment priorities. Leadership & collaboration: Demonstrated ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing, global teams across business, technology, data, architecture, delivery, and operations skills. Excellent collaborator management and interpersonal abilities, with the ability to work with senior leaders in Tax, Treasury, Finance, Accounting, Risk, Compliance, Audit, Data, and Technology.
